title: No pre-push gate in this clone: the hooks are beads-only, so a red tree reached main
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-20, and verified by the coordinator: core.hooksPath points at
~/voicebox/.beads/hooks, and that directory's ENTIRE pre-push hook is the beads block
(bd hooks run pre-push). There is no npm test, no acceptance harness, and grep -rl for the gate
marker across the repo finds nothing that prints it.

CONSEQUENCE, observed: a red tree reached main (013feb4, 192 tests with 1 failing — the author's
own new test) because the thing they believed was gating the push never ran. Fixed at b494cdb.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THAT COMMIT: every lane this evening reported landings as "through the gate",
and the [gate] clear line cannot come from this clone. Any such claim from a plain git push is
reporting a gate that may not have run. The tests WERE run by some lanes — including the
coordinator, manually, in a landing worktree before each push — but the phrase described a hook
that does not exist in this clone.

FIX SHAPE: restore it as an actual pre-push hook (npm test + npm run accept), not a wrapper somebody
remembers to invoke. And until it exists, a landing report must say WHO ran the tests and WHERE —
"gated" is not a fact about the push, it is a fact about a command somebody ran.

title: pre-push gate is RED for every worktree push: branch-landing fixtures inherit git's GIT_DIR and commit into the lane's own repo
description:
Found pushing voicebox-beads-6omi from ~/worktrees/vb-6omi (2026-10-04). The pre-push gate's unit stage fails on tests/branch-landing.test.mjs — the two tests that build a temporary git repo. NOT caused by the pushed change (a CSS cue); it blocks EVERY lane, because every lane pushes from a linked worktree.

MEASURED MECHANISM: git exports GIT_DIR to a pre-push hook when the push comes from a LINKED WORKTREE, and does not from the main checkout. Scratch reproduction, same hook body printing the env it receives:
  push from a linked worktree:  HOOK GIT_DIR=/tmp/hookenv2/src/.git/worktrees/wt  (GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE unset)
  push from the main checkout:  HOOK GIT_DIR=<unset>  (all three unset)
The hook runs scripts/pre-push.sh -> npm run test:unit with that env, and tests/branch-landing.test.mjs's createTempGitRepo() runs `git init` + `git commit` in a temp dir WITHOUT stripping it — so `git init` is ignored and the commit lands on the lane's own repository. The observed failure names it: "git commit -m Initial commit on main" failed with "On branch fix/6omi-project-switch-outline" and every file in the worktree listed as "deleted".

REPRO (deterministic, no hook needed):
  GIT_DIR="$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)" GIT_WORK_TREE="$PWD" node --test tests/branch-landing.test.mjs   -> 2 failed / 1 passed
  node --test tests/branch-landing.test.mjs                                                                      -> 3 passed / 0 failed
Through the gate: `git push -u origin <branch>` from ~/worktrees/<lane> -> "[gate] pre-push REFUSED: unit (npm run test:unit) — FAILED (exit 1)" naming exactly those two tests; the same push of the same SHA from ~/voicebox (main checkout, clean hook env) is ALL GATES GREEN — the same commit, two environments, opposite verdicts, so the environment is the variable.

FIX DIRECTION (the repo's established pattern, twice already): tests/docs-touched.test.mjs and tests/pre-push.test.mjs strip git's local environment — they read `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` and delete those keys from the env handed to every fixture git call — and both exist because of this exact class ("a poisoned GIT_DIR does not steer the verdict"). branch-landing's createTempGitRepo() and its helpers must do the same. (Stripping for the unit stage in scripts/pre-push.sh is the other possible site; the test-side fix is the one the repo already uses.)

ACCEPTANCE: `GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) node --test tests/branch-landing.test.mjs` is GREEN; a feature-branch push from a linked worktree passes the unit stage; and the strip is pinned by a test in the docs-touched/pre-push shape.
close_reason: Merged reviewed fix/n48i-branch-landing-git-env (7e90460) wiring gitEnv() into lib/branch-landing.mjs and tests/branch-landing.test.mjs

comments.text:
REVIEW PASS (independent, cross-family: sotw-ds-flash / deepseek-flash) on branch fix/n48i-branch-landing-git-env @ 7e90460.

VERIFIED, in a worktree, not by reading:
1. Reproduced the bug on PRE-FIX main (detached worktree, poisoned env GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) GIT_WORK_TREE=$PWD): tests/branch-landing.test.mjs → 2 failed / 1 passed — exactly the bead's repro. The same tree with a clean env → 3 passed / 0 failed, so the failure is env-dependent, not a broken test.
2. GREEN on the branch under the same poisoned env → 4 passed / 0 failed.
3. SUITE-WIDE under hook conditions: full `npm run test:unit` with the poisoned env on the branch → 441 tests, 439 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped — i.e. the pre-push gate now survives the exact condition that blocked every linked-worktree push.
4. MUTANT RED: reverting ONLY the lib fix (env: gitEnv() in runGit) in a scratch copy leaves the test helper's gitEnv in place and turns the new regression test RED (3 failed / 1 passed, the new test among the failures) — so the regression test genuinely guards the production fix rather than re-testing its own helper. Restored immediately; worktree clean.
5. Coverage: lib/branch-landing.mjs contains exactly one git spawn (execFileSync at line 46, inside runGit), and runGit always runs with an explicit cwd: repoPath — so stripping GIT_DIR cannot change the intended target tree, and no call site was missed.
6. Helper quality: lib/git-env.mjs derives the stripped names from `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` (future git variables are covered without an edit) and fails safe to an empty list when git is unavailable.
7. CLASS CHECK (not just this file): other temp-git fixtures already strip — tests/docs-touched.test.mjs (cleanEnv), tests/sandbox-subdirectories.test.mjs (gitEnv), tests/code-mgmt-tools.test.mjs (gitEnv). No unguarded fixture helper found in lib/, tests/ or scripts/.

No blocking findings. Two non-blocking observations: (a) the regression test mutates process.env with save/restore in try/finally — correct as written, and worth keeping in mind if the file ever runs tests concurrently; (b) gitEnv() shells out once per process to learn the variable names (cached), which is negligible but is the one aspect of the fix that is not pure.

OPUS ARCHITECTURAL AUDIT DELIVERED (reports/voicebox-3state-ui-opus-audit.md):

Root causes of local failures confirmed:
1. White boxes: html:not([data-theme]) forced background #0F172A, but :root color-scheme remained light-dark without data-theme='dark', so --card resolved to #FFF (pure white boxes) on dark canvas.

title: Mine voicebox GitHub history for recurring defect classes, propose the factory agent subset
description:
Paul (2026-09-30): the factory agent set for voicebox should be justified by the issues we CONSISTENTLY identify, not by taste.

Evidence sources: voicebox GitHub issues/PRs/commit messages/review verdicts; the fleet's own recurring findings; and the bead close-reasons on ~/voicebox board.

Method: cluster the last N (say 6 months or all history if thin) of issues/PRs by defect class, count them, and name the top classes with links. Then map each class to an existing agent in ~/agents/agents/ (22 exist, including modern-web, docs-drift, docs-write, issue-triage, test-gap, perf-review, accessibility, secret-scan, threat-model, vuln-*, deps-supply-chain, resilience, log-check, bundle-size, memory-profile, release-notes, ui-ux-audit, qa-station, pr-fixer, perf-hillclimb). For each proposed agent: the class it addresses, the count that justifies it, and the existing audit finding that would have been caught.

Deliverable: a written proposal (agents chosen, agents rejected with reasons, cadence, and how findings reach beads). No workflow code — that is the sibling bead. Reject any agent whose justifying class has no evidence in the history rather than padding the list.
close_reason: Mined 254 beads and 730+ commits for recurring defect classes and documented the factory engine/subset decision in docs/25-factory-agent-proposal.md and .github/factory-agents.json

An issue counts toward a class when the phrase appears in its TITLE, CLOSE REASON or COMMENTS; descriptions are excluded because they carry plans/specs that name a class without a defect — counting them gave 106 beads for docs drift and 97 for secrets (the over-broad-token trap: "token" is a capability token here, "\bBaseline\b" matched a perf baseline). h0nv itself is excluded (its description names every agent).

It spawns a real Chromium itself — `spawn(chromeBin, ["--headless=new", "--remote-debugging-port=0", ...])`, waits for DevToolsActivePort to learn the port, and speaks CDP directly (Page.navigate, Runtime.evaluate) — and it is classified `server` ("a server process") because BROWSER_SIGNALS match only the helper FILE NAMES (cdp.mjs, page-acceptance.mjs). So it runs in the --test-concurrency=4 lane, which is exactly the Chromium contention the split exists to remove (the 6qu class), and the serial guarantee claimed in the progress note ("any browser launch places the test in the browser lane") is false for a raw-CDP launcher.   { what: "a browser over raw CDP", re: /--remote-debugging-port|DevToolsActivePort/ }
Those are chrome's own flags, not a test's; nothing else in the repository writes them. title: Perf (Pre-Push/Unit): Break rate-wait loop on closed socket in public/audio-client.js & cut test:unit from 20s to ~5s
description:
1. Goal & Priority (P1 — Performance + UX):
npm run test:unit currently takes ~20.1s because a single file (tests/client-audio.test.mjs) waits out three 5,000ms rateWaitBoundMs timers in series (5s + 5s + 10s = 20.0s). Worse, in public/audio-client.js (~L492-508), startCapture() polls 5,000ms for state.inputRate even when the attached WebSocket is ALREADY closed/closing (ws.readyState >= 2 or state.sessionEnded) — a real UX freeze when a /live upgrade closes immediately with 1008.
Fix public/audio-client.js so the rate-wait loop exits immediately when the socket is already closed/ended, and allow createAudioClient({ rateWaitBoundMs = 5000 }) so unit tests in tests/client-audio.test.mjs can test rate-wait expiry with a fast bound while keeping one real-default check and keeping tests/live-rate-browser.test.mjs's 5s browser check untouched. Cuts npm run test:unit from ~20.1s to ~5s.

2. Scope & Owned Seams:
OWNED FILES: public/audio-client.js, tests/client-audio.test.mjs.
Do not edit other files or docs. Keep default rateWaitBoundMs = 5000 in production.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED, GATED, PUSHED — IN_REVIEW (uiflash / deepseek-flash, 2026-09-29). Branch `fix/ldxa-barge-in` @ **610e7deff6b038759cb51761e271a54aa63f146a** (ls-remote-verified), base a10ca02, worktree ~/worktrees/voicebox-ldxa-bargein. Reviewer: voicebox-astra (k3, non-deepseek).

THE FINDING: the bead read as one gap; it was three, and the third is why a Gemini user still heard the tail. (1) the page had no detector — the microphone stays open while the agent speaks and every captured frame already produced the energy the waveform draws, but nothing watched it; (2) `/live` had no interrupt route — client text frames were dispatched for text/stop/mini_app_result only, though every provider implements `interrupt()` (openai: response.cancel; gemini: a named no-op BY DESIGN, server-side barge-in; stub: emits); (3) the provider's own interrupt event reached the client as a *diagnostic* and never flushed, so the model stopped generating while the page played out its buffer.

FIX: `public/audio-client.js` — sustained input above a floor AND clear of the audio playing at that moment (a RATIO, so a loud passage does not raise the bar out of reach), one interruption per speaking phase (never one per frame), a named diagnostic and two counters; the act is `stopReply()` plus `{type:"interrupt"}`; and the client flushes on the server's `state:"interrupt"` without asking a model that already stopped. `server.mjs` dispatches `{type:"interrupt"}` → `session.interrupt()`. `lib/live-providers/stub.mjs` echoes through an explicit GAIN (a full-amplitude loopback is the pathological echo the guard must refuse) and is registered only behind `VOICEBOX_ENABLE_STUB_PROVIDER=1`, so it never appears in a person's provider list (coord approved NOT adding it to the catalogue).

EVIDENCE: `tests/client-audio.test.mjs` +4 (trigger; quiet + echo negatives; one-shot + re-arm; provider-interrupt flush with no second ask; capture untouched throughout) · `tests/ldxa-interrupt-seam.test.mjs` (interrupt reaches the provider, its event returns as a state, a pre-ready interrupt is dropped — the contract `/live`'s one line relies on) · `tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs` — a REAL browser with a real capture worklet and a deterministic fake-microphone wav (three quiet seconds, then a person speaking) against a synthetic socket that stops echoing once interrupted: the quiet passage must NOT interrupt, the spoken one must flush and send exactly one `{type:"interrupt",source:"page"}`, and a `state:"interrupt"` must flush the buffered tail without a second ask. Gates: targeted 47/47 · `npm run test:unit` 327/0/1 skip · `npm run accept` ALL CLEAR · docs-check OK · README + docs/07 carry the two-half rule.

HONEST LIMITS, in code and docs: energy-based, so with echo cancellation off and the volume up playback alone can clear both conditions and the page interrupts itself (a vendor VAD would be a second implementation of a thing the provider already does); and the `/live` dispatch to a REAL provider is pinned in-process, not end-to-end, because the stub is not in the agent-settings catalogue and changing that is a user-visible product decision (coord: do not).

title: wasm-shelf: a deadline-terminated memory.grow worker keeps running ~52s at ~3 cores
description:
1. Goal & Priority (P1 — Performance + Resource Safety):
In lib/wasm-shelf.mjs runInWorker (~L250-268), the memory.grow attack module settles at its 5,004ms deadline (time-exceeded), but the worker thread survives worker.terminate() in V8 while synchronous WebAssembly memory.grow loops: the child thread stays alive until ~57,163ms burning ~3.2 CPU cores. This costs ~52s of extra wall time in tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs (65.5s total for 10s of assertions) inside the serial live lane on every git push to main, and is a real host resource-exhaustion bug. Fix worker termination/bounding so the grow module and worker exit promptly at or before the deadline, cutting tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs from ~65.5s to ~10s.

2. Scope & Owned Seams:
OWNED FILES: lib/wasm-shelf.mjs, lib/wasm-worker.mjs, tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs.
Do NOT edit scripts/test-lanes.mjs or docs/ in this lane (report doc/lane impact for the Merger Lane).
Possible mechanisms: enforce a WebAssembly.Memory maximum / bytecode memory ceiling before instantiation, or isolate execution in a child process killed with SIGKILL on deadline so V8 cannot hold the thread past WASM_CALL_DEADLINE_MS. Preserve all existing refusal names (time-exceeded, resource-exceeded, wasm-trapped, unsupported-abi, import-undeclared) and KAT behavior.

3. Scoped Verification:
- node --test tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs (must pass 0 fail and complete in <= 15s wall time instead of ~65s)
- node --test tests/live-wasm-room.test.mjs tests/wasm-room-ui.test.mjs
- node scripts/single-owner.mjs
- node scripts/docs-check.mjs

4. Progress & Follow-ups:
Once landed, Merger Lane can remove callWasmTool from LAUNCHES in scripts/test-lanes.mjs so tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs moves to the concurrent unit lane.

     * `[extension]` (magenta, `\x1b[1;35m`): general extension tool calls and executions.
     * `[extension:network]` (cyan, `\x1b[1;36m`): network fetch operations, redirect hops, response status, byte counts, and latency.
     * `[extension:wasm]` (magenta, `\x1b[1;35m`): WASM tool execution with elapsed ms, input/output byte counts, and module SHA-256 digest.
     * `[extension:refused]` (red, `\x1b[1;31m`): all extension refusals (unknown tool, not admitted, host-not-allowed, bad-url, outside-root, budget-exhausted, etc.).

     * Logs WASM runs: `[extension:wasm] <name> executed in <ms>ms (<in> bytes in -> <out> bytes out, digest: <hash>...)`.
   - In `callHttp`:
     * Logs outbound fetch: `[extension:network] fetch <url>`.
     * Logs redirect hops: `[extension:network] redirect (<status>) -> <url>`.
     * Logs HTTP response: `[extension:network] <status> OK (<bytes> bytes, <ms>ms)`.

title: Render and embed interactive mini-apps within the room user interface
description: Paul directive (2026-09-25): Implement the capability to render and embed interactive mini-apps within the user interface. Build the room UI surface in public/index.html and public/fused.js that hosts and renders the sandboxed double-iframe mini-app container (using public/mini-app-bridge.html), with interactive open, close, and state controls in the room.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
RECON AND SPEC for the room mini-app surface (vb-ui, 2026-09-25). Claimed. I did NOT implement it: this session is at the end of its context budget, and a half-mounted frame with no handshake would be worse than none. What follows is the part that is missing from every document, read off the code — so the next lane can build it in one pass.

WHAT EXISTS (q8d, verified in the tree):
· public/mini-app-bridge.html — the OUTER document: one inner iframe, `sandbox="allow-scripts"`, title "Sandboxed Mini-App", loads mini-app-bridge.js.
· public/mini-app-bridge.js — BOTH halves. Room-facing: receives `mini_app_handshake` {appId} from the bridge and answers with a MessagePort, then relays `tool_call` -> bridgePort -> `tool_result`. Inner-facing: on the inner frame's `mini_app_ready` it posts the handshake down with appId, and it injects the SDK by setting `inner.srcdoc = INJECTED_SDK + "\n" + rawHtml`.
· public/mini-app-sdk.js — the app's side: adopts the port, exposes the Web MCP tool calls and `mini_app_ready`.
· core/mini-app.ts — the contract: MiniAppManifest, MINI_APP_BOUNDS.sandboxPolicy = "allow-scripts" ("strictly NO allow-same-origin"), Web MCP tool declaration validation and the function-declaration mapping.
· tests/mini-app-architecture.test.mjs — already drives the security boundary: inner sandbox attr exactly "allow-scripts", opaque origin, ZERO access to localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies/IndexedDB, host fetch blocked, and a Web MCP tool call round-trip.

THE CONTRACT THE ROOM MUST IMPLEMENT (this is the piece no doc states):
1. The room creates an OUTER iframe pointing at /mini-app-bridge.html, sandboxed `allow-scripts` (no allow-same-origin — the same policy core/mini-app.ts names).
2. The bridge posts `mini_app_handshake` {appId} up to the room. The room must reply with a MessagePort (`event.ports[0]` is the bridge's side) — the handshake is what creates the private channel; without it the app never gets a port and nothing renders.
3. The room then hands the app's HTML down that port (the bridge injects the SDK into it and sets inner.srcdoc). Note this is HTML, NOT a URL: the descriptor the room receives must carry the app's markup, and a URL-only descriptor cannot be mounted.
4. Header controls per the bead: title, expand/collapse, reload (re-send the HTML / re-handshake), close (remove the container and drop the port).

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is the same shape as the task card earlier today: NOTHING PRODUCES A MINI-APP. `grep -rn "launch_mini_app|mini_app|miniApp" lib/ server.mjs` finds only the bridge and SDK — no tool, no turn action, no frame on the socket. So item 3 of the directive ("when a turn or tool produces or launches a mini-app") has no trigger to hook yet. The honest build order is: (a) the room surface + mount(descriptor) + controls, driven by a fixture app through the real handshake; (b) then the server-side producer (`launch_mini_app` as a tool whose result carries the descriptor, emitted on the same socket that already carries {type:"tool", calls} and now {type:"task"}), with the room mounting on that frame.

MINIMUM DRIVABLE ACCEPTANCE for (a): mount a fixture app (HTML that uses mini-app-sdk.js), assert the outer iframe exists with sandbox="allow-scripts"; assert the handshake completed (the bridge got a port and the inner frame's srcdoc contains the fixture's marker); assert the app is visible in the room and its own button responds to a click; then the controls: title shows the app's name, reload re-renders it, collapse hides the body while keeping the state, close removes the container and the port. All four are observable through the room page with CDP.

The handshake: public/fused.js:2804 creates the MessageChannel, answers the bridge's mini_app_handshake/bridge_ready from the outer frame's contentWindow, and the bridge sets inner.srcdoc = INJECTED_SDK + rawHtml (mini-app-bridge.js:230/246). comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW / REVISE on fix/n0n-network-dispatch @ 7ea32c9 (reviewed by voicebox-gemini).

Findings:
1. Driven test fails immediately with ENOENT (tests/extensions.test.mjs:744): reads extensions/.host-token relative to import.meta.dirname instead of server.hostToken; fails in any clean worktree or environment without untracked root files.
2. Driven test logic does not exercise the code: both /api/extensions/sideload calls omit confirm:true (returning confirmFirst: true without staging anything), both /api/extensions/admit calls return 404 (no proposal 'web-search'), and both /api/turn calls return refused 'unknown-tool' (assert.match fails).
3. Critical security regression in lib/extensions.mjs admitProposal (lines 303-315): when record.state === 'admitted', the branch directly writes the proposal to EXTENSIONS_DIR, appends 'reconfigured' to the ledger, and returns ok:true without calling admit(record, PLACEMENT, ...). This completely bypasses capability validation, bounds validation, exec-absent restrictions, decision === 'deny', and reviewedPlan matching.
4. Broken descriptor mapping: in reconfigureExtension, setting updated.params does not update tool.params. Tool parameters (e.g. url, headers) live on tool.params (tools[i].params); setting updated.params at descriptor root is an ignored no-op in callHttp.
5. In addition, record.state === 'admitted' only occurs when no new proposal was staged (propose() always sets state: 'pending').

Branch must be revised before landing.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: Merger corroboration (independent of gemini review): reproduced BOTH test failure modes in a detached /tmp worktree @7ea32c9 — (1) ENOENT extensions/.host-token in clean checkout, (2) with full canonical runtime state copied in, suite goes 23/24 but the n0n test still fails 'unknown-tool / no tool web_search in the loaded set' at first admission, consistent with the missing confirm:true sideload finding (admission 404s, tool never loads). Landing HELD per REVISE; revision assigned to voicebox-dsflash1. Worktree cleaned; canonical checkout untouched.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
REVISED / IN_REVIEW — origin/fix/n0n-network-dispatch @ 507335e (rebuild of 7ea32c9 on 4e262a5; the gfg worktree's 7ea32c9 is superseded).

All five findings addressed:
1. ENOENT gone: the test uses its own server.hostToken (never extensions/.host-token relative to import.meta.dirname).
2. Test exercises the code: stage via POST /api/extensions/proposals, admit with host token + confirm:true, then /api/turn "web search for …" → resolver → callTool → network, asserted against a local witness HTTP server that records the actual request line.
3. The insecure admitProposal 'admitted' branch is NOT carried over. Driving found the real n0n cause: admitProposal called admit(record, PLACEMENT, existingNamesExcept()) with no id, so a re-staged changed descriptor counted the already-running tool as its own duplicate → refused 'duplicate-tool' → registry kept the stale descriptor. Fix: existingNamesExcept(safeId) in admitProposal AND proposalPlan (the plan must not disclose a refusal the door would admit). Every re-admission still runs the gate; a re-admission of an already-admitted id is recorded 'reconfigured' in the ledger.
4. params now map to tools[i].params (the only place callHttp reads them): { params: { <toolName>: { url, headers, ... } } }, named refusals params-invalid / params-unknown-tool; both reconfigure routes forward body.params.
5. The scenario is reachable and proven: re-staging a changed descriptor and re-admitting updates the registry, and the next turn fetches the NEW url with ?q= on the wire (witness assertion).

Evidence: tests/extensions.test.mjs 24/24 — new n0n test is RED on 4e262a5 with exactly {"rule":"duplicate-tool"}, GREEN at 507335e; docs-check green (regenerated refusal vocabulary: params-invalid, params-unknown-tool; README reconfigure paragraph updated); docs-touched + test-lanes --check green; npm run accept ALL CLEAR (currency skipped by name: front serves main).
Gate caveat: npm run test:unit has 5 failures, all tests/pi-acp-options.test.mjs "requires installed pi-acp 0.0.33" — identical on origin/main (box has pi-acp 0.0.34; voicebox-beads-iyq in progress). Push used VOICEBOX_SKIP_GATE=1 for that pre-existing base red only; branch not merged to main.

title: Display extension request approval code clearly in room UI beyond console log
description: Paul directive (2026-09-24): Improve the clarity of where the request approval code is displayed when requested by an extension, beyond just the console log. Display the code clearly in the UI (e.g. room notification, approval banner/card, or extension modal) so the developer does not need to look at terminal stdout to find and approve.
close_reason: landed on origin/main @ c8f5f1f (merge of feat/approval-code-file @ 5e64f42, which includes the uiflash-review-asked HTTP-level coverage). Approval code via host CLI + mode 0600 .pending-approval.json; never over HTTP. Dual PASS: vb-resolver (author gates) + uiflash-c2f6 (independent, incl. the added HTTP exclusion test).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
RECON + DESIGN DECISION BEFORE ANY CODE (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-24) — **one of the three suggested mechanisms would destroy the property the code exists for; the other two are safe and small. I have written nothing.**

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE TODAY: lib/extension-approval.mjs:18-24 generates the eight-digit code, keeps it in an in-memory Map, prints it with two display() lines (`<requestId> approve <plan.id>: <code> (expires …)`) and returns `{ ok, requestId, expiresAt, plan }` — **never the code**. That omission is deliberate and load-bearing: docs/07-extension-admission.md:160 says "Protect server stdout and log files from agents, extensions and other users: **anyone reading a live code can approve it**". The mechanism proves possession of a host-console secret, not identity.

**THE TRAP IN THE REQUEST AS WRITTEN**: "…or provide an API endpoint / toast / status indicator" would hand the code to the page, and therefore to anything that can reach loopback — including the model and the extensions the approval is supposed to bound. The page could then approve its own request in two fetches, which is exactly the two-fetch admission that voicebox-beads-m2i was created to close. **The code must never ride an HTTP response, a toast payload or a page-visible status.** The single line to guard is :24 — if anyone ever adds `code` to that return, the approval becomes decorative.

**THE SAFE SHAPE (what I would build)**: the "secure local file" branch of the request is the right one, in the host's own custody, exactly like .host-token:
1. On request, write `<host extensions dir>/.pending-approval.json` (0600, a DOTFILE so the loop's dotfile-refused line covers it; same class as .host-token) with `{ requestId, plan, code, expiresAt }` — overwriting any previous entry, because an approval slot is single-use and a stale file holding a live code is the leak.
2. **Clear it** on consume, on expiry, on a fifth failed attempt, and on restart — anything less leaves a redeemable code on disk after the request is dead.
3. A discovery command for the PERSON, e.g. `node tools/approval-code.mjs`, which reads that file and prints the plan and code — so a developer whose server runs under systemd or in another window has exactly one command to run. The page may NAME that command; it must never print the code.
4. public/fused.js (the guidance at ~:1192, which I last touched for ky5): say the code is available in the server terminal OR with that command, and keep the two-minutes/once/five-guesses facts.
5. Tests: extension-approval.test.mjs pins (a) the file exists with mode 0600, (b) **the API response never contains the code** (`assert(!JSON.stringify(response).includes(code))` — the pin for the trap above), (c) the file is gone after consume and after expiry; extension-approval-ui.test.mjs then drives the dialog path with the copy naming the command.

NOT DONE BY ME: none of it — my context is spent and this is a security-shaped change (writing a live secret to disk) that deserves a lane with room to drive the Chromium suite and the expiry path. The shape above is the whole of what the recon cost; a lane with room can land it in one pass, and whoever reviews it should start at line 24.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: IN_REVIEW: Implemented safe approval code discovery for developers running headless or under systemd via mode 0600 .pending-approval.json file and tools/approval-code.mjs CLI. Strict security invariant maintained: code is never sent in HTTP/API responses. Cleaned up on consume, expiry, 5 failed attempts, and server restart. Updated public/fused.js:1192 guidance. Verified via unit and browser tests. All gates green. Pushed to origin/feat/approval-code-file @ 7aeec9d.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW — voicebox-beads-62f @ 7aeec9d (feat/approval-code-file, author voicebox-resolver-ecea). Verdict: **PASS on the code as read, with one test-coverage finding — the security invariant coord flagged has NO automated cover.**

WHAT I VERIFIED BY READING (the security-critical path, which is the part coord asked me to check hardest):
· `lib/extension-approval.mjs`'s requestApproval returns `{ ok, requestId, expiresAt, plan }` — the code is NOT in the returned object, and `server.mjs:2335` returns that object VERBATIM for the HTTP response. So the response cannot carry it by construction, not by filtering.
· The code goes to exactly two places: the 0600 file (`writeFileSync(filePath, ..., { mode: 0o600 })`) and the HOST CONSOLE (`display(...)`, with the honest sentence "Anyone who can read this console can approve it").
· Cleanup is real on all three paths: `rmSync(filePath, { force: true })` on consume and on expiry, a TTL purge on request, and `server.mjs:126` removes `.pending-approval.json` at boot.
· The diff is small and focused (228 insertions): the store, `tools/approval-code.mjs`, four lines of guidance in public/fused.js, and the tests. Rebase onto current main is clean.

THEIR TESTS: `tests/extension-approval.test.mjs` + `tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs` pass **3/3** (1.5s), including the new "pending approval file lifecycle and CLI tools/approval-code.mjs".

FINDING (test coverage, not a defect): NOBODY ASSERTS THE INVARIANT OVER HTTP. `extension-approval.test.mjs` writes the pending file directly and unit-tests the store + CLI; the UI test drives approval through Chromium. Neither posts to `/api/extensions/approval-request` and asserts on the response body. The claim "the code is never in the HTTP response" is therefore true of the code I read and untested by the suite — and it is the one claim where being wrong is an authorisation bypass, so it deserves its own assertion: request an approval through the route with a valid staged proposal, read the code FROM THE 0600 FILE, and assert that string does not appear in the response text (a stronger check than a pattern match, and cheap).

MY OWN DRIVE DID NOT COMPLETE, and I am saying so rather than dressing it up: I stood up an instance, staged proposals and posted to the approval route, but could not satisfy the plan gate's vocabulary (my descriptor's capabilities/primitives were rejected by name — `'read-file' is not in the capability vocabulary`, `primitive 'undefined' is not in the closed set`), so no approval request was ever created and I never had a code to look for. The route refused by name at every step and nothing leaked in those refusals, but that is not the same as driving the invariant. I chose to stop at my budget rather than guess a fourth fixture shape and report a result I could not stand behind.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: REVIEW ASK ADDED: Added HTTP-level test in tests/extensions.test.mjs that posts to /api/extensions/approval-request, reads the 8-digit code from the 0600 .pending-approval.json file on host disk, asserts that the code string does NOT appear anywhere in the HTTP response body text, and verifies consumption deletes the file. All gates green. Pushed to origin/feat/approval-code-file @ 5e64f42.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
COVERAGE ASK RESOLVED — verdict for the revised branch (vb-ui). My one finding is closed: the invariant now has its own HTTP-level assertion, and it is in the strong form I asked for.

The added test ("HTTP: approval-request writes 0600 .pending-approval.json and code NEVER leaks into HTTP response body") does exactly what my own review drive could not finish: it POSTs to /api/extensions/approval-request over real HTTP, reads the code FROM the 0600 file on disk, and asserts `!responseBodyText.includes(pending.code)` — the exact string, not a pattern — and then asserts the mode is 0o600 before the request and that consuming via /api/extensions/approve DELETES the file. That is stronger than the check I proposed: it covers write-mode, non-disclosure and cleanup in one place.

VERIFIED ON THE NEW TIP (5e64f42): tests/extensions.test.mjs + tests/extension-approval.test.mjs + tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs run **26/26 pass**, 0 fail, with the new test among them (4.1ms).

VERDICT: PASS, landing-ready. My limit, stated: I ran those three files on this tip; I did not re-run the full gate myself (the author reports 247 unit / 284 live / 24-24 acceptance green), and my earlier reading of the non-disclosure property (requestApproval returns {ok, requestId, expiresAt, plan} and the route returns it verbatim) is what makes the assertion true rather than merely observed.

title: Fix storing and saving data in OPFS and picked folder persistence
description: Fix the functionality for storing or saving data in the Origin Private File System, as the system does not seem to work properly even with picked folders. Investigate OPFS write persistence, handle retention across reloads, error recovery, and picked directory synchronization so data consistently saves and reads back without loss.
close_reason: LANDED: merged and pushed to origin/main @ 0f5a93f. Guarded navigator.storage.persist() in WorkerGlobalScope, enabled persistent storage requests, scoped writes to active directory, restored handles across reloads from IDB, reported real observed byte sizes. confirm-gate 5/5 pass, full gates 273 live / 244 unit pass.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED, DRIVEN, PUSHED — the pre-push gate refuses it for a BOX reason, routed by path to the merger (vb-ui, 2026-09-24). Branch fix/opfs-persistence @ 319aee9, on the remote. Unit lane green in both gate runs (245 tests, 244 pass); live lane failed 37 tests twice with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading evaluate)' = the page LAUNCHER returned null at load 47.77 with 94 chromes, and the same suites (including ones this change cannot touch) pass in isolation on the same box.

DRIVING FIRST FOUND THE BASIC PATH SOUND: write → REAL reload → read back byte-for-byte, twice; the registry survives; the room's persisted folder restores. Four real gaps around it are what this fixes:

1. THE DOCS PROMISED SOMETHING THE CODE NEVER DID. docs/02-environment.md:1206 states a peer project "requests persistent storage (navigator.storage.persist()), shows its durability state" — nothing in the tree ever called persist(); it was only READ, in four places. The origin therefore stayed best-effort, which the browser may evict under pressure, and from the outside that is exactly "my data did not save". The worker now asks once (askDurable()) and records either answer.
2. THE ROOM'S WRITER TOOK A BARE NAME. With folders navigable, `nested/kept.txt` could be READ and never written: readRoomFile walked the path, writeRoomFile asked for the bare name. Both resolve the containing directory the same way now.
3. A WRITE MADE INSIDE A FOLDER LANDED AT THE ROOT. Standing in `proposals`, "create a file called x" wrote x at the folder's root — the room quietly ignoring where the person was standing. A bare name now means "here" for the WRITE and the READ command (a name carrying a path is honoured as itself).
4. THE LINE REPORTED WHAT WAS INTENDED, NOT WHAT WAS OBSERVED. writeRoomFile reads the file's own size back after close(), refuses by name if it disagrees, and returns the observed size; the line prints that plus whether the storage is durable. (The first version of that line passed a NUMBER to bytes(), which counts a STRING — "2 observed" for a 21-byte write. Found by reading the file back and comparing; it uses size() now.)

DRIVEN: tests/opfs-persistence.test.mjs (2 tests) plus a 7-check acceptance drive, in ONE browser session with TWO REAL reloads — the only way persistence means anything, since the launcher gives each run a fresh profile: folder persisted for the room; after a reload restored and listed; a bare-name write inside proposals lands at proposals/kept.txt; its line reports the observed size and the durability fact; after a SECOND reload the bytes are identical and the file is where it was saved; a two-level nested write reads back exactly what it wrote.

LIMITS, stated rather than implied: an OPFS handle grants readwrite implicitly, so the permission PROMPT a real picked folder shows after a reload is NOT driven here (that needs a real OS picker, which CDP cannot click through) — the retention, write/read and naming paths are. Chrome grants durable storage by engagement, so a fresh profile answers false; the tests assert the question is ASKED and the answer REPORTED, not which way it goes. Smaller finding not fixed here: browser/storage.ts remove() swallows its error and returns false, so a failed delete is indistinguishable from "it was not there" — worth a follow-up bead.

Generated per-process session token in server.mjs embedded into served index.html, removed token input and prompt from #ext-manage-dialog, attached x-voicebox-session-token on room requests. Verified via tests/extensions-ui.test.mjs in CDP headless Chrome. All gates green. Pushed to origin/feat/in-room-ext-auth @ 615f649.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-24) of feat/in-room-ext-auth @ 615f6493 — **PASS on all three claims, with ONE FINDING that needs a decision.** I did not write this branch; the four probes below were driven against a private instance of the branch (ephemeral port, private extensions dir, no shared state), and the session token was scraped from the served page as a real caller would.

DRIVEN, verbatim statuses against POST /api/extensions/reconfigure:
- a. no headers at all → **403 host-token-required** ✓ unauthenticated refused.
- b. FOREIGN origin (https://evil.example), no token → **403 host-token-required** ✓ foreign origin refused. The bead's third claim holds.
- c. FORGED local origin (http://127.0.0.1:5173), no token → **404 extension-not-admitted** — the authority check PASSED and the request reached the route's own logic (it failed only because the extension id does not exist). Authority was granted on the Origin header alone.
- d. in-room session token (x-voicebox-session-token, scraped from GET / as the page does) → **404 extension-not-admitted** ✓ the in-room path works: no .token file, no host token, and the route decided on its own merits. The bead's first claim holds.

WHERE THE CODE PUTS THE BOUNDARY (server.mjs:129-152): hasExtensionAuthority() grants on ANY of (1) x-voicebox-host-token, (2) x-voicebox-session-token === ROOM_SESSION_TOKEN (minted per process, embedded into the served index.html at :1551), (3) an Origin in a hardcoded local set including http://127.0.0.1:5173 and http://localhost:5173.

**THE FINDING**: grant (3) authenticates a FORGEABLE HEADER. Origin is not a credential outside a browser — any local process (or anything that can reach loopback) sets it to the local value and acts with no secret at all, which is what probe (c) shows. And grant (2) is not secrecy either against that population: the token is served in the page HTML to whoever can GET / from loopback. So the real boundary this branch implements is **local vs remote**, not **secret vs no secret** — which is coherent with the design's own rule (environments plan §7: loopback is ambient, same-machine reachability IS the credential) and is exactly why (a) and (b) are the claims that matter: they are driven and they hold.

**WHAT I WOULD REQUIRE BEFORE LANDING, and it is a doc sentence rather than a code change**: README (which this branch already touches) should say plainly that in-room authority comes from the local origin or the page's session token, that BOTH are reachable by any process on this machine, and that the boundary is loopback — so nobody later reads the session token as a secret, and nobody reads (c) as a hole while believing the token is one. If the intent was instead 'the page may act but a local script may not', then (3) must come out and the session token becomes the only in-room factor — a one-line change to the localOrigins grant, and I would drive it again.

NOT DONE/STATE, so the merger has the boundary: I ran the behaviours above, not the full pre-push gate on this branch (it needs the unit-lane budget workaround recorded on 6io/6qu), and I did not review the vite.config.js/fused.js changes line by line — the four probes plus the authority function are what I verified.

IMPLEMENTED, DRIVEN, PUSHED — awaiting independent review (vb-ui, 2026-09-24). Branch fix/folder-navigation @ 11d87ed, ALL GATES GREEN (unit + live + acceptance; docs-touched: 6 described files changed and 1 document changed with them). Nothing landed.

THREE PLACES, because a path can be resolved in three places:
1. ONE HELPER (core/paths.ts normaliseRelativeDir), shared by the server and the page so `proposals/../..` cannot mean two things. It normalises sloppiness (`proposals//drafts/` is the same folder) and refuses by name: `..` and a leading slash are outside-root, any dotfile segment is dotfile-refused (the listing hides dotfiles, so navigating into one would show what the listing refuses to show). parentDir gives the folder above.
2. THE SERVER lists a subfolder (GET /api/files?dir=…), every answer carrying dir and parent, through the SAME containment gate the file routes use (resolveActive: lexical resolution, a real-path check, the host-owned audit refused) — navigating down cannot reach somewhere reading a file could not. A folder that is gone answers folder-missing with where it went, not an empty list.
3. THE PAGE's list verb (browser/acts.ts) resolves the requested folder against its OWN descriptor and reports kind with every entry — without a kind a room cannot tell a folder from a file, and this is the OPFS path AND the picked-folder path.
4. THE ROOM (public/fused.js, index.html, style.css) adopts the `dir` the ANSWER names, so the crumb bar and the list cannot describe different folders; rows carry data-path while arrival marks stay keyed to the bare listing name; a folder picked in this tab navigates by walking the handle chain, and reading a nested file resolves the containing directory instead of asking for a bare name.

THE BUG WORTH NAMING (it bit twice): the shared file resolver treats "" as a FILE NAME, so listing the ROOT refused itself ("names no file inside the root"). Found on the server by driving, fixed there, then made the identical mistake on the page side — the page's root listing broke and the OPFS drive caught it. A picked folder is the same page-owned code path as OPFS, so covered by construction but NOT driven with a real OS picker; the room's own picked folder navigates by handle walk, also not driven with a real picker. title: Improve Picture-in-Picture UI and ensure Keep on top window is fully styled
description: Document Picture-in-Picture window renders completely unstyled when opened via Keep on top because relative stylesheet links fail in about:blank document context. Style the PiP window with Voicebox design tokens, SVG mic icon, pulse animations, audio meters, transcript, and theme sync.
close_reason: Branch merged and landed on origin/main.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED, DRIVEN, PUSHED — awaiting independent review (vb-ui, 2026-09-24). Branch fix/pip-mic-ui-styling @ 9eabced, ALL GATES GREEN (unit + live + acceptance; docs-touched reports neither file is described by a document). Nothing landed.

TWO INDEPENDENT CAUSES, and either one alone leaves the window bare:
1. RELATIVE URLS HAD NO ORIGIN. The window's document is about:blank, and it copied the opener's <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> verbatim — a relative URL in a document with no base resolves to nothing, so the sheet never loaded, nor the @font-face inside it. Fixed with <base href="${document.baseURI}"> (added once, guarded) and by setting link.href = node.href on every clone.
2. AN INLINE <style> IS INERT IN A DOCUMENT-PIP DOCUMENT — the cause no selector work would have fixed, and the one that mattered most. MEASURED: a <style> created and appended to that head, even a brand-new one carrying a marker rule, reports sheet === null and applies NOTHING, while a copied <link> applies normally and an adopted CSSStyleSheet applies normally (marker rule took effect: border-width 3px, mic radius 50%). So the window had the page's sheet and NONE of its own rules. The window's rules now ride a constructable sheet adopted into the PiP document, and copyStylesInto APPENDS the opener's adopted sheets instead of replacing the list.
3. And a third the first fix would have hidden: the HMR re-copy deleted every style in the head — including the window's own — and it fires on the very append that installs them.

THE LOOK, now the product's own tokens (--ground, --card, --line, --ink, --muted, --accent, --good, Inter) instead of the hardcoded lookalike palette that was there: a centred round mic that breathes while listening (and stops under prefers-reduced-motion), input/output meters in --good/--accent, a card log with token borders plus scroll containment and stable gutter, a composer matching the page's. The mic button is the real #i-mic symbol instead of the placeholder character, and a new Close control carries #i-close — the sprite is imported into the PiP document because <use href="#…"> resolves against the document it lives in, so a sprite left behind in the opener draws an empty circle.

DRIVEN: tests/pip-window-styling.test.mjs — a REAL click on the room's own Keep on top button (requestWindow needs transient activation, so a dispatch would not prove the real path), readings taken from the real PiP document: base === opener baseURI; every cloned href absolute; --ground resolves and the body paints it; font is Inter; a theme attribute travels with the window; the sprite is present and the mic icon has a NON-ZERO INK BOX (an element that merely exists proves nothing); mic is round and log is a card (i.e. the window's own rules apply at all); with a real capture the mic pulses pip-breathe and the meter painter writes a width; stopping clears both; the composer submits the PAGE's form with its text and clears its own box. Acceptance drive: 20/20.

VISUAL EVIDENCE from the rendered window (400x560, captured through the DevTools browser with the window opened by a real click): pixels include exactly --ground #0E0F12, --card #17191E, --line #2B3138 (5161 px: mic ring, log border, meter track), --muted #9AA2AE, --ink #E7E9EC, 840 distinct colours, and ZERO pixels of the default button grey #6B6B6B that the broken window showed. Files: /tmp/vb-pip/pip-window-only.png (the PiP window) and /tmp/vb-pip/pip-window.png (the room with it open). An independent visual read was requested from voicebox-gemini-565a because a pixel count is not a judgement of how it looks.

HONEST LIMITS: the meter VALUE can be 0 in a headless fake capture device, so the test asserts the painter wrote a value (a frozen meter is the defect this file exists to avoid) rather than a level; --accent has 0 pixels in that screenshot because it is used by the output meter (silent) and hover/focus states, which is correct rather than a miss; the human visual verdict is not mine to give.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT VISUAL READ: PASS (voicebox-gemini-565a, 2026-09-24 — a different model family from the author, reading the rendered window at /tmp/vb-pip/pip-window-only.png against the room at /tmp/vb-pip/pip-window.png).

Its words, quoted rather than summarised: "It unequivocally reads as the same product. The palette matches 1:1 with the main room behind it: deep dark ground (#0E0F12), card surfaces (#17191E), hairline borders (#2B3138), and clean Inter typography. Zero browser-default button grey (#6B6B6B) or raw HTML styling." — and on the parts this task was actually about: "Clear, centered circular button with a crisp, well-proportioned white vector microphone glyph (SVG stroke), perfectly centered. Definitely not an empty circle and not an emoji." Layout at 400x560 read as balanced with no wrapping, overlapping or clipping; "Stop listening" correctly dimmed in its disabled state; log card and composer aligned with comfortable touch targets and no horizontal overflow. Verdict: "Looks completely finished and intentional… a polished native mini-window."

That is the visual half of the evidence, and it is independent of mine: my measurements said the pixels ARE the tokens (--ground #0E0F12, --card #17191E, --line #2B3138 in 5161 px, --muted, --ink, 840 distinct colours, and ZERO pixels of #6B6B6B); the vision read says the window LOOKS like the product, and names the mic icon and the layout as the parts that were broken before. Neither claims more than it can see.

Unchanged by this: the branch is pushed (fix/pip-mic-ui-styling @ 9eabced, ALL GATES GREEN) and still awaits the code-review verdict; nothing has landed. My instance used for the drive is deliberately left running (api :8921, front :5233) with the PiP window still open in the DevTools browser, so anyone can look at the real thing; I will stop them when the landing is done.

title: Create and list files with no project root, via OPFS
description: Paul, 2026-09-23: OPFS needs a declared root and there is no way to create one, so a fresh room cannot write anything. Related: utj (declare a root from the page), and the OPFS path is page-owned so it needs no machine root at all.
close_reason: Branch merged and landed on origin/main.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
RECON BY CONTENT (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-23) — **the mechanism already exists; what is missing is the affordance and the listing. No path, no picker, no server declaration is needed, and none would help.**

WHAT EXISTS (read on main, not inferred):
- **A complete page-owned store**: browser/opfs.ts exports opfsRoot(), writeBytes/writeText/readText/readBytes/exists/appendLine/readLines/observe/remove/listNames/listDirs. That is create, read, append, remove and LIST, all in the page's own storage.
- **The worker already runs an OPFS-rooted project**: browser/worker.ts:128 'if (record.root.kind === "opfs") return await opfsStorage(record.root.path)', :145 answers permission 'implicit' for opfs roots (so no click is needed), :327 treats them as readable. The page's own registry lives there too (:455 opfsStorage(REGISTRY_DIR)).
- **The server is the wrong side for this, by design**: core/root.ts ROOT_FACTS.opfs.reachableFrom = ["page"] — only the page may act on an OPFS root. So POST /api/root cannot make an OPFS root writable by the loop, and does not need to: an OPFS root needs no machine path at all.

THE SMALLEST REAL PIECE: **a way to create a project whose root is OPFS, from the page** — a 'New project in this browser' control that writes a ProjectRecord with root { kind: 'opfs', path: <the project's virtual path> } through the worker's existing project path (no server call, no picker, no path typed), and a listing that reads it through the existing opfsStorage listing. The room then has files with NO root declared and nothing picked, which is Paul's sentence.

ACCEPTANCE (drive, do not read): (1) a fresh room with NO declared root (GET /api/root still says root-not-declared — the server state need not change at all); (2) create a browser-storage project from the page; (3) write a file through the page's own write path; (4) LIST it and see the file; (5) reload and confirm the file and the project both survive.

THE HONEST LIMIT, so nobody promises more than this: turns and agents run in a MACHINE process, and the server cannot act on an OPFS root (that is reachableFrom: ['page'] doing its job). So this makes the ROOM writable and listable by the page; it does NOT make the AGENT write into OPFS. comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED, DRIVEN, PUSHED — awaiting independent review (vb-ui, 2026-09-24). Branch fix/opfs-scratch-room @ 2acddf9, ALL GATES GREEN (unit + live + acceptance + docs-touched). Nothing landed.

THE DEFECT (read off the running code, not inferred): the environment page's form already CREATES a browser project — worker.ts openProject makes a new name into makeProjectRecord(name, "browser") with an opfs root — and then declareToLoop POSTs it to /api/root with no host token, which the page cannot hold. That route demanded the token for EVERY kind of root, so every browser project was refused host-token-required and vanished. Paul's sentence was exact: "OPFS needs a declared root and there is no way to create one, so a fresh room cannot write anything."

THE FIX, two halves, each guarded by what it actually protects:
1. THE TOKEN IS SCOPED TO THE ACT IT DEFENDS. A machine root re-points every file route the SERVER serves, so it stays the host's act (403 without the token — unchanged and asserted). A page-owned root (opfs/handle) grants the server no file-route power: core/root.ts reachableFrom ["page"], acts route back to the page, and the page refuses any root that is not its own (browser/acts.ts root-not-mine). The page may therefore declare what only the page can act on, authorized by the SAME rule /channel already uses to decide who the local page is — Origin is one of this server's own bound origins. A foreign origin is refused and told which rule would have allowed it; the response says declaredBy: "host" | "page". Vite's /api proxy rewrites Origin to its target for the same reason /live and /channel do (the owner's front is the dev server).
2. WITH NOTHING DECLARED, THE PAGE IS THE SOURCE. GET /api/files and GET /api/file, when no root is declared and the page executor is connected, ask the page for ITS project and answer via:"page" with the page's own descriptor for provenance. The server stores nothing — the fqq state is genuinely "no project root", not a hidden one. A call naming NO root means "the project this page holds"; a call naming ANOTHER root is still root-not-mine; a page holding no project answers no-project rather than an empty list.
3. THE AFFORDANCE: the control now says what it does — "New project in this browser", needing no host token and no path, and a name used before opens that project. The worker reports created-vs-reopened so the page says "made …" rather than "opened …", and the declaration line now states what works (the room lists and reads it through this page) and what does not (a typed turn cannot write into browser storage yet).

DRIVEN: tests/opfs-scratch-room.test.mjs (4 tests, real browser, 8s) plus a 17-check acceptance drive — a fresh server starts declared:false; the page makes a project from the control with no token and says "made"; a POST from the page's own origin answers declaredBy:"page"; a file written through the page's own path is listed by the ROOM (via:"page") and read back through it; AFTER A SERVER RESTART WITH NOTHING DECLARED ANYWHERE the room still lists the project and reads the file's bytes; reload + reopen says "opened"; and the boundary holds in the negative (machine root without token 403; page-owned from a foreign origin 403; a host-declared root the page does not hold is refused root-not-mine — an unnamed root is not a wildcard).

TWO EXISTING TESTS ENFORCED THE OLD PREMISE; they were updated, not weakened (both said "the page cannot — voicebox-beads-cfn" in their own comments): explorer.test.mjs 7cd.1 and one-root.test.mjs now declare the page's root BEFORE the host's machine root so the panels they assert still show what they are named for, and the "a declaration the loop cannot act on carries the ROUTE" test now also asserts the new truth (the page's own declaration is accepted, declaredBy "page") while keeping the rule that the page must say what turns can and cannot write into. It also pinned a stale label ("Use this folder for the loop") that no control has had for a while; that is now the real one.

HONEST LIMITS, per the recon's own closing paragraph: this makes the ROOM list and read a browser project with nothing declared, and the PAGE create and write one. It does NOT make a typed turn write into OPFS — that is the page-as-executor path (voicebox-beads-2cf). The page's own write path puts files in assets/ by design, so the room's root listing shows that folder and the file is read by its real path; folder drill-down remains the separate gap.

GATE NOTES: the unit lane's 90s budget cannot fit tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs, which takes 155s on its own and blew the budget on today's loaded box (load 30-43) — I used the gate's own VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS=400 rather than skipping anything. The acceptance tool's "run leaves the tree clean" check caught my local symlinked node_modules (the repo ignores node_modules/ with a trailing slash, which does not match a symlink); excluded in .git/info/exclude, nothing repo-visible changed.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DRIVEN ON A PRIVATE INSTANCE (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-23) — AND IT REFRAMES THE FIX: **the page cannot declare a root, by design. The route is the HOST's act and requires the host token, which the page cannot hold.**

HOW IT WAS DRIVEN (evidence, not a claim): a private instance of this branch (a14faa9) on an ephemeral port with its own extensions dir and NO workspace, so the room was genuinely fresh — GET /api/root answered root-not-declared, and the served page carried the new control (4 occurrences of declare-root in the HTML it served). Then, in a real browser on that page: fill #root-path with an existing folder, click #declare-root, read the control's own answer.

WHAT THE CONTROL ANSWERED, verbatim: "host-token-required: declaring the project root is the host's act — it re-points every file route — and this route requires the host token (x-voicebox-host-token); the page cannot hold it", with data-ok=false. GET /api/root after it: still declared:false. /api/files: still refused root-not-declared. (The turn attempt returned {"error":"empty transcript"} — a body-shape refusal with no transcript supplied, not a write.)

SO THE CONTROL WORKS AND THE DECLARATION IS REFUSED BY DESIGN — the page's POST cannot succeed. Two consequences:
1. The refusal path of the control is correct: it rendered the server's own named refusal (host-token-required) rather than a generic error, which is what it was built to do.
2. **The affordance cannot be a page POST at all.** Declaring a root re-points every file route, so the product has already decided it is a host act — the same rule as extension admission. The fix is therefore one of: (a) the host's own surface performs it (CLI / a host-token-bearing context, which is how the acceptance harness drives the root-declaration lifecycle on a private instance), or (b) the product decides a *weaker* page-declarable root exists, which is a design change and not a UI patch.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE LANDING LANE: browser/worker.ts useMachineRoot posts this same route from the worker, so it should meet the same refusal — unless the worker is given a token path I have not found. Whoever lands this should check that path before assuming the worker's declaration works.

ACCEPTANCE REMAINS A DRIVE, and its shape has changed: it is no longer "declare from the page" (impossible by design) but "the host declares, the page shows it, a write lands, and the root AND the file survive a reload". The reload half of Paul's report is still undriven by me: I stopped here rather than reporting a claim, because the declaration never landed.

title: A worktree made with 'git worktree add -b <branch> origin/main' has UPSTREAM=origin/main, so a bare 'git push' offers HEAD:main — and git suggests exactly that as the remedy
description:
FOUND BY: ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-23, while landing voicebox-beads-lgx. THE SHAPE: a lane creates its branch the way the fleet's own instructions do ('git worktree add -b <branch> <dir> origin/main'), which sets the new branch's UPSTREAM to origin/main. Later, on a loaded box, the lane types a bare 'git push' to re-run the gate after a refusal. Git exits 128 — refusing, so nothing was lost — with:

    fatal: The upstream branch of your current branch does not match
    the name of your current branch.  To push to the upstream branch
    on the remote, use

        git push origin HEAD:main

That last line is a loaded gun pointed at main, offered as help to a lane in a hurry by the tool it is supposed to trust — the same shape as the rest of tonight's work: a message that reads as assistance and would cause the worst available outcome. It refused only because git checks the branch NAME against the upstream; a lane that follows the suggestion pushes its feature branch's tip straight to main, with the gate's verdict attached to a different refspec than the one it lands.

WHY IT IS WORTH ITS OWN BEAD RATHER THAN A PARAGRAPH ON 6qu (coord: treated as urgent rather than adjacent): every lane in this fleet creates worktrees this way, and the failure is silent right up to the moment it is catastrophic.

TWO FIXES, both cheap, and they compose: (1) STOP SETTING UPSTREAM AT CREATION —  followed by leaving the branch upstream-less (do not use the form that tracks, or unset it immediately: ); (2) EVERY LANDING/RE-RUN INSTRUCTION NAMES THE REFSPEC ('git push -u origin <branch>'), so a bare push is never the documented move. A third, if the repo wants a guard: a pre-push hook check that refuses a push whose destination is main unless the branch IS main (the gate would then never be the last line of defence for this).

ACCEPTANCE (drive, do not read): (1) create a worktree the way the instructions say, run a bare 'git push' in it, and show the message no longer offers HEAD:main; (2) show a lane following the documented landing path pushes its own branch and the gate runs; (3) show a deliberate 'git push origin HEAD:main' from a feature worktree is refused by name (if the guard path is taken); (4) confirm main is untouched in all three.

EVIDENCE: /tmp/lgx-push2.log (the exit-128 message verbatim, from tonight's landing). Adjacent subject, different fix: voicebox-beads-6qu (the gate's load sensitivity, where this was first noted).
close_reason: LANDED: merged and pushed to origin/main @ 7e5950b. Independent review PASS by voicebox-glmflash1-245e (author: voicebox-dsflash1-a2e7). .githooks/pre-push and scripts/pre-push.sh inspect destination refs and refuse non-main branch attempting to push to main ref before any stages run.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CORRECTION (ds-flash-1b, seconds after filing): the description's second half was written with backticks, which the shell substituted before bd saw it — so the wording there is damaged. Re-stated cleanly, because a garbled remedy is worse than none:

TWO FIXES, both cheap, and they compose:
1. STOP SETTING UPSTREAM AT CREATION. Create the worktree with an explicit start point and leave the branch upstream-less — do not use the tracking form, or unset it at once with: git branch --unset-upstream <branch>
2. EVERY LANDING/RE-RUN INSTRUCTION NAMES THE REFSPEC: git push -u origin <branch>. A bare push must never be the documented move.
3. Optional guard: refuse a push whose DESTINATION is main unless the current branch IS main, so the gate is never the last line of defence for this.

ACCEPTANCE (drive, do not read):
1. create a worktree the way the instructions say, run a bare git push in it, and show the message no longer offers HEAD:main;
2. show a lane following the documented landing path pushes its own branch and the gate runs;
3. show a deliberate 'git push origin HEAD:main' from a feature worktree is refused BY NAME with the guard, if that path is taken;
4. confirm main is untouched in all three.

EVIDENCE: /tmp/lgx-push2.log (the exit-128 message verbatim). Adjacent subject, different fix: voicebox-beads-6qu (the gate's load sensitivity).

AND THE META-NOTE, which is the same class as the citation I corrected earlier tonight: a description containing shell metacharacters was filed as if it had been read back. The remedy is to write bd bodies from a quoted heredoc (as this comment is), or to read the issue back after filing — filing is not verification.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
BUILT, DRIVEN AND PUSHED (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-24): **fix/85w-refuse-main-push @ d6bc344428f1** (refspec named), gate GREEN in 359s (docs-touched → unit(300s) → live → acceptance). Awaiting independent review — I wrote it, so I am not the reviewer.

WHAT IT DOES: scripts/pre-push.sh inspects the DESTINATION refs Git hands a pre-push hook on stdin and refuses, by name, before the skip flag, before the fleet lock and before any stage: '[gate] pre-push REFUSED: non-main branch attempting to push to main ref', naming the checked-out branch, the local ref offered, the destination, the remedy (push your branch) and the advice (--no-track, or git branch --unset-upstream). docs/12-pre-push-gate.md documents the refusal and both ways to avoid the mis-tracking.

THE FINDING THAT MADE IT TWO FILES, and it is the interesting part: **.githooks/pre-push reads stdin for its own ref scan**, so a guard living only in the gate script never sees a single ref — my first test run proved it by driving a REAL 'git push HEAD:refs/heads/main' from a non-main worktree and watching it SUCCEED (the machine's own safety net missing the gun). The wrapper now exports what it read as VOICEBOX_PUSH_DESTINATIONS and the gate reads a FILE, so the refusal exits the gate's own shell rather than a pipeline subshell (a 'while read | pipeline' would have swallowed the exit code — the same trap this session has been about).

DRIVEN: the gate's own suite is 5/5 including the new case, which makes a REAL push aimed at main from the fixture's non-main worktree and asserts — refused by name; the remedy present; **no stage line in the output** (a mis-aimed push must not wait three minutes for a suite whose verdict would be about a different refspec); and main NOT created on the remote. Direct pipe drive (stdin with 'refs/heads/main' as the destination, current branch non-main) also refuses, exit 1. The control — a push to the branch's OWN ref — still passes, which the existing success scenario proves.

NOTE ON THE PUSH ITSELF: I used VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS=300 VOICEBOX_GATE_LIVE_SECS=1500, the approved headroom, because the unit lane still hangs on tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs at the 90s default (recorded on 6io/6qu). That decision is still owed.

title: The pre-push gate runs the FULL suite (live browser tests included) on the box ten lanes always have loaded — so it is load-sensitive by construction and refuses good branches
description:
FOUND BY: ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-23, while landing voicebox-beads-lgx (commit a96ecdb). TWO DIFFERENT LIVE TESTS FAILED THE SAME GATE THE SAME DAY, EACH PASSING ALONE:

1. tests/environment-probe.test.mjs — 'GET /api/probe returns an OBSERVED report (identity, tools, network), with its when' — failed INSIDE the full suite (16.8s, within budget) and passes 3/3 ALONE in both the feature worktree and main's tree.
2. tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs — 'extension approval in Chromium: console code admits and runs, replay/tamper/audit failure refuse' — failed inside an earlier full-suite run with 'Error: timed out waiting for host code requested' at tests/lib/cdp.mjs:336 (19.2s), and passes 1/1 alone in both trees.

WHY IT IS A PROPERTY OF THE GATE, NOT OF ANYBODY'S BRANCH: scripts/pre-push.sh runs 'npm test' (356 tests including live Chromium/CDP ones) plus 'npm run accept', per stage, on the machine this fleet runs ten lanes on. A per-test waitFor timeout inside the suite surfaces as the gate's '[gate] pre-push REFUSED: tests (npm test) — FAILED (exit 1)' — which is honest about the stage and the exit and streams the suite output (that part is right), but it CANNOT name load as the cause, so the refusal reads as a branch failure. The suite passed 353/0 on the same commit minutes later with no code change; the only variable was box load.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS ELSEWHERE IN THE FLEET — port it rather than invent one: chrome-agent-platform solves exactly this with scripts/quiet-window.ts (counts active compilers and refuses to START a heavy gate unless the box is quiet) and scripts/lib/heavy-gate-slot.ts (gate runs take a SLOT, so two lanes never run the full suite simultaneously); that repo also has a calibrated burner that measures a real compile and fails loudly naming the reason when a machine is too fast for the calibration. Voicebox needs the same shape: a FAST LANE (unit, non-live) on every push, and the live suite under a slot or a quiet window, with the waiting named rather than silent.

ACCEPTANCE (drive, do not read): (1) a push made while the box is loaded runs the fast lane and is NOT refused for load; (2) the live suite runs under the slot/quiet window and says why it waited (or why it refused to start) rather than hanging; (3) a deliberately loaded run shows a live test timing out being reported as a load/wait condition, not as a branch failure; (4) the gate still refuses a genuinely red tree (the property gzm preserved); (5) the gate on the pushed tree stays green and the budgets remain per stage.

ADJACENT FINDING FROM THE SAME LANDING, landing-safety rather than load: a worktree created with 'git worktree add -b <branch> origin/main' has its UPSTREAM set to origin/main, so a bare 'git push' in that worktree offers HEAD:main and fails with exit 128 ('The upstream branch of your current branch does not match'), suggesting 'git push origin HEAD:main' as the remedy. It refused rather than pushing to main, so nothing was lost — but the suggested remedy is exactly the wrong thing for a lane to follow in a hurry. Either do not set upstream on creation, or make the landing path always name the refspec.

EVIDENCE: /tmp/lgx-push.log (first refusal, environment-probe), /tmp/lgx-push3.log (green re-run, 353/0), /tmp/lgx-probe-mine.log and /tmp/lgx-probe-main.log (3/3 alone in both trees), /tmp/lgx-suite.log (the extension-approval-ui failure and its error).

Serialized live and acceptance pre-push stages via /tmp/voicebox-gate.lock; added per-run nonce to systemd transient units in lib/unit-fence-provider.mjs. All gates passed clean in 220s.
