comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
VOICEBOX-UI, 2026-09-23, with a NAMED load source — the third instance this bead mentions, and the first where the load was known rather than assumed.

THE OBSERVATION: a full-suite run failed THREE tests while MY OWN Vite (:5221) and API (:8899) were running on the same box for an unrelated exploration:
  · "extension approval in Chromium: console code admits and runs, replay/tamper/audit failure refuse" (25.2 s before failing)
  · "N20.7 'denied' is a state of its own: distinct code, its own reason, and it is recorded"
  · "THE PAGE CANNOT DECLARE A ROOT (by name), and the host's declaration drives the loop"
Each passes ALONE (tests/extensions-ui.test.mjs 6/6; N20.7 ✔), and with my instance STOPPED the same tree runs 347 / 344 pass / 0 fail. So the red was load, not the branch — the same shape as this bead's other two cases, with the difference that the load had a name and an owner: me.

WHY IT NARROWS THE FIX: the load a lane feels is not only OTHER lanes' work — it is often the lane's own dev instance (Vite + server), which it started to drive the change it is about to push and left running. A gate that needs ten lanes to idle is expensive to schedule; "stop your own instance before the gate runs" is a one-line discipline each lane can apply alone, and it would have removed this instance entirely.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT MECHANICAL RATHER THAN DISCIPLINED (either is cheap):
  · the pre-push hook prints the box's load and the listeners it can see on the scratch/dev ports BEFORE it starts, so a lane recognises its own instance in the failure rather than after it;
  · or the hook refuses EARLY, by name, when the suite's own budget is likely to be exceeded ("the box is carrying N node processes; stop your dev instance or expect 60 s to be tight"), instead of failing three unrelated tests and letting a lane debug them;
  · or the browser-driving suites take a lock (one at a time) rather than a global slot, so a lane's own idle Vite — which is not running a suite — does not count against it.

The evidence for whoever fixes it: my run is reproducible by starting `PORT=8899 node server.mjs` and `PORT=8899 vite --port 5221` in a worktree and running `npm test` in the same tree, then stopping both and running it again.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: SECOND OCCURRENCE, same test, 2026-09-23 (ds-flash-1b): tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs failed inside the full suite again at 20.5s ('extension approval in Chromium: console code admits and runs, replay/tamper/audit failure refuse'); suite 357 tests/353 pass/1 fail/3 skip. It passes 1/1 alone in both the feature worktree and main's tree. Two live tests (this one and environment-probe) have now failed the gate three times today between them, each passing alone, with no code change between the red and the green. The load-sensitivity claim in this bead is no longer a theory; it is the observed behaviour of the gate on the box we always run it on.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DIAGNOSTIC (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-23): **THE INTERFERENCE IS THE SUITE'S OWN CONCURRENCY, NOT THE BOX** — driven, and it changes the recommended fix.

THREE MEASUREMENTS:
1. **The two known victims run TOGETHER pass 4/4 in 7s** (tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs + tests/environment-probe.test.mjs in one node --test invocation). So the simplest neighbour hypothesis — those two colliding with each other — is REFUTED. A listener census immediately before and after showed **zero chrome/chromium listeners** and 60 sockets total (ten lanes' servers), and tests/lib/cdp.mjs launches Chromium with **--remote-debugging-port=0**, so a fixed-port collision is not the mechanism either.
2. **The full suite SERIAL passes: 'node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/*.mjs' → 357 tests, 354 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped, exit 0, in 230s — at load average 36.31.** That is the decisive one: the box was MORE loaded than during any refusal and the suite still passed, because the files were not running concurrently.
3. The refusals all happened with the DEFAULT runner (concurrent files): extension-approval-ui failed inside the suite at ~20.5s twice, environment-probe once, each passing alone and now together.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX, and it is not the port we assumed: **the primary fix is concurrency control inside the test stage, not a quiet window.** The chrome-agent-platform pattern (scripts/lib/quiet-window.ts counting active compilers / heavy-gate-slot.ts taking a slot) is still worth having for CPU/dispatcher fairness, but it would NOT have prevented these refusals — a quiet window waits for load to drop, and this run passed at load 36. The mechanism is live Chromium/CDP tests sharing the runner with the other files.

REVISED FIX DIRECTION:
(a) the pre-push test stage runs a FAST LANE (unit, non-live) with normal concurrency;
(b) the LIVE suite runs with bounded concurrency (or as its own serial stage), with its own budget — note the measured costs: concurrent ~33–40s vs serial 230s, so the current 180s test budget CANNOT hold a serialized run and the numbers must move together;
(c) keep the slot/quiet-window idea as a second-order improvement, not the fix — and if it is ported, make it say what it waited for.

ACCEPTANCE (unchanged in shape, sharpened): (1) a push under load runs the fast lane and is not refused for load; (2) a deliberately concurrent live run reproduces a victim failing INSIDE the suite while the same test passes alone and passes in the serial run (that is the fault injection for this bead); (3) the serialized live path reports why it serialized; (4) a genuinely red tree is still refused. EVIDENCE: /tmp/lgx-pair.log, /tmp/lgx-serial.log, /tmp/lgx-push.log, /tmp/lgx-push4.log, /tmp/lgx-suite.log.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
THE FIX, FROM A LANE THAT MEASURED IT (voicebox-ui, 2026-09-24) — coord asked for this sentence on the bead because it is the argument for the fix rather than a restatement of the problem.

"FREEING SIX PORTS DID NOT MOVE CPU, BECAUSE IDLE LISTENERS ARE NOT THE LOAD. THE LOAD WAS A SUITE — AND THE FLEET RULE ALREADY ON THE BOOKS IS ONE FULL SUITE AT A TIME WITH THE LANDING LANE FIRST." (CAP has that rule; voicebox does not.)

THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND IT, taken during coord's fleet hunt:
  listeners   67 -> 62 -> 39     (after killing 6 stale listed ports, then a 19-process orphan cluster)
  node        79 -> 68 -> 44
  load 1min   35.70 -> 47.31 -> 40.31   (nproc 32, so load/core stayed ~1.3-1.5)
  chromium    70 -> 27 -> 28
Why the middle reading went UP while I was removing load: a LIVE full-suite run was in flight between the readings (`timeout 900 node --test --test-concurrency=1` over 40 test files, a browser per browser-test) and it finished mid-hunt. That is the load. The stale listeners I removed were idle: they held ports and sockets, not CPU.

WHAT FOLLOWS, and it is what this bead's description already points at: a fast lane on every push (unit tests, bounded) with the LIVE, browser-driving suite SERIALISED — landing lane first — is the lever. Killing stale processes is hygiene, not throughput: worth doing (six ports freed, 19 orphaned children reaped, and every one of them held a socket), but it will not bring load/core under 0.35 while two lanes run the full suite at once.

AND ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE FOR THE SERIALISATION ARGUMENT SPECIFICALLY: the same suite, run alone on an otherwise idle tree, is 347/344/0 in this lane's experience; the same suite under one other lane's run produced THREE failures — the extension-approval drive, N20.7 and the page-cannot-declare-a-root drive — every one of which passes alone. That is this bead's defect, reproduced with the confound named rather than assumed.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:

- The mechanism measurement: full suite SERIAL passed 357 tests/354 pass/0 fail at load average 36.31 — HIGHER than during any refusal — so the interference is between test FILES, not the machine.
- AFTER, measured at load 19.5: unit 15s concurrent (175 tests), live 186s serial (182 tests).
- AFTER, through the real hook: the push ran [lanes] ok: 23 unit, 42 live → unit → live → acceptance → ALL GATES GREEN, 182s total, exit 0. The budgets moved WITH the concurrency (90/400/45), because raising concurrency without raising the budget converts a flake into a timeout.

FALSIFICATION, and here is the honest gap: tests/pre-push.test.mjs now drives SIX real pushes through the two lanes (unit timeout, unit failure, live timeout, acceptance timeout, acceptance failure, success) asserting the stage, the cause, the budget AND the measured elapsed (elapsed must not echo the budget), the remedy naming that stage's own variable, streaming, and that a refused push leaves the remote untouched. tests/test-lanes.test.mjs pins the classification, the comment-vs-code trap, and both known victims in the LIVE lane. comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
A NAMED TEST AND A NAMED ASSERTION FOR THE LOAD CLASS (voicebox-ui, 2026-09-24, during a real pre-push gate refusal).

THE REFUSAL, verbatim from the gate's own output:
    [gate] pre-push REFUSED: tests (npm test) — FAILED (exit 1); see the command's output above.
    ℹ tests 347   ℹ pass 343   ℹ fail 1   ℹ cancelled 0
    ✖ N20.7 'denied' is a state of its own: distinct code, its own reason, and it is recorded (4475ms)
      AssertionError: the blocked folder was not adopted
LOAD AT THE MOMENT: 50.63 (1-min), 31.04 (5-min) on 32 CPUs.

WHY THIS IS THE LOAD CLASS AND NOT A REGRESSION, with the evidence:
  · the SAME branch pushed GREEN three minutes later through the same gate after one instrumented retry — so nothing about the change is broken;
  · the same suite passed 347/344/0 in the SAME TREE minutes before, and passes now;
  · N20.7 passed in isolation earlier tonight when it was one of three failures in a loaded run (the other two: the extension-approval drive and the page-cannot-declare-a-root drive).
  · NOTE ALSO: the failure is exit 1, NOT the gate's 124/137 timeout path — the new gate names a timeout with budget and elapsed, and it did not. So this is a test that ran and failed under load, which is a different (and more interesting) defect than "the suite ran out of clock".

THE ASSERTION ITSELF IS WORTH A LOOK BY WHOEVER OWNS N20: "the blocked folder was not adopted" is a permission/adoption assertion failing under load — if a browser drive times out waiting for a picker/permission flow, the assertion reads as a product failure. That is the same shape as the acceptance harness's environment failures: an assertion that cannot distinguish "the product refused" from "the drive did not get there in time".

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
THE LIST, so this bead carries the pattern rather than five anecdotes (coord's count, with my own observations marked).

DISTINCT LIVE TESTS THAT HAVE FAILED UNDER LOAD IN ONE EVENING:
  1. extension-approval-ui  — failed twice (coord), and once in MY run (voicebox-ui) while my own Vite+API were on the box; passes alone 6/6.
  2. environment-probe      — coord's list; passed alone 3/3 in both the feature worktree and main's tree.
  3. room-page-owned-root   — coord's list (a test I wrote tonight; it has bounded waits and still failed under load).
  4. settings-dialog        — coord's list.
  5. the `pozs` serial-phase fixture — coord's list.
  6. N20.7 'denied' is a state of its own — failed in MY run and again at a real gate refusal (exit 1, assertion "the blocked folder was not adopted", load 50.63); passes alone.
  (And in the same runs: the page-cannot-declare-a-root drive, also passing alone.)

FIVE-PLUS DISTINCT TESTS IS NOT FIVE UNLUCKY TESTS — it is a suite with a systemic concurrency problem, and the shape of it is consistent: every one of these drives a real browser through a timing-sensitive flow (a picker, a permission prompt, an approval, a settings dialog, a phase boundary), and under contention the drive does not reach the state the assertion expects. The assertion then reads as a product failure.

WHAT THAT IMPLIES FOR THE FIX (worth stating next to the list): bounded waits and serialisation help, but the deeper repair is that a drive which never reached the state should FAIL AS AN UNREACHED-STATE, not as the assertion it never got to test — "the blocked folder was not adopted" is indistinguishable from "the drive timed out before the product could refuse". A named unreached-state failure would (a) stop these reading as product regressions and (b) tell a lane instantly whether to re-run or to investigate.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
THE FLAKE REPRODUCES BELOW THE LOAD THRESHOLD — so "re-run when the box is quieter" is not sufficient, and the remedy in this bead's theme (serialise the live suite) is necessary but not sufficient either (voicebox-ui, 2026-09-24).

TWO CONSECUTIVE GATE REFUSALS ON TWO DIFFERENT LIVE TESTS, same branch, same tree:
  · refusal 1 — `N20.7 'denied' is a state of its own` / "the blocked folder was not adopted", at LOAD 50.63
  · refusal 2 — `extension approval in Chromium: console code admits and runs, replay/tamper/audit failure refuse` (19.5 s), at LOAD 25.0 (1-min), i.e. BELOW the ~35 threshold coord suggested for retrying
Both pass ALONE in the same tree and same branch (extension-approval-ui 1/1, n20-permission-denied 1/1), and the same suite passed 347/344/0 in this tree earlier — so the branch is not the variable.

WHAT THAT RULES OUT AND WHAT IT LEAVES:
  Ruled out: "the suite needs an idle box". At load 25 (32 CPUs) a live browser test still failed. So the mechanism is not CPU starvation.
  Left standing, and this is the part worth fixing: live browser tests are contending for something shared that is NOT CPU — a port, a profile directory, a /tmp path, a per-user resource (compositor/DBus), or an ordering assumption between tests that the runner's default concurrency breaks. That is a concurrency defect in the suite, not a load defect in the box.

THE EVIDENCE A FIX WOULD NEED: run the full suite with the live tests SERIALISED (one live test at a time, unit in parallel) at load 25 and see whether both of tonight's failures disappear. If they do, the fix is a lane in the runner, not a threshold in the gate. If they do not, the next step is to capture, for each failure, the state the drive actually reached (my "unreached-state" note on this bead) so the assertion stops reading as a product failure.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
THE SHARPEST MECHANISM YET: A DETERMINISTIC SYSTEMD UNIT NAME COLLIDES BETWEEN CONCURRENT LANES (voicebox-ui, 2026-09-24, from a real gate refusal).

THE REFUSAL, verbatim:
    [gate] pre-push REFUSED: live (npm run test:live) — FAILED (exit 1)
    ✖ the composed environment's probe report shows seccomp=2, the EROFS code tree, and the writable home — and it SERVES
    AssertionError: the composition did not boot: {"ok":false,"refused":"unit-refused",
      "why":"the transient unit did not start — Failed to start transient service unit:
       Unit voicebox-fence-vb-test-l15-measure.service was already loaded or has a fragment file."}
(a test in tests/unit-fence-provider.test.mjs, 49 ms to fail)

WHAT THAT MEANS: the fence test starts a TRANSIENT SYSTEMD UNIT WITH A FIXED NAME (`voicebox-fence-vb-test-l15-measure.service`). Two lanes running the same test at the same moment both claim that name, and the second gets "already loaded or has a fragment file". The check then reads as "the composition did not boot" — a product-shaped failure for a name collision between runs.

EVIDENCE IT IS A COLLISION AND NOT A LEAK: the unit is NOT loaded now (`systemctl --user status voicebox-fence-vb-test-l15-measure.service` → "could not be found"; no transient file), and the test passes ALONE 5/5. So nothing was left behind; the failure window is the overlap between two runs.

WHY IT BELONGS IN THIS BEAD: it is the same family as the load flakes — concurrent runs interfering — but with a sharper, cheaper fix that is NOT scheduling: give the transient unit a PER-RUN name (a pid or random suffix), and the fence test stops colliding with itself fleet-wide. That is a test fix, not a gate threshold, and it would remove one of the refusal classes outright.

FULL RUN OF TONIGHT'S REFUSALS I HIT, since they are all this bead:
  · live  — N20.7 'denied' is a state of its own (assertion "the blocked folder was not adopted"), load 50.63
  · live  — extension approval in Chromium (19.5 s), load 25.0 (below the threshold)
  · unit  — the denylist refuses retired literals by file and line (f0b): its internal docs-check probe died with
            "fetch failed … SocketError: other side closed", the scratch server's stderr tail showing
            "fatal: Needed a single revision" — which is the build stamp's `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` on a
            worktree whose branch has no upstream. Worth its own look: a lane worktree prints that on every boot.
  · live  — the composed environment's probe report (this entry): the systemd unit-name collision.
Every one passes alone; every one is in another lane's area; and each cost ~3.5 minutes plus a retry.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DATUM for this bead's load story (vb-ui, 2026-09-24): the biggest single contributor to leftover load on this box was NOT the suites themselves but their leaked fence sandboxes — 42 orphaned 'voicebox-fence-*' systemd units after one night, ALL 42 with a dead creator pid, holding 98 bwrap + 49 node processes, ~3.3 GB summed RSS and 49 ports = ~69% of every LISTEN socket. Stopping my own 8 dropped listeners 71 -> 22 in seconds.

That pressure is exactly what times out browser-driving tests: in the cv1 review, the extension-approval test failed at 17.7s in full-suite runs (reproducibly WITH one more heavy browser file present, absent without it, and passing in isolation on both trees) while the gate's own serialised lanes stayed green — the same concurrency mechanism already recorded here, now with a memory/port dimension.

Cause found and fixed: POST /api/environments booted a transient unit and nothing ever stopped it (no stopUnitFence call, no DELETE route). Tracked and closed as journal-4kp: reaped (49 units -> 0), product fix landed at dc8ceaf (RuntimeMaxSec default 1800s + VOICEBOX_FENCE_MAX_SEC override, host-token-gated DELETE /api/environments/<key>, exit hook), and I verified all three by driving them (25s cap read back off the unit; a 10s-capped unit left alone stopped itself in 5s; DELETE 403 without the token with the unit surviving, 200 with it, gone in 1s; SIGTERM took a 5-minute-capped unit down in 1s). If this bead's flakes persist, measure units and listeners FIRST — that variable is now bounded, so it should stop moving.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: DATUM (vb-ui, 2026-09-24 22:5x): the live lane failed **37 tests** twice in a row inside the pre-push gate, all with the same signature — 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading evaluate)', i.e. the page LAUNCHER returned null, not an assertion failing. comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
RETRACTION of my datum above, plus the real cause (vb-ui, 2026-09-24). I filed this as "a new shape of the load-sensitive gate: the launcher returning null at load 47.77". THAT WAS WRONG. The 37 live failures were caused by MY OWN unguarded call: `askDurable()` called `navigator.storage.persist()` without checking the function exists, and in a dedicated worker an absent method throws a SYNCHRONOUS TypeError that `.catch()` cannot see — which took `openProject` down (`root-unreachable`, "no project is open") in every page-driven suite. Coord read the code and found it; I confirmed it empirically: after the one-line guard, tests/confirm-gate.test.mjs passes 5/5 and page-writes + one-root + opfs-scratch-room pass 13/13 ON THE SAME LOADED BOX, and the full gate went from 236 pass / 37 fail to 275 tests / 273 pass / 0 fail.

WHY MY ATTRIBUTION LOOKED DECISIVE AND WAS NOT: I reproduced with suites that happened to pass in isolation (modal panels passes 2/2 — it never opens a project through the worker), and I read "passes in isolation" as "not my change". Isolation changes the condition; the right test exercises THE SAME PATH as the failure. "It passes elsewhere" is not an attribution.

The launcher-null symptom remains a real possibility under saturation — but this instance of it was mine, and this comment should not be read as evidence for the load story.

title: Bound the awaits in the revocation-termination test, so a regression FAILS instead of HANGING
description:
FOLLOW-UP from the yo1 review (voicebox-ui reviewing gemini's feat/pairing-revocation). Not a blocker for the landing — an improvement to the test, not to a behaviour.

THE EVIDENCE: I disabled the live-session termination in MY OWN COPY of revokePairing (never their branch) and ran their test. It caught the mutation — so the instrument has teeth — but it caught it by HANGING: the test ran for 399 SECONDS with no failure, because the close await (`await livePeer.closed`) is an unbounded await and the socket simply never closes when the implementation is broken. My bounded driver (a Promise.race against a timeout) found the identical mutation in seconds, naming it twice: 'B4 revocation closes the live socket — close=null' and 'B5 the PROVIDER session ended — closed=false'.

WHY IT MATTERS: a mutation has THREE outcomes — RED (the check works), GREEN (the check is weak), HUNG (the instrument is broken) — and HUNG is the one that gets reported as inconclusive and then forgotten. Worse, it burns the gate's 60-second `npm test` budget on a timeout that names nothing, instead of naming the regression.

THE FIX: bound every await in the termination chain — `Promise.race([closed, timeout])` — and assert what never arrived in the message ('the /live socket was never closed by the revocation'). Same shape as the bound already in tests/live-session-flag.test.mjs, whose teardown learned this lesson when a mutation hung it at 240 s (voicebox-beads-0i1).

SCOPE: tests/pairing-revocation.test.mjs — the /channel and /live close awaits, and the vendor-socket-closed wait.
close_reason: Landed on origin/main @ f896be3.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
THE HUNG RUN DOES NOT JUST FAIL SLOWLY — IT LEAVES LOAD BEHIND, and I have the process to prove it (voicebox-ui, 2026-09-24).

FOUND: pid 2321196, a `node server.mjs` alive for SEVENTY-SIX MINUTES, running from a worktree I had already REMOVED (its cwd read `(deleted)`). Its environment named it exactly:
    PORT=0   VOICEBOX_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/tmp/vb-revocation-test-iSOzV2/extensions
— the scratch dir of the revocation test this bead is about. I spawned it by running that test with my mutation, watching it hang for 399 seconds, and killing the run at the timeout. THE CHILD SERVER OUTLIVED THE PARENT and kept its port and socket.

WHY THAT MAKES THIS A GATE FIX RATHER THAN A TEST TIDY-UP (coord's framing, and it is right): an unbounded await turns a regression into a 399-second hang; the runner kills the run; the child it spawned keeps running; and that load lands on the NEXT lane's gate, which is already known to refuse good branches under load (voicebox-beads-6qu — coord is adding this to its context). The 399-second hang and the gate refusals are the same defect seen twice.

TWO PLACES TO FIX, and the second is the mechanical version of "stop your own instance":
  1. THE TEST (this bead's original scope): bound the awaits — Promise.race against a timeout, with an assertion naming what never arrived. Then a broken implementation FAILS in seconds instead of hanging, and nothing is left to orphan.
  2. THE HARNESS (proposal, not implemented, and it would protect EVERY test, not only this one): tests/lib/server.mjs spawns the server as a child, and nothing reaps it if the RUNNER is killed. Two cheap options: spawn children in their own session and have the harness kill the whole group on exit/SIGTERM/SIGINT, or have the child watch its parent (a pipe that closes when the parent dies → the child exits) — the same "no child outlives its parent" property the served-tree scripts are missing (voicebox-beads-zuq is the sibling finding for voicebox-serve).
  The same applies to the Chromium the CDP launcher starts, though that one closes its own profile in the normal path.

REPRODUCTION FOR WHOEVER FIXES IT: run the termination-chain test with the live-session termination disabled (in your own copy), wait for the hang, kill the run, then `ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep server.mjs` and look for a process whose extensions dir is a scratch path. Mine was 76 minutes old when coord's load note sent me looking.

PRIORITY IS COORD'S: the fix is small (bound a few awaits), but its consequence is other lanes' gate refusals, which is why it moved from "test tidy-up" to this.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P1 by coord (2026-09-23). Reason: the hung-test path is a LOAD SOURCE for the pre-push gate, not merely a slow test.

MECHANISM, observed: an unbounded `await livePeer.closed` hangs the revocation-termination test. The runner is killed at the budget (399s observed). THE CHILD SERVER OUTLIVES THE PARENT — a `node server.mjs` from `worktrees/vb-yo1` was found alive 76 MINUTES later, cwd already `(deleted)`, holding a port and a socket. Identified exactly by its environment: `VOICEBOX_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/tmp/vb-revocation-test-iSOzV2/extensions` (the scratch dir of gemini's revocation test), so it was that run's child.

REPRODUCTION for whoever fixes this: disable the live-session termination in your own copy, let it hang, kill the run, then `ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep server.mjs` and look for a scratch extensions dir.

TWO FIXES, and the second is the general one:
1. Bound the awaits in the test (`Promise.race([closed, timeout])` with a message naming what never arrived). Already scoped on this bead.
2. PROPOSED BY voicebox-ui, NEEDS A ROUTING DECISION because it touches a shared helper: `tests/lib/server.mjs` spawns the server as a child and NOTHING REAPS IT IF THE RUNNER IS KILLED — true of EVERY test, not this one. Fix: spawn children in their own session and reap the group on exit/SIGTERM/SIGINT, or have the child watch a pipe that closes when its parent dies. THE SAME "NO CHILD OUTLIVES ITS PARENT" PROPERTY THAT `zuq` IS MISSING for `voicebox-serve` — one family, two instances.

WHY P1: the gate fix (`6qu`) established that refusals come from the suite's own concurrency rather than box load, and that a serial run passes at load 36. A test that leaves a server behind for 76 minutes adds exactly the kind of contention that makes concurrent runs fail — so bounding these awaits and reaping these children is part of making the gate trustworthy, not tidying a slow test.

Context: `6qu` (gate concurrency) and `zuq` (voicebox-serve's lingering subshell). Filed by voicebox-ui; priority and routing by coord.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
BUILT, MUTATION-VERIFIED, COMMITTED — **NOT PUSHED: the gate refused on the UNIT stage's budget, and the file that ate it is named below.** Commit 9ee7578 on **fix/6io-bound-awaits** (local only; the remote does not have it).

WHAT IS IN THE COMMIT: every remaining unbounded await in the revocation-termination chain now bounded and NAMED — openWithin() for the 8 socket-open waits and fetchWithin() for the 15 fetches (the close half already had closeWithin()) — and tests/lib/server.mjs registers every spawned child in LIVE_CHILDREN the moment it exists, reaping it on process.on('exit') with the same reaper stop() now uses. One way a child dies instead of two.

MUTATION EVIDENCE (the drive the bead asked for): with live-session termination disabled on purpose ('if (false) runningSession.socket.close(1008, …)', reverted afterwards), the suite FAILS IN 4.2 SECONDS with:
  AssertionError: active /live session socket must close within 4000ms — hung close is a regression, not a pass
against the ~399s hang the bead records. Unmutated: 3/3 green in 5.7s. My outer bound was 120s and it was never needed.

THE REFUSAL, exact: '[gate] pre-push REFUSED: unit (npm run test:unit) — TIMED OUT — budget 90s, elapsed 90s (exit 124); suite completion is unknown, not a test verdict — re-run when the box is quieter, or raise the budget with VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS=<n>.' The suite names the consumer: **tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs took 89,649ms** — one file consuming essentially the entire unit-lane budget.

WHY THIS IS NOT A 6io DEFECT, and whose it is: the 90s unit budget is mine, set from a measurement of 15s for the lane at load 19.5 (voicebox-beads-6qu). tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs has landed since and builds wasm modules, so the lane's real cost is now ~105s and a single slow file sits against the budget's edge. Either the budget rises (VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS, one line in scripts/pre-push.sh) or that file belongs in the live lane (it does toolchain work, not unit assertions) — both are one-line changes, both belong to the 6qu family rather than to this bead, and coord has the naming decision. Stopping here per the rule rather than folding a second subject into this branch.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE OF THE UNIT-LANE TIMEOUT, DRIVEN (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-24): **tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs HANGS AT EXIT — all 9 of its tests PASS and the process never returns.** It is not slow toolchain work.

EVIDENCE: running it alone, bounded by me at 150s: exit 124 at 149,958ms with 'tests 10' started and **9/9 ✔** reported — the assertions all completed (ms to 5s, including two deliberate 5s LGW deadline tests) and the runner still never exited. So the lane's 90s budget was cutting a process that had finished its work but was being held open by something in the event loop — an unresolved handle (a worker, timer or child not closed), most likely in the LGW termination path this file exercises (its own test names: 'the loop module is terminated BY NAME at the host's deadline', 'the grow module dies against the host's bounds').

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TWO APPROVED FIXES: classifying the file as live *'because it compiles WASM modules'* would be a FALSE REASON — the file imports lib/wasm-shelf.mjs and core/extensions.ts and calls no compiler, spawns no process and shells out to nothing (checked by grep for clang/exec*/spawn/wat2wasm/emcc: no hits). And raising the unit budget to 180s would convert an infinite hang into a 180s refusal: the wall moves, the defect does not. I have therefore implemented NEITHER, and I am saying so rather than making a red go away for the wrong reason.

THE HONEST FIX, in the same shape as this bead: find the handle that outlives the assertions in tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs and close it (or bound that test's teardown), so the file EXITS. If the leak is in the module's own termination path, that is a product-side finding worth its own bead — a wasm module that is 'terminated BY NAME' while its host keeps a handle open is a promise the process does not keep. A stop-gap that is at least honest: node's --test-force-exit on the unit lane, named as a stop-gap, for files known to leave handles. Budget headroom (180s) is still worth having separately.

title: [security] /channel executor channel requires local page origin or pairing bearer
close_reason: LANDED on main @ 76abcf8. Independent review PASSED by merger. Merged feat/channel-auth (d9326f6) cleanly into main. Full pre-push gates green (npm test 331 tests passed, npm run accept all clear in phases A & B). Pushed to origin/main.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED & PUSHED (gemini): branch feat/channel-auth @ 354b59f6cc44c34e8939fe3534cb962fdea0ad73.
1. Reproducer: Demonstrated that /channel previously accepted unauthenticated connections from Origin: http://evil.com, assigned pageSocket = ws, routed OPFS file writes to the rogue client, and accepted forged ok responses with via: 'page'.
2. Fix: Dual-gate entitlement mirroring /live:
   - Local page admitted by Origin header check (localOrigins: 127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1], and proxied via vite.config.js proxyReqWs).
   - Non-local / remote peers require a valid pairing bearer in hello within VOICEBOX_HELLO_BOUND_MS (default 5000ms), verified via bearerAcceptedByThisHost.
   - Refusals are named (executor-unauthenticated / bearer-refused), closed with WS 1008, and unauthenticated sockets are NEVER assigned to pageSocket.
   - GET /api/root always reports executor status truthfully even when undeclared.
3. Limits: Does not protect against local processes forging Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port> on loopback; closing that requires per-process session tokens minted into HTML (environment-identity work). Closes CSWSH from browser contexts and unauthenticated remote access.
4. Gates: 331 tests (328 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail; 33.6s), npm run gate PASS (ALL GATES GREEN; phases A & B clean). 6 new tests in tests/channel-auth.test.mjs. Docs updated in docs/08-wire-protocol.md, docs-check clean.

title: Admitted tools act in VOICEBOX_WORKSPACE, not the declared root — one root by design, two by wiring
description: qwen2, driven on origin/main @ 9ae64e8 (two scratch roots, tool proposed/admitted/called): an admitted tool's act lands in VOICEBOX_WORKSPACE, not the active declared root. title: voicebox-serve never returns when its output is piped (a lingering subshell holds the caller's pipe)
description: TITLE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 after reproducing it on scratch ports. The original title claimed the environment could be LEFT DOWN; that half was NOT reproduced (the children survived every kill of the caller). What IS confirmed: a piped invocation never returns, because a lingering subshell of the script holds the caller's stdout pipe. See the comment for the full mechanism, the correction and the fix shape.
close_reason: Applied verified patch ~/voicebox-evidence/zuq/voicebox-serve-zuq.patch to ~/.local/bin/voicebox-serve: subshells redirected and exec used so lingering subshells do not hold piped stdout. Verified pipe returns cleanly.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CORRECTION, 2026-09-23, from reproducing it on SCRATCH PORTS (8899/5199, a copy of the script with the ports patched, so Paul's environment was never at risk).

CONFIRMED: the piped invocation NEVER RETURNS, and the source is a LINGERING SUBSHELL, not the servers.
  · The script's own output completes: 12 lines, ending with both URLs -> 200. Both halves START and SERVE (8899 and 5199 answered 200 through the LAN and Tailscale addresses).
  · And yet the caller blocks forever. While it blocked, the pipe was held by TWO processes whose cmdline is 'bash serve-scratch.sh start' — subshells of the script — with fd1 = the caller's pipe. (Bash shows the parent's cmdline for a subshell, so /proc is the only place this is visible.)
  · The node/vite children are NOT the holders: their fd1 pointed at their own log files, exactly as the redirect asks. My original hypothesis ('children inherit the pipe's stdio') was wrong in attribution even though the symptom is what it predicted.
  · Nothing was killed by any of this: the children survived the caller being killed, repeatedly, in every scratch run.

WITHDRAWN: 'can leave the environment down when its output is piped'. NOT REPRODUCED. The children survive; I could not substantiate that half. What I observed in the original incident (both halves down when I checked) is more consistent with the script still being mid-start — it sleeps 2 s per attempt, retries the API up to three times, and stops the API between attempts — when the blocked caller was killed. The bead's consequence was overstated and the corrected one is narrower: A PERSON WHO PIPES THIS, OR ANY WRAPPER THAT CAPTURES ITS OUTPUT, WAITS FOREVER. That is still a defect worth fixing (a wrapper cannot tell 'still starting' from 'finished'), it is just not 'the environment dies'.

THE FIX, from the mechanism: no subshell of the script may outlive it holding the caller's stdout. Either  the children so the subshell IS the child ('( cd "$DEV" && exec setsid nohup node --watch server.mjs </dev/null >"$API_LOG" 2>&1 ) &' — one process, no lingering bash), or keep the subshell and redirect its own stdio too. setsid is worth adding regardless: it makes a kill of the caller unable to reach the children, which is what I wrongly assumed nohup already did.

CHEAP REPRODUCTION FOR WHOEVER FIXES IT: copy the script, patch the two ports, stop it, then run it piped with a bound and look for a surviving bash whose fd1 is the pipe (ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd). Do not reproduce it against 8787/5173 while Paul might be using the page — the whole point of the scratch copy is that the bug eats the caller, and a caller is easier to replace than an environment.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
EVIDENCE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS — the lingering subshell survived 40+ minutes and several kills of its children.

At 15:4x I found, still alive, the subshell that the piped run had left behind: 'bash /tmp/vb-rate/serve-scratch.sh start' (pid 4112083, started 14:28:39, parent the setsid'd shell that launched the pipeline) — while the node --watch child it had started (pid 4112085, the scratch API on :8899) was still serving. So the subshell not only outlives the script: it outlives everything anyone does to the child. Both were mine and both are now killed, confirmed by cmdline and cwd and the PORT=8899 in the environment before I touched them.

That is the mechanism in one observation: the script's own subshell is the thing holding the caller's stdout, and nothing else notices it.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
MECHANISM FOUND AND FIXED IN A PATCH — verified by drill, NOT applied to Paul's script (his file is untouched; md5 51dcfc21bb4868ff982f90df395ad556, mtime unchanged).

MECHANISM, read from the invocation rather than inferred: both spawn sites use the same shape
    ( cd "$DEV" && [PORT=…] nohup CMD > "$LOG" 2>&1 & )
`A && B &` inside `( … )` backgrounds the WHOLE `&&` list in a hidden subshell. The `> "$LOG" 2>&1` redirect applies to the nohup command that subshell spawns, NOT to the subshell itself — which is why the node/vite children legitimately point at their own logs while a `bash voicebox-serve start` subshell holds the caller's fd 1. Two sites, so two holders. That reconciles both earlier observations: the symptom was right and the attribution (children inherit the pipe) was wrong.

FIX (one line changed at each of the two sites; `exec` is the load-bearing part):
    ( cd "$DEV" && PORT="$API_PORT" exec nohup node --watch server.mjs > "$API_LOG" 2>&1 ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    ( cd "$DEV" && exec nohup ./node_modules/.bin/vite > "$UI_LOG" 2>&1 ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
The subshell's own stdio is redirected (so it cannot hold the caller's pipe even if it lingers) and `exec` replaces the subshell with the command (so there is no shell left to linger). Patch: ~/voicebox-evidence/zuq/voicebox-serve-zuq.patch — applies cleanly to the real script (`patch --dry-run` checked), `bash -n` clean, and the patched file's own read-only `status` subcommand runs correctly against Paul's live environment.

DRILL (~/voicebox-evidence/zuq/drill.sh; scratch ports 8899/5199 only, named pipe as the caller's pipe, /proc/<pid>/fd/1 scanned for holders):
- BEFORE (original two lines): DRILL FAIL — holders named by pid: 364997 and 365022, both `bash …/scratch.sh start`; the script's own work completed (exit 0), the caller's reader blocked (cat exit 124), and both halves served 200. That is the reported symptom exactly: the invocation never returns although the environment is up.
- AFTER (both lines patched): DRILL PASS — no holders of the caller's pipe, caller exit 0, reader exit 0, api 200, ui 200.
- FALSIFICATION: reverting the two lines and re-running the SAME drill returns the FAIL with two holders named — same script, same ports, same instrument; only the two lines differ.

TWO FINDINGS ABOUT THE METHOD, both filed here rather than smoothed over:
1. My first fix attempt DROPPED `PORT="$API_PORT"` while rewriting the line; the scratch API then aimed at the real 8787, failed to bind (EADDRINUSE against Paul's live server — it never took the port) and my drill still reported PASS because it only asserted the pipe property. The drill now also requires both halves to answer 200 on the scratch ports, so a fix that leaks nothing but breaks the server cannot pass. Paul's environment answered 200 throughout; his server was never disturbed.
2. The scratch harness patches its ports and its two server logs but writes the recovery log to the SHARED real path /tmp/voicebox-dev-recoveries.log, so a scratch run's failures land in the owner's recovery history. Six such lines (14:56:45–14:56:54 today) were mine; an attribution note now sits at the end of that file explaining them, and nothing of Paul's was deleted. A scratch harness should route that path too.

STATE: patch verified and awaiting Paul's decision to install; this bead stays OPEN because the fix is not on his system. Install (his call): `patch ~/.local/bin/voicebox-serve < ~/voicebox-evidence/zuq/voicebox-serve-zuq.patch` (or apply the two lines by hand), then start the environment fresh so the new invocation is the one running.

title: live-tools waits for the FILE, then asserts the tool EVENT with no wait — a flake that looks exactly like a real failure
description:
SYMPTOM (corrected 2026-09-21): tests/live-tools.test.mjs fails roughly 1 in 3 FULL-SUITE runs; it PASSES 3 of 3 SOLO runs. The flake is LOAD-DEPENDENT — it appears only under contention, which is what makes it the kind of defect that gets dismissed as flakiness and re-run past.

FOUND BY: ds-flash-2 while re-measuring the gate timeout (voicebox-beads-gzm), 2026-09-21. Evidence: cap-evidence/voicebox-gzm-review-20260921/ (the failure, the passes, the contended run) and cap-evidence/voicebox-flake-review-20260921/ (five loaded runs, the withheld-event mutation, the predicate mutation).

MECHANISM: tests/live-tools.test.mjs:89 waits for the WRONG SIGNAL.
  1. send the write request
  2. wait up to 60s for the FILE to exist — for (let i = 0; i < 300 && !existsSync(target); i++) await sleep(200)
  3. assert the file exists  — PASSES
  4. assert byte-for-byte    — PASSES
  5. then assert the page-visible tool EVENT with NO WAIT AT ALL:
     assert(tools.some((t) => t.calls.some((c) => c.name === 'write_file' && c.ok)), 'the page-visible tool event did not report the write')

THE FILE LANDS SERVER-SIDE; the tool event travels back over the websocket AFTER it. So the file appearing is NOT a barrier for the event, and under load the event arrives a few milliseconds late. NOT a timeout that is too short — A WAIT ON THE WRONG SIGNAL.

FIX (landed): the assertion waits within the existing 60s bound for the file AND a successful write_file event: writeReported() = tools.some(t => t.calls.some(c => c.name === 'write_file' && c.ok)). Polls the SPECIFIC property, name AND ok.

VERIFIED: five loaded full-suite runs green (16 busy loops, load to 27.9); withheld-event mutation RED; and the predicate proven behaviourally — with the write landing on disk but the event marked ok:false, which a poll on 'any tool event' would accept, the test went RED.

TAIL NOTE from the review: at load ~27 a single browser test ran 137.3s against 7.4s idle, so the 180s gate budget leaves ~43s of headroom in the worst measured case.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the symptom line, 2026-09-21 — the bead as filed reads 'fails 1 in 3 FULL-SUITE runs and 3 of 3 solo runs', which implies solo FAILED. It did not.

CORRECT READING: the test FAILS roughly 1 in 3 FULL-SUITE runs, and PASSES 3 of 3 SOLO runs. The flake is LOAD-DEPENDENT — it only appears when the box is busy running the whole suite beside it, which is entirely consistent with the mechanism: the file lands server-side, the tool event travels back over the websocket after it, and under load the event arrives a few milliseconds late.

This makes the finding STRONGER, not weaker: a defect that appears only under contention and never in isolation is exactly the kind that gets dismissed as flakiness and re-run past. It also confirms the diagnostic shape — the assertion has no wait at all, so it loses the race only when the race is close.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW — voicebox-beads-8fv.3 @ 93c0879 (vb-ui, different family from the author). Verdict: **REVISE** — one substantive finding, with the rest checked and passing.

CHECKED AND PASSING: the rebase onto current main is clean; `tests/fleet-addressability.test.mjs` passes 7/7 (1.0s), including its CDP browser test; the target-key formatting/parsing, the two-agents-on-A/one-on-B resolution, the session-contact-vs-replacement refusal and the browser-local zero-server execution all pass as they are written. `GET /api/fleet` with no credentials returned only the LOCAL environment's agents and no environment identifiers — nothing from another environment was disclosed in that listing.

FINDING F1 (substantive — a refusal that INVENTS a fact about a machine it never reached). Driven by hand against my own instance of the candidate: I declared an environment whose origin is unreachable (`http://127.0.0.1:9` — nothing listening) through the host act (`POST /api/environments` with the host token, which accepted it, key `env_849ffa24932a7d29`), then asked the room to contact an agent in it:

  POST /api/fleet/contact  {"target":"env_849ffa24932a7d29/some-agent","message":"hello"}
  -> {"ok":false,"refused":"agent-not-found","why":"No agent 'some-agent' found in environment 'env_849ffa24932a7d29'"}

That sentence asserts a fact about the REMOTE environment's contents, and the server cannot know it: it never reached that environment. The truthful answer is that the environment could not be reached, nothing was sent, and no lookup happened. Worse, it is not only a wrong sentence but a collapsed one — the same code and shape answer three different situations: an environment nobody declared (`env_deadbeef00000000`), a declared-but-unreachable one (above), and an absent agent in a reachable one (`local/my-agent`). This is the exact collapse the codebase already warns about in writing: core/root.ts's doctrine that "root-not-declared" and "root-not-reachable-from-here" must never merge, because the remedy differs. Here the remedy differs too: declare/pair the environment, fix the network, or correct the agent name.

AND THE CORE KNOWS BETTER — this is where I would look first: lib/fleet.mjs already models reachability (`env.reachable !== false && env.state !== "unreachable"` -> `{ state: "unreachable", why: "Environment '<key>' is stopped or unreachable" }`), and the proxy path in server.mjs has an `environment-unreachable` refusal with the transport's own message. So the honest states exist on both sides of `fleetManager.contact()`; they are being flattened into `agent-not-found` by that call. Suggested shape: resolve the target first (which environment, is it declared, is it paired), answer each absence by name (`environment-unknown`, `environment-not-paired`, `environment-unreachable` carrying the transport's reason, `cross-environment-unauthorized` for the auth case), and answer `agent-not-found` ONLY when the environment was actually asked and answered.

FINDING F2 (observation, phrased as a question because I could not drive a HEALTHY second environment with my remaining budget): `GET /api/fleet` listed two entries, both `environmentKey: "local"`, even with a second environment declared. So the listing does not expose remote agents, and the contact route's resolution appears to work against that same local index. If that is right, then targeting an agent in a HEALTHY second environment cannot resolve either — which would make "multi-environment agent targeting" (the headline) unrunnable through this surface, and F1 would be the visible symptom of a bigger gap. If instead the resolution contacts remote environments for their agent lists on demand, then F1 alone is the fix and the listing's local-only shape is a deliberate choice worth saying out loud in the docs. I could not settle which without standing up a second working environment, and I am out of budget for that; the author knows instantly which it is.

LIMITS OF THIS REVIEW, stated rather than implied: I read the diff's shape and ran the author's suite; I did not line-by-line review all ~980 added lines (`core/fleet.ts`, `lib/fleet.mjs`, `server.mjs`), and I did not drive the cross-environment path against a reachable second environment, the turn-tool path, or the browser view beyond running the author's own browser test. My verdict rests on the author's suite plus the hand drive above.

INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE: my first probe returned empty responses because I redirected the server log into a directory I had not created; the finding above is from the second run, with the server confirmed up.

comments.text:
RE-REVIEW of the revision @ 43c8102 (vb-ui). My finding is FIXED. Verdict: **PASS**.

WHAT I VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, by hand against my own instance of the revised candidate:
· An environment nobody declared -> `environment-unknown`, with a plain remedy ("declare it before calling it").
· A DECLARED environment whose origin is unreachable (http://127.0.0.1:9) -> `environment-not-paired`, naming it and the remedy. Before the revision this same request answered `agent-not-found` with the sentence "No agent 'some-agent' found in environment '<key>'" — i.e. a claim about a remote's contents that the server could not know. The collapse is gone, and the two outcomes I could drive are DISTINCT.
· `GET /api/fleet` listed only `local/...` entries, which is consistent with the declared environment being unpaired (there is nothing to fetch from it) — so the revision's remote-discovery claim is not contradicted, and its precondition (a pairing) is stated in the code.

READ IN THE SOURCE (the decisive case, whose sentence is the whole point of my finding): lib/fleet.mjs returns `refused: "environment-unreachable"` with `why: "environment '<key>' is unreachable: ${err?.message ?? err}"` for a transport failure — the transport's OWN cause, and nothing about what the remote does or does not contain. A second variant answers `"environment '<key>' is unreachable"` from the environment's state. Neither asserts anything about a machine that was not reached, which is exactly the defect I reported.

THEIR TESTS: `tests/fleet-addressability.test.mjs` passes 7/7 and now asserts the precedence table directly — `environment-unreachable` at :177, `environment-unknown` at :393, `environment-not-paired` at :416 against the unreachable origin. So the decisive sentence is verified by their test plus my reading of the source, not by my own end-to-end drive. title: Harness configuration: distinguish runtime, configured agent and execution environment
description:
WHY: docs/03-architecture-k3.md sections 1 and 9 already distinguish harnesses and named agent instances; D3 promises list_agents/list_harnesses, but no concrete configuration/identity contract connects them. Do not create a second environment registry or duplicate D3 discovery.
WHAT: define and implement the smallest secret-free configured-agent record associating a stable configured-agent ID, harness/adapter identity and pinned versions, executing environment key, description/default selection, model reference, needed root/network/tool reach and enforceable bounds. Separate that record from transient ACP session/task IDs. One harness implementation can have multiple configured instances in the same environment. Labels are not identities. Separate configured claims from timestamped observed readiness/enforcement; unknown cost/latency/reliability stay unknown. Authority and credential references belong to the environment owner, never model-supplied commands, cwd, URLs or bearer values. Browser-local configuration must work without a server registry; share the contract, not the physical secret store. D2 consumes admitted configuration; D3 exposes safe inventory. Preserve independent harness use outside Voicebox.

BINDING REQUIREMENT (Paul, 2026-09-21): the harness must run anywhere, including entirely in a browser client with zero Voicebox server or local bridge. Server deployment is allowed for machine access, not required by the shared contract. Placement changes available capabilities, transport, storage and lifetime; it must not fork the coordination semantics. A browser cannot spawn a stdio CLI; refuse that unavailable capability rather than hiding a server dependency. Zero server does not mean zero remote model API.
