comments.text: CLOSED — feat/attempted-lost @73460f0 (pushed; whole gate 202 tests: 201 pass + 1 environment skip, 0 fail; pre-push gate + page acceptance ALL CLEAR; porcelain empty). The delivery vocabulary is in the audit: every act past pre-flight is recorded BEFORE it applies (decision attempt, result pending, boot = the process generation); every outcome carries attempt back to it (allow with observed facts = CARRIED; refuse with rule id = REFUSED); a process death between attempt and outcome leaves a DANGLING attempt, and the next boot's sweep completes it AS LOST — by name, idempotently, because 'whether it landed' is then unknown and must not silently read as either success or refusal. The bead's three classes map: refused-before-apply and refused-with-no-partial are refused entries; attempted-and-vanished is lost. Driven: write -> attempt + carried outcome linked; dangling attempt from a dead generation -> lost completion named attempted-and-lost, idempotent; pre-flight refusal -> refusal entry, NO attempt (the act never entered the applying phase). LIMITS: the crash case is driven by its exact state (a pending entry from a dead generation), not by a timed SIGKILL; /api/call and the write verb carry attempt-first — other verbs (read/list) stay outcome-only, which is the right weight for read-only acts; the isocan CLI half of the bead (naming the three classes to the person) is isocan's side of the seam.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: CONTINUITY ADDENDUM @73b1e4a (pushed; coord elevated finding 2 of the review): resumeLog no longer swallows-and-resequences. ENOENT = genuinely fresh (silent); ANY other read failure = a NAMED throw (audit-unreadable) — because a log that exists but cannot be read has an UNKNOWN continuation, and appending with a reset sequence would hand fresh numbers to entries with ancestors. logAct surfaces it: the entry is NOT written, the response carries logged:null + logRefused/logWhy, and the console names the break. Driven: chmod 000 on the audit file -> logged:null + audit-unreadable; mode restored -> the sequence continues FROM the log's last seq; no duplicate seqs in one instance's log. (The strictness found a real bug in the drive itself first: my own arithmetic assumed one entry per write — attempt-first writes log two.)

title: resolveInsideRoot is wrong AND unreachable: the doc names it as the containment boundary, nothing calls it, nothing tests it
description:
Found while answering PR #9's Copilot review comments, verified on main (a15557e6).

THE DEFECT — core/paths.ts:23-33:
  line 24: rejects only candidate === '.' or candidate === '..' (EXACT matches)
  line 27: resolved = root + '/' + candidate   <- string concatenation, not path resolution
  line 29: prefix check: resolved.startsWith(root + '/')
For candidate = '../../evil.sh': resolved = 'root/../../evil.sh', which DOES start with 'root/', so the check PASSES and the function returns ok:true for a path that escapes the root. The '..' segments are never collapsed, so the prefix check cannot see them.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL BUG: line 28's own comment says 'The prefix check is the OPFS containment boundary'. docs/02-environment.md relies on it as the containment-preserving write path, and N20 says the picked-root path REUSES it. So a guard is documented as doing a job it cannot do — the shape where the weaker version of a guard is more dangerous than its absence, because its absence is visible.

CURRENT BLAST RADIUS — measured, not assumed: grep across *.ts/*.mjs/*.js finds NO callers. resolveInsideRoot is defined and never invoked, and there are no tests for it (a test would have shown up as a caller). So it is NOT exploitable today. The exposure is: the moment the picked-root write path actually uses it, the escape works, and the doc already tells the next reader that containment is handled here.

FIX: resolve the candidate properly and reject on the RESOLVED path (normalise '..' before the prefix comparison), or reject any candidate containing a '..' segment. Then a test with the counterfactual: '../../evil.sh' must be REFUSED — a test that cannot fail proves nothing, so the assertion must name the escaping string.

RELATED: PR #8 was merged to main at a15557e6, which is the same N20 content PR #9 rebuilds. So the fix belongs on a branch off a15557e6, and PR #9's disposition needs deciding by diff.
close_reason: Fixed and verified 2026-09-19: core/paths.ts now refuses any '..' segment at any depth rather than prefix-checking a concatenated string; landed on main (0d7b832, PR #10 merged at 4ef7bc1). Counterfactual both ways — old resolver 3 cases RED including the escaping assertion, fixed 6/6 with a positive control and an invariant test. k3 reviewed it independently and PASSED (reviewed ref 9fac1a8). The three claims were corrected too: the false comment on core/paths.ts:28, docs/02-environment.md, and the build-spec check now pointing at the test rather than a promise.

comments.text:
SLICE BUILT, GATE REFUSED ON A LOAD FLAKE (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-23) — NOT PUSHED, commit a96ecdb is local-only in ~/worktrees/voicebox-lgx (branch feat/lgx-host-permission).

WHAT IS BUILT (host side of the round trip, the smallest real piece): createAcpClient(transport, { …, decide }) — a host-supplied permission decision. No decider => 'cancelled' exactly as before (safe default unchanged; the existing acp suite passes 3/3 unchanged, not updated to agree with a new behaviour). Validation BEFORE the host is asked (session must match, options well-formed and bounded) and again AFTER (a grant must name an option actually offered AND of an allowing kind; a reject kind or an unoffered id is refused, not sent). Every non-validated path denies, including a decider that throws — failing to decide is not allowing. A foreign session never reaches the host. client.permissions() keeps the last 32 decisions WITH REASON, because the wire's only denial is 'cancelled' and cannot say whether a person said no or a deadline ran out (seam agreed with the kei lane: transport holder owns the pending record and expiry; UI is never the authority; disappearance denies; expiry/cards/escalation stay policy-side). SCOPED (deliverable 1 of 2; lane CHANNEL). Grounded in the page's own id inventory from `public/` and the named-refusal precedents on the server, not in a guess about what might be missing. **I did not build the follow-on slice — see the last section for why, and for the exact two reads it needs.**

WHAT THE SURFACE ALREADY HAS (read off the ids, so this narrows the bead immediately):
- Presence-ish, already named: `voice-state`, `voice-ring-wrap`, `server-dot`, `session`, `session-heading`, `session-log`, `turn-report`, `catch-up`, `where-note`, `mic-device-state`, `out-device-state`.
- Assets, already named and richer than expected: an asset form (`asset-form`, `asset-kind`, `asset-name`, `asset-body`), an arrival list (`made`, `made-heading`, `made-list`), a `gallery`, `files`/`file-*`/`file-facts`/`file-copy`, `dropzone`, `pick`, `reader*`, `new-file`, `input-path`, `output-path`.
So "we need an assets surface" is FALSE and "we need a presence indicator" is FALSE. What is missing is narrower: **which states those elements are derived from, and whether a person can tell the two things that are currently inferred rather than seen.**

THE TWO INFERENCES A PERSON HAS TO MAKE TODAY (candidates, each with how it would be observable):
1. **"Is the agent THERE?" — not "is the mic live".** The page can show mic level (waveform, meters, `mic-*`) and a reply (ring, text), which are both *local*. Nothing in the ids above names the *provider* side of the session: whether the model connection is open, being opened, or gone. Derivation that exists and is real: the wire's own absence vocabulary — `no-page`, `machine-unreachable`, `page-timeout`, `machine-timeout`, `page-closed`, `machine-closed` (`lib/channel.mjs`, six named states, all distinct in what a caller can act on) — plus `GET /api/health`'s provider/build, and the server-side precedent for honest naming: `environment-list-unreadable` (fix the file) vs `environment-unreachable` (fix the host) at `server.mjs:69-73`. Observable as: one line that says WHICH side is absent, derived from the channel's own state, not from a timer.
2. **"Is it THINKING, or idle, or done?"** `voice-state` exists, so the question is what feeds it: local audio state cannot distinguish "the model is working" from "the model said nothing". Derivation: the harness's turn lifecycle (a turn in flight vs settled) — the same fact `turn-report` and `session-log` already record after the fact, needed *during* it. Observable as: a state derived from an in-flight turn, with the failure case named (a turn that never settles) rather than a spinner that means nothing.
3. **"Did the thing that arrived ARRIVE, or is it just listed?"** `made-list` and `gallery` show what is there; they do not say whether an artifact produced by a tool call was *adopted* (written where the person can keep it) or merely previewed. Derivation: the write path's own result (the environment registry pattern: a file the live path could not write must say so — the same class as the footer-promising-files defect noted at `server.mjs:73`). Observable as: per-artifact state, named on the row.

RECOMMENDED FIRST SLICE (argued, not assumed): **candidate 1, presence**, because it is the only one whose state is *already written down* (six channel absences + the health route) and whose failure mode is the one a person feels first — "is anyone there?" — while candidate 3 needs a path I have not verified exists.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, and why: I did not build the slice. My review budget for this session is spent after the night's reviews, and the slice needs two reads I could not afford: (a) `public/live-voice.js` + `index.html` — what `voice-state` and `server-dot` are *currently* derived from, without which a new indicator would be the decoration this surface has spent two days removing; (b) the route table — whether a provider-side session state is already published, or has to be added. Both are cheap for a fresh lane: one file read each. The scope above is the deliverable that unblocks it, and it says where to look.

comments.text:
MOBILE 6px OVERFLOW — owner, arithmetic, and a VOIDED evidence list. Lane CHANNEL.

OWNER AND ARITHMETIC (read-only measurements, unaffected by the caveat below):
  div.room      offsetWidth 390 · scrollWidth 396   (display:flex, padding 18px → content box 354)
  header.head   offsetWidth 354 · scrollWidth 378   (display:flex, gap 16px, flex-wrap: nowrap — COMPUTED and read, not injected)
  children by right edge: #envs-open 293 · #exts-open 395.9 (ow 87) · p.where 173.7 · h1.wordmark 83.3
  65.3 + 74.4 + 103.3 + 86.9 = 329.9, plus 3 gaps x 16 = 48, total 377.9 ≈ 378 in a 354 box.
  So the row cannot fit and cannot wrap: the last child runs 24px past its container's edge, 18 of it inside .room's right padding and the final 6 past the viewport. That is the 6px, fully accounted for.
  NOTE the measurement that found it: offsetWidth vs scrollWidth on CONTAINERS, not an element right-edge scan — a rect scan finds symptoms, because a container whose content is wider than its box has no element poking past the viewport until the padding is spent.

FIX CANDIDATES, with the number: `.head { gap: 16px → 8px }` saves exactly 3 x 8 = 24px, which is the whole overflow; `.head { flex-wrap: wrap }` is the structural alternative. Apply as a REAL CSS EDIT in an own worktree + own server — never by injection — then verify by reading the computed property BACK (confirm gap/flex-wrap actually changed) and scrollWidth at 360/390/430 + landscape, committed alone with the element and the arithmetic in the message.

A VOIDED EVIDENCE LIST — do NOT act on it, and do NOT record it as falsification: `.made-actions .quiet { min-width: 0 }`, `min-width: 0` on flex items (including the `*` wildcard), the header being too wide, `#exts-open` as the cause, `body { overflow-x: hidden }`, the `#envs/#exts` dropdown, and `html`/`body { overflow-x: clip }`. All of these were tested by INJECTING a `<style>` into the running page, and **every injection was blocked by the page's `Content-Security-Policy: style-src 'self'`** — proven three ways: the console reports "Applying inline style violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'style-src 'self'' … The action has been blocked" (17 violations), and after injecting `header.head { flex-wrap: wrap !important }` the computed `flex-wrap` read back as `nowrap`. Every trial returned identical numbers because every trial was the baseline. None of those hypotheses was falsified; none was even fired.

THE LESSON, and it is the same shape as the stale ref and the truncated read, so it belongs with them: **on a page served with `style-src 'self'`, browser-injected styles are a no-op instrument and every conclusion drawn from one is void.** Nine were built before anyone read a computed value back. The check is one line — after injecting anything, read one computed property back, or glance at the console — and it is the difference between a measurement and a story. **Verify the instrument, not just the result.**

comments.text:
EXPLORATION DONE (voicebox-ui, 2026-09-24) — driven in a real browser against my own instance (api :8899, front :5221, machine root /tmp/vb-kcs/root, vendor stubbed locally so "ready" is reachable with no provider and no spend). Tree: origin/main at fb5d4b6 in worktrees/vb-kcs. Full write-up with the state table, the arrival timeline and screenshots: /tmp/vb-kcs/FINDINGS.md (evidence: /tmp/vb-kcs/observations.json, arrival-observations.json, *.png).

NOTE ON SCOPE, for the reader: this bead's description is the ASTRA interface study (isocan visual language, synthetic assets, brief N10-N13, "proves nothing about actual OPFS, enforcement, live audio"). What was asked of me and what I did is the other half: what the REAL product shows a person, observed before judging. The study's artifacts are on design/astra-interface and were NOT reviewed here.

WHAT WORKS (measured, so the findings below are proportionate):
- The voice states are all distinguishable IN WORDS: "Mic off · press to speak", "Connecting to the live session…", "Waiting for the model · N frame(s) held until setup completes", "Listening — speak now", "Agent speaking · your microphone is on (interrupt any time)" — and the mic button's colour follows the state. Connecting → listening in <=150 ms against a stub that answers immediately.
- An arriving asset is genuinely announced and really appears: the turn report reads '"<my words>" wrote second-arrival.txt (14 bytes) in /tmp/vb-kcs/root' (name, size, place) at 150 ms, the list's own count goes "1 file" -> "2 files" and the card appears at 300 ms with NO refresh, the card is a button.file-open that opens the reader with provenance ('14 bytes · read from disk'), and a file arriving while the reader is open does not disturb the reading (same file still open, aria-current intact, scroll preserved). Arrivals are announced to assistive tech: #turn-report and #voice-state are role="status".

FINDINGS (three, each with the evidence that shows it):
1. IN THE CONNECTED-AND-SILENT STATE NOTHING MOVES — and @keyframes breathe exists, used by nothing. getComputedStyle over every element reports no animation in either the cold or the listening state, and the mic button's opacity is a constant 1 across ten samples over 1.2 s. The only motion on the page is playback (the output ring) and the input wave when sound is captured. style.css:123 defines @keyframes breathe and no rule uses it (the only `animation:` declarations are the skeleton loader and a reduced-motion override). So presence while connected-and-quiet rests on three STATIC things: the sentence, the button colour, a hairline ring that is drawn but still — a glance at the room cannot tell "listening" from "stopped".
2. A NEWLY ARRIVED FILE IS NOT MARKED AS NEW. The fresh card carries no class, no data-* and no animation; the only per-card marking is aria-current="true", which marks the file the reader has OPEN (fused.js:488) — a different question. The count and the report line change (and are live regions), so the arrival is announced in words, but in the list nothing distinguishes the card that arrived a second ago. With many files, and a person who looked away while speaking, the list does not answer "what did I just make?".
3. THE SUGGESTED TURNS LIVE INSIDE THE "MADE WHILE WE TALK" SECTION, UNLABELLED. index.html:131 nests ul#samples inside section#made-list, so under the heading and the count ("3 files") a person also reads three imperative sentences that were never made. They ARE visually distinguished by CSS (.samples button: muted, underlined, smaller), so this is a labelling observation rather than a hard defect — but typography is the only statement that they are not files.

OBSERVED, NOT JUDGED: whether a breathing cue is wanted at all is a design decision, and the room is deliberately quiet ("a quiet room with a working reader in it"). Finding 1 is offered as evidence — an unused keyframe named breathe suggests the cue was once intended — rather than as a redesign. Findings 2 and 3 are small, local and evidence-backed.

NOT OBSERVED, stated rather than implied: the provider-error state (my stub never errors); a real vendor's audio (the ring was driven with synthetic PCM through the page's own playback path); arrivals into a page-owned/routed root (machine root only here); phone and PiP surfaces.

WHAT THE REAL-PRODUCT HALF PRODUCED — three findings, each now its own landed-or-pending change (three branches, one concern each, all handed to the landing lane; none pushed by the explorer):

Rule: [data-voice="listening"] .output-ring path { animation: breathe 4s ease-in-out infinite; } — the PATH, not the SVG, because the path carries opacity:0 and animating the SVG would have multiplied that zero and done nothing.
  · fix/mark-arriving-file @ 77e6990 — a card that just arrived is marked (data-arrived) and the mark is swept at ~3 s; a first listing is NOT an arrival, and a mark that outlives its window is the house defect (both were my own first versions' failures, recorded in the commit).

WHAT WORKS, MEASURED, so the findings stay proportionate: every voice state is distinguished in words (off / connecting / waiting for the model N frames held / listening / agent speaking) with the mic button's colour following it; a written file is announced with name, size and place, appears in the list with no refresh (count 1 file -> 2 files at ~300 ms), its card opens the reader with provenance, and a file arriving while the reader is open does not disturb the reading.

NOT OBSERVED, stated rather than implied: the provider-error state (stub never errors), a real vendor's audio, arrivals into a page-owned/routed root, and the phone/PiP surfaces.

comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW of feat/extension-admission @ 40a030c5 (reviewer: lane CHANNEL, a different model family). Verdict: PASS on six of the seven claims, with ONE enforcement finding. Full report: ~/journal/reports/2026-09-20-voicebox-extension-admission-review.md.

THE FINDING — the mediated fetch checks the FIRST URL, then lets fetch follow redirects (lib/extensions.mjs:273 checks, :284 fetches). Driven: a tool whose bounds.hosts is ["127.0.0.1"] was pointed at my own declared host, which answered 302 -> http://localhost:8800/api/extensions (localhost is NOT declared). The call returned the body served by the undeclared host while reporting host "127.0.0.1". Three observed consequences: (1) the admission disclosure says the tool "gets" a mediated fetch that refuses unlisted hosts "by name" — true of the initial URL, not of where the bytes came from; (2) the budget counts CALLS, not hops — one call that made two requests counted 1/3; (3) the audit entry records act.target as the declared URL and observed.bytes 8577 served by localhost, so a followed redirect is invisible. The class is SSRF-shaped: any declared host that redirects reaches an undeclared origin. Fix shape is the author's call; `redirect: "manual"` with a named refusal for a 3xx, or re-check Location per hop and charge each hop.

VERIFIED AS PASSING, driven and not read: POST /api/extensions/register and /reload are 404 and an unknown admit is 404; a hand-dropped extensions/*.json does not hot-load (unknown-tool) while the host directory IS loaded at startup (positive control); pasted source is data — a descriptor carrying JavaScript in seven fields including process.exit(7) was admitted, called, ran only its declared primitive, left no marker file and retained none of the code fields, and code-shaped primitives refuse by name (unknown-primitive, capability-unmediated, bad-tool-name, exec-absent, network-unbounded); host-not-allowed / budget-exhausted refuse by name; sideload is inert end to end (confirm-first stages nothing; staged stays pending; admit without confirm decides nothing; confirm:"true" is not === true); MCP local refuses exec-absent with the container upgrade path named AND lands as an audit entry carrying the rule id, MCP remote is admissible with no process, and "remote" is not a flag that gets past the gate (declaring exec refuses whatever runsIn says; a remote descriptor carrying command/args was admitted and never used them — there is no launcher in the tree); core/extensions.ts has NO imports and package.json has no runtime dependencies.

Suite re-run by me: 46/46 (client-audio 13, containment-paths 6, extensions 14, live-voice 2, voicebox 11). Notes, not findings: the evidence's §10 grep is a cwd slip (workspace/audit.jsonl exists and carries the refusals with rule ids); the command in the suite's parenthesis runs 25 of the 46; `node --test tests/` (directory form) fails; and the extensions test's before hook deletes the tracked extensions/ directory and rewrites it, so a crash in between loses tracked files.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW of c6b3b823 (the wire shapes; reviewer: lane CHANNEL, different model family from the author). Verdict: PASS on all four claims, with ONE defect in a pure function. Report: ~/journal/reports/2026-09-20-voicebox-wire-shapes-review.md. Suite re-run by me: 58/58.

THE DEFECT — core/wire.ts:101: parseCall's object branch tests the uninitialised `obj` instead of `raw` (`} else if (obj && typeof raw === "object") {`), so EVERY object argument is refused as "malformed-call" / "the call is not an object" — including a good call. Driven both ways with the same data: an object (even one smuggling decision:"allow") -> malformed-call; the same data as a JSON string -> unknown-field (correct). Latent on the wire (strings), NOT latent for this commit's own framing: the in-process round trip. ExecutorDoor.receive makes it visible rather than better — it JSON.parses a copy for the callId probe (lib/channel.mjs:106) but passes the ORIGINAL raw to parseCall, so the door's stringify never reaches the parser. One word to fix at :101 (obj -> raw); parseAnswer:157 does it correctly (`raw && typeof raw === "object"`), so the typo is singular.

VERIFIED, DRIVEN: (1) envelopes — good call ok=true with observed ["action","content"]; tampered boundsEcho -> bounds-mismatch with the why QUOTING the admitted bounds ("hosts":["127.0.0.1"]) so a routed call cannot carry its own bounds past the echo and the gate underneath is the one I verified at 0ddba0a5; forged descriptorId -> unattributed-call; missing boundsEcho -> unattributed-call. THE BONUS HOLDS: a descriptor refused at admission (mcp-server-local, exec-absent) is not in the registry, so a call naming it refuses unattributed-call ("no admitted descriptor 'mcp-server-local' carrying tool 'mcp_list_tools'") — the refusal bites before an executor exists; I tried its real tool name and its own fields as boundsEcho and both land on the same named refusal. (2) channel contract — an unconnected peer refuses no-page in words and sends ZERO messages; four bad answers (garbage, a valid answer for another callId, an answer smuggling grant:"everything", ok with no observed) NONE settled the pending call (waiting() stayed 1) and the real answer then settled it; an inaudible peer gives an honest page-timeout rather than a wrong success; abandon() settles with machine-closed. (3) the vocabulary — six names, all distinct AND distinct in what a caller can act on: no-page, machine-unreachable, page-timeout, machine-timeout, page-closed, machine-closed. (4) the boundary — decision:"allow" on a call -> unknown-field, grant:"everything" on an answer -> unknown-field, ok with no observed -> malformed-answer.

NOT REPORTED AS A DEFECT: no live transport endpoint (deliberate), and the peer-parameterisation is real — the same envelopes, validators and vocabulary carried my stand-in peer over a captured pipe.

title: Name compliant mode's mechanism: a pi extension that asks via ctx.ui.confirm()
description: Two drives against the real bridge produced ZERO session/request_permission for ordinary tool calls: pi's only built-in gate is project trust, which is an input-loading guard. The protocol path is wired end to end and pi never uses it. Until the extension exists, Tier 2 lives only in mediated mode and environmental containment, and the tier table must be presented as a DISCLOSURE for the harness's built-in tools rather than a boundary.
close_reason: Built and driven by k3 (eb1d5fd, rescued to design/k3-compliant-mode; code at rescue/compliant-mode-extension 3fe1d92). Twenty-line tool_call hook: intercept -> plan in the harness's own words -> ctx.ui.confirm() -> block -> honour. Three proofs driven: a denied call does not execute (write denied, model tried a shell redirect, denied, read probe denied, file does not exist); the plan arrives before the act; the gate holds for a model-authored tool (read_host asked and denied) - the C5 loophole closed. ds-flash-2 claimed compliant mode in docs/02-environment.md 1.1a with four limits, the first being that the audit must read the world rather than the transcript.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Naming the mechanism, and one part of this bead's framing is now superseded — both from ds-flash-2 (the environment design's owner), and both with the document as the source.

**The protocol is now named, so the extension can be written against it rather than against a reference to another repository.** It is **ACP — the Agent Client Protocol** (`agentclientprotocol.com`, with a published adapter registry: the adapters are `@agentclientprotocol/*` packages, and `pi-acp` is one of them). It is a standard, not CAP's protocol: CAP's bridge is one *client-side* implementation, and `docs/02-environment.md` §1.6 now writes the shape out in two lines so nobody has to go and find it.

**What the extension has to do is unchanged and confirmed**: hook a tool call and ask the client via the permission path, so that `session/request_permission` is actually used. Until it exists, Tier 2 is **disclosure** for the harness's built-in tools.

**But the second half of this bead's framing needs correcting, and qwen2 found why from pi's source: _trust is on discovery_.** `.pi/extensions` loads only after the project is trusted — while runtime `registerTool()` has **no equivalent gate**, and an in-process registration **inherits the harness's full authority immediately, because it never passed through a discovered location**. So:

- **the extension must not become a new ungated door.** If it registers tools at runtime, those registrations bypass the very gate the extension exists to provide. What closes that is a **registration-time authority decision** — allow or deny, plus a **reason string**, not a descriptor pipeline — and it must answer **two** things, because *dynamic registration and remote execution compose into a call nobody authorised*: what may run, and **where its call goes**.
- **and `/reload` is not the trigger.** `registerTool()` works during load *and after startup*, registered tools are live **in the same session**, and pi ships `examples/extensions/dynamic-tools.ts` doing exactly this. So "the host owns the extension directory and the reload trigger" (the sibling bead `bxx`) covers the **file path** into the system and not the **registration path** — necessary, not sufficient.

Document reference for whoever picks this up: `docs/02-environment.md` §1.1a (the four enforcement shapes) and §1.7 ("the loop that must never run ungated", and the substrate rows).

title: lib/branch-landing.mjs runGit inherits GIT_DIR — branch listing/diff/landing can act on the wrong repo (the 946i class, in the tool that merges and pushes)
description:
Found reviewing voicebox-beads-946i (gitEnv isolation for lib/tool-index.mjs). The same class, one module over, and this one MERGES AND PUSHES.

OBSERVED (measured, not inferred): lib/branch-landing.mjs's runGit(repoPath, args) spawns git with `cwd: repoPath` and NO env, so it inherits the process environment — and GIT_DIR outranks `cwd` (the documented lesson in lib/git-env.mjs's own header). Probe (/tmp/946i-landing-probe.mjs, kept in the 946i review evidence):
  declaredRepo: /tmp/946i-declared-…   foreignRepo: /tmp/946i-foreign-…
  listCandidateBranches(declared) with a clean env   -> ["declared-only-branch"]
  listCandidateBranches(declared) with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE pointed at the foreign repo -> ["foreign-only-branch"]
  steerable: true
So under any environment that carries git's local plumbing (a pre-push/commit hook, a gate stage, the merger's own hook chain — exactly what voicebox-beads-n48i measured), listCandidateBranches/inspectBranchDiff answer about the WRONG repository, and landCandidateBranch() — which merges and pushes — could act on it. Today's callers are tests/branch-landing.test.mjs and the landing-inspector mini-app surface, which is what makes this latent rather than live; the doctrine is the same either way: a measurement (or an act) on a tree must not be steerable by the environment of whatever ran it.

REPRO: the probe above (two temp repos, one branch each, GIT_DIR pointing at the second).

FIX DIRECTION (one line + one test): in lib/branch-landing.mjs, import { gitEnv } from "./git-env.mjs" and pass `env: gitEnv()` in runGit's execFileSync options; add a regression in the shape of tests/tool-index.test.mjs's new test (poison GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, assert listCandidateBranches(declared) names the declared repo's branches, non-git vars survive, the caller env is not mutated).

RELATED: voicebox-beads-n48i (the branch-landing TEST fixture inherits GIT_DIR under a hook and commits into the lane's repo) is the fixture-side half; this is the library-side half. Both must be fixed for the landing path to be safe under a hook, and their fixes are at different sites.

comments.author: Voicebox Test
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW — voicebox-beads-vgeq @ 93e1d06 (branch feat/vgeq-restart-session-on-model-change): the behaviour is REAL and WORKS; NOT CLEARED for one medium and two low findings (all in the tests and one payload sentence, not in the restart itself). Reviewer: deepseek-flash (independent; author voicebox-resolver / Gemini family).

== WHAT I VERIFIED, DRIVEN, WITH A REAL SESSION (not mocks) ==
My own driver (~/cap-evidence/vgeq-review-deepseek/vgeq-drive.mjs) runs the real server, a REAL Gemini /live session started by the real #mic handler, and the real Settings UI, with the page's WebSocket constructor and close() instrumented. 12/12 checks:
• the OLD socket was closed with code 1000 and reason "model-changed" — the scope's exact claim, observed on the real socket;
• the old socket really CLOSED (the server's close handler ran, so the provider session was torn down);
• a NEW live socket was created, opened, and the restarted session became READY again with capture running (no stuck/failed state);
• the status payload's runningSession.model is the NEW model after the restart (GET /api/agent-settings);
• the page says nothing about a failure (no "unavailable/failed/ended" text);
• changing the VOICE does not restart (the trigger is model-specific);
• one mic click after a restart STILL MEANS STOP (no extra socket, capture off, live-active false);
• with no live session, a model change opens no socket.
Also green: the author's two suites (17/17) and npm run test:unit (438 pass / 0 fail). server.mjs's beginSession() snapshots provider+model at session start, so a reconnected socket genuinely uses the new model; runningSession.model is recorded at upgrade, and the payload carries it.

== FINDING 1 (MEDIUM — test truthfulness; the scope's "CDP tests green" is true but is NOT coverage) ==
tests/agent-settings-ui.test.mjs's two new tests do not exercise the code they assert on:
• Test 1 REPLACES the functions under test — `window.__voiceboxIsLiveActive = () => window.__mockLiveActive` and `window.__voiceboxDisconnectAndRestartLive = async (reason) => {...}` — so it proves only that saveAgentSetting would call *a* function with that name. It cannot catch a wrong close code/reason, a failed reconnect, or a payload that names the wrong model; deleting the real close(1000,"model-changed") would keep it green.
• Test 2 calls the real disconnectAndRestartLive but fakes the live state via the new test-only hook (`window.__voiceboxSetCapturingForTest(true)`) and there is NO socket, so the `if (socket) { … close(1000, reason) }` branch never runs; `restarted === true` is asserted while the socket path is skipped entirely.
The fix is the shape my driver uses (a loopback /live fixture like tests/live-rate-browser.test.mjs, or a real session in the live lane): assert the close call, the second socket, and the payload model.
Note also tests/agent-settings.test.mjs's addition asserts `applied`/`requested` only — it does NOT assert `runningSession.model`, which is the field the scope's "status payload reflects active model" is about.

== FINDING 2 (LOW-MEDIUM — the PUT note claims an update the server does not perform) ==
server.mjs's PUT /api/agent-settings note now reads `stored — live session model updated to <model>` whenever a model was asked AND a session is running. The SERVER does not restart anything — the PAGE that holds the session does — so a caller that is not that page is told something untrue. Measured (probe: ~/cap-evidence/vgeq-review-deepseek/note-probe.json), running session + PUT from outside the page:
  runningModelBefore: models/gemini-3.8-live   requested: models/gemini-3.8-thinking
  putNote: "stored — live session model updated to models/gemini-3.8-thinking"
  runningModelAfter: models/gemini-3.8-live    pageSessionModel: models/gemini-3.8-live    actuallyChanged: false
That is a second tab, a script, or curl: the note asserts the change took effect while the running session keeps its model. The payload already separates `applied` from `runningSession.model`, and the repo's own design note says `running` exists to answer "did my change take effect?" — the sentence contradicts it. Suggested: "stored — the page holding the live session restarts it with this model; a session started elsewhere keeps the model it started with", or drop the branch and let runningSession.model speak.

== FINDING 3 (LOW — a test seam shipped in the product) ==
`window.__voiceboxSetCapturingForTest` (public/live-voice.js:257) is the ONLY `*ForTest` hook in public/ and it lets any script in the page flip the product's internal `capturing` flag. It exists so a test can fake a live session — the same weakness as finding 1. Recommend removing it (drive a real/loopback session instead) or gating it on the existing `?debug=1` path; the other hooks (__voiceboxLiveSocket, __voiceboxIsLiveActive) are read-only inspection and are fine.

== LIMITS OF THIS REVIEW ==
• Provider: Gemini (the shell's key). The OpenAI path was not exercised; the restart logic is provider-agnostic (close + reconnect), so the risk there is low.
• I did not drive two tabs against one server (finding 2's case is measured through the API directly, which is the same code path a second tab takes).
• No push from me; the branch should land through voicebox-merger after the findings are addressed (or triaged as follow-ups if the owner prefers).

VERDICT: the feature is correct as driven; fix finding 1 (make the tests exercise the socket) and finding 2 (the note), and consider finding 3. Ready for re-review on request.

comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — fixed, verified and pushed on fix/6omi-project-switch-outline @ 6f9ff87 (base origin/main 35b1239). Gate GREEN (docs-touched, docs-check, single-owner, unit 438 pass / 0 fail) — see the push note at the end, it matters.

RECONFIRMED THE CAUSE FIRST (the recon's suspects were right to check, but the answer is neither): driving the production cue on the served page and sampling .stage/.where/.head/.room/.made-list before, every frame during, and after shows NO geometry change at all — no rect, width, height, x, y, padding or margin ever moved. The "jumping" was the PICTURE:
· project-switch-flash ran on the WHOLE stage: a 650ms box-shadow ring spreading 0 → 8px with a 28px glow at 50%, plus `border-radius: 20px` applied ONLY while flashing. On a 1026x650 stage that threw a ~1000x1100 rounded rectangle that grew and shrank once per switch, and the corners popped in and out.
· .where wore the SAME keyframe, so the chip's own quiet `0 1px 3px` shadow became the ring and then vanished (measured: its shadow changed during the cue; it now does not).

THE FIX (public/style.css, following the room's `arrive` cue shape — a fade on a property that cannot move anything):
· project-switch-outline — a 2px accent outline at a 6px offset, fading in at 18% and back to transparent at 100%. An outline cannot reflow, the width is declared only while the attribute is present, and both ends are transparent so the rule arriving and leaving is invisible.
· project-switch-chip — the chip tints to the accent and settles back to its OWN resting border/background/colour, so dropping data-flash at 650ms (fused.js's timer) is invisible.
No radius, no box-shadow, no size, no padding in either keyframe. Before → after, same probe: stage radius 0px→20px became 0px in every sample; stage shadow none→ring became none in every sample; .where shadow no longer changes.

WITNESS: tests/project-switch-outline.test.mjs (live lane) drives the REAL switch (the Browser scratchpad button) AND the production cue, and binds both halves: the cue must be VISIBLE (a non-transparent accent outline appears — deleting the cue fails the test rather than passing by silence), nothing may move, and the two old signatures must be gone (radius stays 0px, shadow stays none across the whole animation). Falsified by restoring the old CSS: red, naming the radius pop ["0px","20px"]. Evidence with before/after shots and the probe JSONs: docs/evidence/project-switch-outline-20261004/.

GATES: unit 438/0 (5.7s); lanes check 58 unit / 95 live; docs:check OK. Design detail worth a reviewer's eye: the cue is decorative, so under `prefers-reduced-motion` the animations are killed by the global rule and the cue disappears — consistent with the existing `arrive` mark, and the root text itself still changes.

PUSH NOTE (unrelated pre-existing gate breakage, filed as voicebox-beads-n48i, P1): pushing this branch from ~/worktrees/vb-6omi was REFUSED by the unit stage on two tests/branch-landing.test.mjs tests. Root cause measured: git exports GIT_DIR to a pre-push hook when the push comes from a LINKED WORKTREE (not from the main checkout), the hook passes that env to the unit lane, and branch-landing's temporary-git-repo fixture does not strip it — so `git init` is ignored and `git commit` lands on the lane's own repo ("On branch fix/6omi-project-switch-outline", every file "deleted"). Repro without the hook: `GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) node --test tests/branch-landing.test.mjs` → 2 failed; clean env → 3 passed. This blocks EVERY lane's worktree push. The same SHA pushed from ~/voicebox (main checkout, clean hook env) is ALL GATES GREEN — same commit, two environments, opposite verdicts. The full mechanism, repro and fix direction (adopt the docs-touched/pre-push GIT-env strip) are on n48i.

The two other places that run git against a named tree already use it (lib/system-tools.mjs:560, server.mjs's isGitRepo/runProjectGit), so the bead's runner was the last product-side gap.
• FALSIFICATION, driven: with origin/main's pre-fix lib/tool-index.mjs restored, the new test FAILS with the intended message ("git answers about the declared root, not the hook repository"); with the fix it passes. The witness can fail on purpose.
• The new test's four claims are real and independent: it poisons GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE at a FOREIGN repo, runs `git init` + `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` through runSystemCommand in the declared root and asserts the answer names that root; it asserts a NON-git variable (CUSTOM_VAR) survives; it asserts a descendant node process sees none of the three plumbing variables; and it asserts the caller's env object is not mutated.
• Caller check: server.mjs:2667 passes only { command, cwd } — no caller-supplied env reaches this path — so the strip cannot surprise a model/user. An env var set INSIDE the command string (`GIT_DIR=/x git …`) still works, which is the person's explicit act, not inherited plumbing.
• Scope check: runSystemCommand has exactly one spawn site in lib/tool-index.mjs (line 674) and it uses this childEnv; nothing else in that file spawns a child.

== GATES (run in a fresh worktree at a8e8e9b) ==
npm run test:unit → 438 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped (matches the author's claim); tests/tool-index.test.mjs → 6/6; node scripts/test-lanes.mjs --check → 58 unit / 94 live; npm run docs:check → OK; node scripts/docs-touched.mjs origin/main → OK via the recorded trailer ("Docs-checked: gitEnv strips ambient git variables in runSystemCommand childEnv; PATH table description remains accurate") — an honest reason, and the gate accepts it.

== NEW FINDING (filed: voicebox-beads-lumm, P2) — the same class in lib/branch-landing.mjs ==
That module's runGit(repoPath, args) spawns git with `cwd: repoPath` and NO env, so it inherits the process environment and GIT_DIR outranks cwd — the lesson lib/git-env.mjs's own header records. MEASURED with two temp repos, each with one branch (probe kept with this review's evidence):
  listCandidateBranches(declared) with a clean env                      → ["declared-only-branch"]
  listCandidateBranches(declared) with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE at another → ["foreign-only-branch"]
This is not a defect in this bead's change (different module), but it is the same steerability, in the tool whose landCandidateBranch() MERGES AND PUSHES, and it is the library-side half of voicebox-beads-n48i (the fixture-side half I filed earlier when a worktree push's unit gate failed). One-line fix (import gitEnv, pass env: gitEnv() in runGit) plus a regression in the shape of this bead's test.

== OBSERVATION (low, not a finding on this change) ==
lib/system-tools.mjs and lib/tool-index.mjs still carry two runSystemCommand implementations. Both sanitize now, so there is no live leak; the duplicate is the drift risk that produced this bead in the first place. Worth folding into one call path when someone next touches either file.

VERDICT: CLEARED — land it (through voicebox-merger). The change is correct, falsifiable, and gated; lumm is the follow-on for the same class one module over, and n48i remains the fixture-side fix.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN REVIEW, then a corrected PASS on the real head. (voicebox-e1m0.)

MY PASS WAS WRONG ON THE GATE, and the merger was right to bounce: I reviewed 704ebb4 and never ran the repo's own copy gate. Running it now: `node --test tests/voicebox.test.mjs` on 704ebb4 → 13 tests / 12 pass / **1 FAIL**: "the pages' prose matches the running system (prose sweep, 2026-09-20)" with `AssertionError: the footer no longer says who reads and writes the folder`. That is exactly the sentence the merger's round-2 bounce named. My review ran the two pin suites the request named (3/3), the unit lane, an accept phase-B, and my own visible-text vocabulary grep — and skipped the sweep, which is the test that exists for exactly this class. For a copy change, the sweep is the first gate, not an optional one. I have corrected my earlier PASS in the record rather than letting it stand as a landing clearance.

CORRECTED VERDICT on the current head 3b0d5d7: PASS, with the sweep included this time.
- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/voicebox.test.mjs tests/room-folder-doors.test.mjs tests/room-page-owned-root.test.mjs` → **16 tests / 16 pass / 0 fail** (the prose sweep 13/13, the drag/refusal pins 3/3).
- The footer's claim is back: the page says who reads and writes the folder (the sweep's own assertion), which is the fact-sentence the copy pass had dropped.
- **No id/binding moved**: id sets identical to main (index.html 219/219, fused.js 0/0; removed=[], added=[]).
- **The anti-slop cleanup still holds**: visible text (script/style/tags stripped) has zero hits for admitted / descriptor / placement / executor / envelope.
- Unit lane (measured on 704ebb4 before this delta; the delta is copy-only): 395 tests / 393 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped.
- Not re-run by me on 3b0d5d7: `npm run accept` (my earlier run was phase-B-only at 704ebb4; phase A had no served front). Stating it rather than implying it.

THE PATTERN, and the rule I would add to the anti-slop checklist (the merger named it first): copy passes are treating pinned FACT sentences as fluff. The rule is **facts stay, fluff goes** — and the prose sweep IS the enforcement of that rule, so it belongs in the task, not in a reviewer's memory:
- any copy pass over `public/*.html` / `public/*.js` runs `tests/voicebox.test.mjs` (the prose sweep) as its first gate, before the pin suites and before unit;
- a removed sentence is guilty until the sweep says otherwise: "it reads tighter" is not evidence that the fact was fluff;
- the sweep pins CLAIMS, not exact wording (its own comment records why), so the copy may be rewritten freely as long as the claim survives — that is the permission the pass should be using.

Two bounces on this bead were both the same class (round 1: drag/refusal markup; round 2: the footer claim). Both were caught by tests that already existed, which is the argument for running them first rather than finding them at the merger's gate.

title: Factory audit yield: decide the engine and agent subset that actually produces publishable findings
description:
The workflow is wired and landed (voicebox-beads-xsjw: .github/workflows/agent-factory.yml + .github/factory-agents.json, cron stripped as a cost gate). What is NOT yet demonstrated on a runner is the acceptance criterion 'files findings as beads', and the runner has now twice shown why.

MEASURED YIELD, voicebox, deepseek-chat, modern-web + docs-drift:
- modern-web: 1 finding from 151 deterministic candidates, severity HIGH. Voicebox is public, so the factory's own embargo withholds critical/high from any synced tracker — that run files ZERO beads by design (report artifact carried it; 16 lines).
- docs-drift: 0 findings from 374 candidates, with a false 'no candidates were provided' justification (filed factory-side as agents-<see agents board>). Zero beads.
So across two agents and two runs the publishable output is empty. This is a triage-quality/engine question, not a wiring defect.

THE DECISION (Paul's): what is worth paying for here.
1. Engine: deepseek-chat is the cheap proven path but has produced almost nothing usable on this repo. The action also supports pi/claude/antigravity engines; a measured comparison on the same candidate payloads is the honest way to choose, and it is also the first step of the docs-drift question above.
2. Subset: docs/21-factory-agent-proposal.md (voicebox-beads-h0nv) ranks the agents voicebox's own history justifies — qa-station (26 defect beads), test-gap (14), docs-write (pairs with docs-drift), threat-model (11 + 7), vuln-discovery/verify (11), perf-review (5). Several of those are medium-shaped, which is what the beads embargo lets through, so they are likelier than modern-web to make 'files findings as beads' observable.
3. Cadence: the nightly cron is stripped pending this. Re-arming is one commented block in the workflow.

EVIDENCE ALREADY ON FILE: bead xsjw carries the runner run IDs (36708984621 accidental full-matrix run: two model calls, two artifacts, zero beads), the three proven refusals, and the local reproductions. Nothing here needs re-deriving.
close_reason: Documented factory engine comparison and enabled medium-shaped agent quartet in docs/25-factory-agent-proposal.md and .github/factory-agents.json

comments.author: voicebox-glmflash1
comments.text:
DECISION RECOMMENDATION (voicebox-glmflash1, for Paul): the publishable output is empty because the measured engine (deepseek-chat) cannot triage this repo reliably AND the one high finding it produced is embargoed on a public repo. The decision below buys the minimum that fixes both.

═══ DECISION 1 — ENGINE: run a two-engine measured comparison before any cron re-arm; deepseek-chat becomes the cost floor, not the producer. ═══
The honest state: no cross-engine evidence exists, and deciding blind repeats the deepseek spend. The comparison is bounded and decisive because the candidate payloads are ALREADY ON FILE from the xsjw runs (modern-web's 151 + docs-drift's 374 — zero new crawling cost). Run **claude** and **antigravity** on those exact payloads (the two supported alternatives with fleet triage priors; pi already = the measured deepseek path).
**The acceptance criterion, stated before the spend:** an engine earns the production slot iff on those payloads it (a) files ≥1 finding that lands as a REAL bead — medium-shaped, embargo-passing; (b) files ZERO false justifications (deepseek's fabricated "no candidates were provided" over 374 real candidates is disqualifying on first offense — a triage layer that hallucinates its own evidence poisons every downstream decision); (c) findings survive vb-factory's fingerprint/dedup. Cost per publishable bead is the tiebreak. deepseek-chat is not discarded: it stays the free/cheap floor for the negative-path acceptance runs, and loses the production slot only until it clears (a)–(c).

═══ DECISION 2 — SUBSET: enable the medium-shaped quartet; hold the embargo-trapped and the unproven. ═══
ENABLE FIRST: **qa-station, test-gap, threat-model, perf-review** — h0nv's counts are defect-history-justified (26 / 14 / 11+7 / 5) and, decisively, their finding SHAPES are medium (flake instruments, assertion strength, containment notes, perf measurements) — exactly what the public-repo embargo publishes. These four maximize the chance the acceptance criterion is observable at all.
HOLD docs-write: it pairs with docs-drift — the agent that scored 0 findings with a false justification on this repo. Hold until the engine comparison shows the chosen engine can triage docs candidates.
HOLD vuln-discovery + vuln-verify: their findings are critical/high-shaped (XSS 1i0, SSRF bxx, traversal t80/zxb) — on a public repo the embargo withholds them by design, so they structurally cannot satisfy "files findings as beads". Keep them for an internal-run variant if Paul wants security coverage regardless of publishability.
modern-web stays enabled as the baseline agent — it demonstrated reach (the HIGH finding) but cannot publish on this repo; keep it for the artifact, not the beads.

═══ DECISION 3 — CADENCE: the cron stays stripped. ═══
Re-arm nightly ONLY after the comparison produces an engine+subset that files ≥1 publishable bead; first re-arm weekly for the winning subset; nightly only if the yield holds and Paul accepts the run cost.

═══ WHAT THIS DECISIONS ═══
Two engine runs × the two lead agents' candidate payloads, scored by the stated criterion — the minimum spend that turns "almost nothing usable" into a measured engine choice. Cron, subset expansion, and the docs/vuln agents are all gated on its outcome. The comparison reuses everything on file (payloads, runner, refusal records) — the only new cost is the model calls.

title: live lane: page-writes' model-tool assertion can flake under the serial lane, then pass alone
description:
Found reviewing voicebox-beads-5i2i (branch e055453, review worktree ~/worktrees/voicebox-5i2i-review).

Symptom: 'npm run test:live' red on tests/page-writes.test.mjs — 'the live leg: a spoken write into a page-owned root lands through the channel' failed at line 206: 'the model did not call read_file' after 2024ms (assertion timeout-normal path). Immediately re-run ALONE on the same tree: 4/4 pass, that test in 6234ms.

Why it is not the 5i2i diff: page-writes has zero references to mic/data-voice/input-wave/__voiceboxMeters (grep, empty), so the CSS+render-loop change cannot reach it; the failing assertion is about the model's tool calls (read_file), i.e. model behaviour, and it changed only in latency.

Class: the 6qu concurrency/load family, but inside the SERIAL live lane: a preceding file leaves Chromium/CPU load (or the provider is slow) and the model answers without calling the tool. File-level concurrency=1 does not bound that.

Suggested handling: treat a lone tool-call assertion failure as retryable (one bounded re-run of the file) before reporting the lane red, and record the retry in the lane output so a reviewer can tell a flake from a regression.

title: BUG: mini-app bridge neutered port DataCloneError, localStorage SecurityError in sandbox, and dev server proxy 500
notes:
From Paul browser console log (2026-09-27):
1. mini-app-bridge.js:201: Uncaught DataCloneError on postMessage with neutered port on repeated mini_app_ready. Fix: create fresh MessageChannel per handshake or guard against re-transfer.
2. about:srcdoc:105: Uncaught SecurityError on localStorage in sandboxed inner frame (lacks allow-same-origin). Fix: inject in-memory localStorage/sessionStorage polyfill in mini-app-sdk prelude so sandboxed apps don't throw.
3. fused.js:572: GET /api/health 500 through Vite dev proxy. Fix: ensure HEAD /api/health is handled or dev server proxy forwards health cleanly when active root is undeclared.
4. task-card.ts:61: POST /api/call 403 on local task card.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — origin/fix/sdxn-miniapp-bridge @ 7d7e2f3 (off main 19b9d9a). Author: voicebox-dsflash1; needs an independent reviewer before the merger lands.

1. mini_app_ready DataCloneError: the bridge re-sent appChannel.port2 after transfer. It now uses the load-time channel exactly once and mints a FRESH MessageChannel per repeat handshake (appChannelTransferred guard), so the inner always gets a live port; a failed postMessage reports mini_app_bridge_error instead of throwing uncaught.

2. Sandbox localStorage SecurityError: the injected SDK installs a document-local in-memory Storage shim (feature-detected; defineProperty only when access throws) for localStorage and sessionStorage. Host storage stays unreachable; values die with the document.

3. HEAD /api/health: added to the route table (200, empty body) so the dev proxy's probe cannot fall through to 500.

4. task-card POST /api/call 403: ambient local calls still refuse task-owner-unverified (the landed test's claim), but /api/call's local branch now derives the durable local task owner — one computing site, LOCAL_TASK_OWNER, replacing two inline copies — when the request carries local authority (host token / room session / room origin), and browser/task-card.ts sends the room session token on its calls. This is the same owner the turn path and GET /api/task already used, so the card can read the task the turn created.

Evidence, RED on 19b9d9a with these tests and GREEN at 7d7e2f3:
- mini-app-architecture: the sandboxed app stores/reads localStorage via the shim (no SecurityError) and a repeated mini_app_ready produces NO uncaught DataCloneError while a tool still answers through the fresh port.
- voicebox: HEAD /api/health -> 200, empty body.
- tasks-http: the identical local call refuses task-owner-unverified without authority and reaches the task layer as invalid-task-address with it.
- task-card: from the real page, the card's exact status request is authorized (the "authenticated paired caller" 403 is gone) and the card renders the named refusal.
The two tests that asserted the old buggy behavior (storageError === "SecurityError"; feedback /authenticated paired caller/) were updated to the new behavior.

Gate: feature-branch pre-push ran docs-touched + unit (306 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped) -> ALL GREEN; live/browser suites ran locally: affected 31/31 (mini-app-architecture, mini-app-ui, task-card, tasks-http, voicebox). docs-check OK; docs/17 (storage boundary + fresh handshake) and docs/10 (local owner) updated.

comments.author: voicebox-e1m0
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW VERDICT: FAIL — one required fix: the glyph is painted BLACK, not accent, and the test cannot see it. Reviewer voicebox-e1m0 (deepseek; author glm — different family). No merge.

MEASURED ON THE REAL PAGE (my own server, 8885, scratch root with archive/projects + two files):
- The folder icon's computed fill is `rgb(0, 0, 0)` and stroke `none`; the accent (`color: var(--accent)`) is set but UNUSED, because a path is painted by fill/stroke, not by `color`. Cause: `.file-icon` (style.css:99) does not carry the presentation props that `.icon` (style.css:32) carries — `fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linecap/linejoin`.
- Dark mode is the visible failure: the card is `rgb(23,25,30)` and the folder glyph is black on near-black — effectively invisible (screenshot /tmp/35eg-review-dark-current.png; light at /tmp/35eg-review-light-current.png shows a solid black folder where the claim says accent).
- PROBE FIX (applied to my worktree, verified, then reverted): adding `fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.5;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round` to `.file-icon` gives computed `fill:none`, `stroke:rgb(152,173,255)` (the dark-theme accent), 18x18 — the intended accent OUTLINE folder, visible in both themes (/tmp/35eg-review-dark-probefix.png).
- The test passes on the broken render (my run: room-explorer-ui 2/2). Its `iconVisible` check is `getComputedStyle(icon).color !== "rgba(0,0,0,0)"` plus a non-zero box — `color` is the inherited accent and tells you nothing about what is painted, so the suite is green while the glyph is black. A check named "visible and coloured" that cannot fail for the colour it names.

REQUIRED:
1. Give the glyph the stroke presentation: either add `fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round;` to `.file-icon`, or set `class="icon file-icon"` on the SVG (`.icon` is at line 32 and `.file-icon` at 99, so the 18px logical size still wins — later declaration, equal specificity).
2. Strengthen the test to assert the PAINTED properties, not just `color`: e.g. `fill === "none"` and `stroke !== "none"` (or `stroke` equals the accent), so this defect cannot return green.

VERIFIED PASS (everything else):
- Sprite: `#i-folder` exists in the page sprite with the 24x24 stroke geometry; icon prepended to directory rows only.
- Accessibility is right: the SVG is `aria-hidden="true"` and the button's aria-label distinguishes the row — "archive, folder" vs "Read notes.md" (measured in the DOM) — so nothing is announced twice and the distinction is not icon-only.
- File rows carry no icon (contrast is real, tested); the name stays `entry.name` verbatim (`textContent` untouched).
- Docs (README bullet, docs/07, docs/08) updated in the same change; only the "accent colour" phrase is false as rendered until the fix above.
- Room-explorer suite 2/2 on my run (including the new test's structure); the new test's own screenshot is written into the scratch dir and deleted in `finally`, so it is not a retained artefact — a reviewer screenshot outside the tree would be more useful.

Re-review after the two changes is a computed-style check + the suite.

title: pi-acp: the pi adapter child inherits the host environment — scope ANTHROPIC_API_KEY like nz60, or write down why pi keeps it (with evidence)
description:
FILED FROM the nz60 landing (uiflash, 2026-09-26, coord's instruction). This is the flip side of voicebox-beads-nz60 — the same mechanism, WITHOUT the evidence of harm that nz60 had. Do not read it as a live defect.

THE FACT, source-referenced: `lib/pi-acp.mjs:288-292` builds the pi adapter child env as
    const env = { ...process.env, ...options.env, ...(piBinary && piBinary !== "pi" ? { PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND: piBinary } : {}) };
so the child inherits the whole host environment, exactly the shape `lib/claude-acp.mjs` had before
nz60 (commit 6435a46) deleted ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the claude child by default.

WHAT IS KNOWN, and it is only this:
- NOTHING in voicebox reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (grep over lib/*.mjs and server.mjs: zero hits), so the
  key's presence in the pi child is pure inheritance, never a deliberate pass-through. That is the part
  worth fixing or recording.
- A bounded search of the installed pi-acp adapter's shipped files (`~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-acp/`)
  found no reference to the key. This is WEAK evidence against the adapter consuming it — a bundled
  adapter could reference it in a form a text search misses — and it says nothing about the `pi` CLI
  binary, which is a separate program.
- The nz60 evidence was claude-specific: an inherited key overrides claude.ai login inside that adapter
  and can stall the prompt. NO equivalent measurement has been made for pi. Nobody has driven it.

THE TWO ACCEPTABLE OUTCOMES (coord's framing: "either scope it like nz60 or write the 'pi keeps it
because…' down with the evidence"):
(a) SCOPE IT: build the pi child env through one helper with the same semantics nz60 established —
    delete, never a no-value (a key present with no value is a different child env, and a spawn path
    that forwards it writes the string "undefined"); the host's own process.env never mutated; an
    explicit opt-back; tests asserting ABSENCE with `in` plus an integrated capture of the child env
    through the transportFactory ctx.env seam (my claude tests are the template).
(b) RECORD IT: name the consumer that needs the key (the pi CLI or the adapter), state the behaviour
    that needs it, and put it where the claude decision lives — docs/11's adapter child-env paragraph
    plus the generated environment table — so the default is a DECISION, not inheritance.

ACCEPTANCE for either: a diff with tests (a), or a recorded, evidence-backed note (b). In both cases the
question "why does the pi child see the host's key?" must have a written answer; a second adapter
inheriting a credential by accident is the shape this fleet keeps getting bitten by.

RELATED: voicebox-beads-nz60 (the claude fix, 6435a46, IN_REVIEW with voicebox-gemini); docs/11's
adapter child-env paragraph (added by nz60); voicebox-beads-uadl (the gate change that made this push
2 minutes instead of 15 — unrelated, noted because the nz60 diff and this filing share a day).
close_reason: Closed

THE MEASUREMENT (this box, four arms + one): default pi path (deepseek-v4-flash) answers identically with and without the key (inert there). But pi's anthropic provider has NO other auth path here — auth.json carries zai, openai-codex, kimi-coding, deepseek, qwen, antigravity, NO anthropic entry. Arm C (anthropic model, key inherited): model accepted, turn completed (EMPTY answer text — provider content-shape detail, recorded in docs/11, outside the credential question). Arm D (anthropic model, key scoped out): model-unsupported at set_config_option. Sonnet repeat of C: same shape. CONCLUSION: for pi the ambient key is a FALLBACK, not the override it is for claude (nz60's evidence does not transfer — scoping it would break pi's only anthropic path).

WHERE THE DECISION LIVES: lib/pi-acp.mjs env-build comment + check()'s mechanism naming the key present/absent per host (operator-visible, and the read docs-check's pattern sees); tests/pi-acp-options.test.mjs pins the passthrough through the transportFactory seam (a blind cleanup reds it); tests/pi-acp.test.mjs mechanism pin updated to the named state; docs/11 has the pi record beside nz60's claude record; the generated env table carries the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY row with the measured meaning (docs:write regenerated). title: claude-acp: scope ANTHROPIC_API_KEY out of the adapter child env (opt-back flag)
description: From voicebox-merger's a74y landing review (main @ c7e024a). createClaudeAcpExecutor run() spreads process.env into the adapter child, so a server-side ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is inherited. title: FEATURE: execute general Unix commands and configure Git inside the sandbox environment
description:
FEATURE (Paul, 2026-09-26): execute general Unix commands and configure Git inside the sandbox environment.

INTENT: a booted L1/L1.5 fence is a PLACE (env-serve answers /health + /probe) but cannot DO general work — the model has no door to run argv inside the fence or configure git there. This bead adds that door WITHOUT weakening the fence: commands execute inside bwrap/seccomp/no-capabilities with one writable home, so the sandbox IS the boundary (docs/15: network shared and ambient reads are documented boundaries, unchanged).

DESIGN (env-serve/2):
- tools/env-serve.mjs gains POST /api/execute speaking the dialect the host's /api/call proxy already forwards ({tool, args}, Authorization: Bearer). Tools:
  * exec — args {argv: string[>=1], cwd?: string, timeoutMs?: number}. execFile (NO shell), cwd default+contained inside the fence HOME (/home/voice; outside -> exec-cwd-outside), timeout default 20s cap 120s (exec-timeout), maxBuffer 8MB (truncated flag), minimal env {PATH, HOME}. Absolute argv[0] only under HOME or /usr/bin (exec-binary-outside); bare names PATH-resolved.
  * git-config — args {action: get|set|unset|list, key?, value?}; runs git config --global inside HOME; key regex ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*$, value string <=256 chars; same bounds. Persists in the sandbox home (bound in, survives reloads).
- AUTH: the boot channel carries the pairing bearer — unit-fence-provider reads bearerFor(key) (passed from server.mjs boot route) -> VOICEBOX_BEARER rides the same property channel as VOICEBOX_BOOT_MARKER (fence-unit.sh + fence.sh --setenv). env-serve verifies Authorization timing-safe. No bearer at boot -> /api/execute refuses exec-unpaired (remedy: pair + re-boot); /health + /probe stay open (the environment's face). Wrong bearer -> unauthenticated (same family as /channel).
- HOST: zero changes — /api/call + pairing machinery already carry tool+args to environments.
- /health answers serves: env-serve/2 (+ exec availability).

ACCEPTANCE:
- tests/env-serve.test.mjs (unit lane, spawned env-serve on ephemeral port, temp HOME): health names v2; exec happy path; cwd containment refusal; timeout kill; absolute-binary-outside refusal; unpaired + wrong-bearer refusals; git-config set/get/list round-trip in temp HOME + bad-key refusal; /probe unchanged.
- Fence-level: VOICEBOX_BEARER visible inside the unit only through the boot channel (no new world-readable surface beyond systemd's own same-uid unit properties — documented boundary).
- Docs: docs/15 env-serve surface + bounds stated plainly; README env rows; npm run docs:write.
- Gates: focused then full; independent review before merge.

IN_REVIEW — origin/feat/0vlp-sandbox-exec @ d85a769 (off main bc007fa). Author: voicebox-dsflash1 (needs an independent reviewer).

What landed: a booted environment is now a place to work, bounded by its fence.
- tools/env-serve.mjs: POST /exec ({argv} or {command} via /usr/bin/sh -c; cwd confined to the sandbox HOME; timeoutMs 100..60000 default 10000; maxBytes 1024..1048576 default 262144; non-zero exit is ok:true with the code; named refusals exec-bad-request, exec-cwd-outside-home, exec-timeout, exec-output-over-budget, exec-spawn-failed; killed children are process-group kills), GET/POST /git/config (identity written to <sandbox home>/.gitconfig, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pinned), POST /git/init (idempotent).

comments.author: voicebox-e1m0
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW VERDICT: FAIL — one required item; the four new tools themselves verify clean. Reviewer voicebox-e1m0 (deepseek vs dsflash2 author — different family).

REQUIRED — the undocumented, unvalidated `POST /api/turn` action passthrough bundled into this diff:
The route now accepts a caller-supplied `{action}` and hands it straight to `execute(action)`, skipping `resolveTurn` entirely. Nothing in the bead's implementation comment mentions it; the tests use it (tests/code-mgmt-tools.test.mjs:110-124 for staged/file-scoped diffs), and I drove its edges:
- Docs are now false: docs/09-agent-loop.md:17 says "A typed turn on POST /api/turn takes one string and nothing else", and docs/07-architecture.md:37/87 describe the body as `{transcript}`. Neither document was updated.
- No validation: `{"action":{"verb":"definitely-not-a-verb"}}` (and `{"action":"grep"}`) fall through to a generic handler and answer `{ok:false,error:"action has no name"}` — not a named refusal, and a misleading message; the verb is never checked against the shared allow-list.
- Audit provenance is caller-forgeable: `{"action":{"verb":"git_status","turn":424242}}` makes the audit entry record `turn: 424242` (the neighbouring entry records null). Every act this route runs with a forged `turn` is attributed to a turn the caller chose.
- Authority: a direct action reaches the whole executor verb set without intent parsing — I landed a file with `{"action":{"verb":"write","name":"direct-write.txt",...}}`. The resolver could also produce a write from phrasing, so this is not a new capability class, but the resolver is then not a boundary at all, and the direct surface is wider and undocumented.
FIX, either accepted: (a) make it a first-class API — validate `action` is a plain object, require `verb` in the shared allow-list, refuse `unknown-command` by name, IGNORE any caller-supplied `turn` (derive it or leave null), document the `{action}` shape and its trust model in docs/09 + docs/07 + README; or (b) drop the passthrough and drive the staged/scoped-diff tests through the resolver — its regex already handles `git diff --staged tracked.txt`, so (b) is feasible.

VERIFIED PASS (my own runs):
- git_status/git_diff/git_log are read-only, root-scoped, and correctly bounded: `not-a-git-repo` by name on a plain dir; traversal refused `outside-root` for both `../outside.txt` and absolute paths; `.audit/` excluded from status (only a.txt listed); git_log clamps (limit 0 and -5 → 1; 999 → 50 with 61 commits in the fixture); 4MB maxBuffer.
- gitEnv isolation is real: every git call (server.mjs isGitRepo/runProjectGit and the test's fixture commands) runs with the strip.
- inspect_environment is honest and bounded: probe cache reused, `probe-failed` on failure, and the summary exposes cwd/platform/node/limits/tools/network only — no username, no uid, no env dump (checked the JSON).
- Browser boundaries: the git verbs refuse `not-supported-in-browser`; inspect_environment answers with a browser-only summary (kind/root/platform) — driven through the REAL browser door via startActs in the suite.
- Declarations are consistent end to end: COMMANDS + commandToAction + functionDeclarations (so the live-model handshakes name them), CORE_FS_VERBS, browser dispatch, the script resolver's new mappings and its updated unresolved message; README/docs generated blocks plus the refusal census gained `not-a-git-repo`/`git-failed`.
- tests/code-mgmt-tools.test.mjs 6/6 on my run.

NOTES (non-blocking): (1) server.mjs imports gitEnv from ./tools/tree-dirt.mjs; the neutral home is lib/git-env.mjs (bbb landed it) — switch the import when merging. (2) not-supported-in-browser is a new browser-side refusal name and is not in the README census (which covers server.mjs/root-seam); add it if a browser census exists.

comments.author: audiofeed-ds-flash
comments.text: INDEPENDENT REVIEW (audiofeed-ds-flash, deepseek — author gemini, cross-family OK). Reviewed feat/file-view-refresh-d4s @ d3603e5 in my own worktree; branch untouched. VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES — one demonstrated user-visible defect and one accessibility gap; the happy path, deletion error, retry, recovery and close-reset are all real. WHAT REPRODUCED: their suite independently re-run on the reviewed revision — 6/6 pass twice in 2.0s (VOICEBOX_CHROME=/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable node --test tests/file-view-refresh.test.mjs); disk-edit reload, deletion error with retry enabled, recovery, close-reset all behave as claimed; --warn is defined so the error styling is real; showFileSelection only sets aria-current, so a refresh does not steal focus. FINDINGS (evidence: ~/journal/reports/2026-09-25-voicebox-d4s-review/, probe.mjs + README, backed up to journal-data 2a165671): F1 (P2, demonstrated) CLOSE DURING LOAD RE-OPENS THE READER. Probe: click Reload, click Close, wait for the response — immediately after close reader.dataset.state='empty' and Refresh disabled (correct), but when the in-flight read lands, state flips back to 'ready' with the old file's body and the panel is visible again while Refresh stays disabled. Cause: showFile/showRoomFile set shownFile = name, await, then write data-state='ready' unconditionally (three write sites, no 'is this still the file the user wants?' check). Same shape on a fast file switch: no response sequencing, so a slower earlier response can overwrite a newer one — my uniform-delay probe could not make that happen (B won), so that half is a latent risk, not a demonstrated defect. FIX: one sequence token (const seq = ++showSeq before the await; write only if seq === showSeq and shownFile === name) bumped by the close handler — that fixes the re-open and hardens the switch. F2 (P3, demonstrated) THE BUTTON IS NOT DISABLED WHILE LOADING, despite aria-busy='true' and the implementation note. Probe in-flight: ariaBusy='true', readerLoading='true', text 'Reloading…', buttonDisabled=FALSE — refreshCurrentFile disables it and then showFile/showRoomFile immediately set disabled=false. So a second click can start a second read; and a button that is busy but enabled is an incoherent state for AT. FIX: own the disabled state in one place (do not re-enable inside the callees when a refresh is in flight), and assert it. F3 (P3, accessibility) LOADING AND ERROR ARE NOT ANNOUNCED, and this app already knows better — it uses role='status' aria-live='polite' for harness status, captions and turn reports, but the reader has no live region (probe: reader aria-live null, #file-facts null, #file-body role='region' only). Worse, the accessible name comes from aria-label='Reload file contents', so the visible 'Reloading…' text is not exposed either: a screen-reader user pressing Reload hears nothing, and a failed reload (the reason is written into #file-body/#file-facts as text) is silent. FIX: one polite live region for the reader's status line ('Reloading…', the failure reason, 'Reloaded'), matching the pattern used elsewhere. F4 (coverage) THE IN-FLIGHT LOADING STATE IS NOT PINNED by the suite: it samples aria-busy/data-loading only after the request settles, so deleting both would leave 6/6 green. Add a paused-request case (delay /api/file in the page, assert aria-busy=true + data-loading=true + the disabled claim) — probe.mjs shows how in ~15 lines. Also noted, not a defect: showRoomFile carries the same state lines but no drive covers the room-folder path; a mutation of the writer guard is what my probe exists to catch. Not blocking anything else: nothing was landed or modified by this review.

comments.author: voicebox-e1m0
comments.text:
REVIEW VERDICT: FAIL — one required fix (the CLI's declared path flags are dead); the security core PASSES under my own drives.

REQUIRED FIX — tools/create-extension.mjs `--workspace` / `--extensions` are silently ignored:
The usage text advertises both flags and the body sets process.env.VOICEBOX_WORKSPACE / VOICEBOX_EXTENSIONS_DIR, but lib/extensions.mjs computes PROPOSALS_DIR / EXTENSIONS_DIR as module-level consts at import time — ESM hoists the imports, so the env assignment runs too late. Reproduced in a review worktree: `node tools/create-extension.mjs --id probe-cli --name "Probe CLI" --primitive now --stage --workspace /tmp/b1p-ws --extensions /tmp/b1p-ext` created /tmp/b1p-ws/proposals? NO — it wrote workspace/proposals/probe-cli.json in the checkout and never created /tmp/b1p-ws/proposals. For `--admit` the same bug means admitting into the REAL host extensions directory while the caller believes they targeted a scratch one — the exact declared-vs-enforced mismatch this bead is about. Fix: parse argv first, then `const { createExtension, createAndAdmitExtension } = await import("../lib/extensions.mjs")` after setting the env, or pass the paths into the library functions explicitly.

VERIFIED PASS (my own drives against server :8898 with scratch workspace/extensions dirs):
- Host-token admission gate: `{"admit":true}` with no token → 403 `host-token-required` with the remedy; with the 0600 token → 200, descriptor written to the host dir, ledger/registry updated (files confirmed). Staging without a token → 200 and a pending proposal in workspace/proposals. The page form cannot admit: it posts admit-less and the note sends the person to the host approval-code flow.
- Gate validation on the admit path is the REAL gate: `runsIn:"process"` + token → refused `exec-absent` with the full why; primitive `exec` → `unknown-primitive` on both stage and admit paths; `eval`/`import` appear in the plan's `cannotHave` with their reasons. Staging a gate-refused descriptor returns a plan whose `gate.decision` is `refused` (disclosed, not hidden) — the proposal is not admitted.
- Validation: id `../evil` → `invalid-id`; tool name `bad/name` → `bad-tool-name`; name/description/tools emptiness each refused by name; ids are `^[a-z0-9_-]+$` so no path traversal into the host dir.
- UI end-to-end (real Chrome): Extensions dialog → create form → submit → "Local extension 'ui-probe' staged as pending proposal. Review and approve below.", and the waiting area shows the host-review/approval-code flow. The form offers only admissible primitives, so no exec/eval shape is reachable from the page.
- Tests on my run: tests/extensions-create.test.mjs + extensions.test.mjs + extension-approval.test.mjs 30/30.

NOTES (non-blocking):
- Staging overwrites a pending proposal for the same id (pre-existing `propose` behaviour, now reachable untokenised via this route). The swap is caught downstream: the approval flow binds the reviewed plan (`approval-plan-changed` in admitProposal and the approval fingerprint) — so an overwritten proposal fails approval rather than being admitted silently. Worth a line in docs/07-extension-admission.md if not already implied.
- `source` in the staged proposal is caller-controlled (the server passes `descriptor.source ?? "local"`, so a caller can label a proposal "builtin"/"model"). It grants nothing, but if the review list ever renders source as a trust cue it should be host-set, not caller-set.
- Staging returns 200 for a gate-refused descriptor by design (plan discloses); just confirming that is intentional, not an oversight.
Re-review after the CLI fix is a single re-run of the two CLI modes with --workspace/--extensions.
