3. DELEGATION: the only program-execution path is a delegated harness's OWN tools (e.g. pi's bash) under the harness's grants — not this environment's probed inventory. And on this machine right now pi delegation is REFUSED (adapter-version-unsupported), so even that path is closed here.

SEVERITY NOTE: the rendered list includes sudo, su, mount, iptables — the current framing doesn't just overpromise capability, it misstates the safety posture.

RECOMMENDATION — direction A (make the UI say only the truth), not B (add an exec verb): B is a large new security surface (arbitrary program execution as the server user), contradicts the executor's fail-closed design, and duplicates the delegation path. A is surgical: in fused.js renderEnvironments, rename the claim to what it is — e.g. summary 'N host programs present (probed <when>; not invocable by voicebox tasks)' with the expanded list headed by one line naming what the environment CAN do (read/write/list/grep/edit/diff/delete, plus delegation to a harness with its own tools). The probe itself stays — it answers 'what does this host have' for the operator; the defect is only the word 'tools' framing presence as capability. Add one driven test asserting the honest copy renders. Small diff: fused.js + one test + docs line.

Awaiting direction confirmation before implementing.

title: Investigate issues with mini-app rendering within the isolated iframe environment
description: From Paul (2026-09-25): investigate issues with mini-app rendering within the isolated iframe environment. Drive the real behaviour in a browser and report what breaks and why before fixing.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION FINDINGS (voicebox-beads-wtz, P1):

Issue: Mini-app rendering completely fails inside the iframe environment; inner app never renders.

Root cause analysis driven live in headless Chromium over CDP:
1. Erroneous Outer Frame Sandboxing (public/fused.js:2799):
   outer.setAttribute('sandbox', 'allow-scripts') was mistakenly placed on the OUTER mediator iframe.
   Per docs/17-mini-apps-architecture.md and tests/mini-app-architecture.test.mjs, the outer bridge (/mini-app-bridge.html) is designed to be SAME-ORIGIN with the room to mediate communication, while the INNER frame (#inner-app in mini-app-bridge.html) possesses sandbox='allow-scripts' to isolate untrusted app markup.
2. CORS Error on Module Script:
   Because the outer frame is sandboxed without allow-same-origin, its origin is opaque ('null'). In public/mini-app-bridge.html, <script type='module' src='mini-app-bridge.js'> is fetched via CORS. Chromium blocks this with:
   'Access to script at http://127.0.0.1:.../mini-app-bridge.js from origin null has been blocked by CORS policy: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present on the requested resource (net::ERR_FAILED)'.
   mini-app-bridge.js never loads or executes.
3. Broken PostMessage Handshake:
   Because mini-app-bridge.js never runs, bridge_ready/mini_app_handshake never fire. Furthermore, postToHost calls window.parent.postMessage(msg, window.location.origin) where origin is 'null' (refused by parent window), and fused.js:2816 checks e.origin !== window.location.origin.
4. Consequence:
   inner.srcdoc remains null, inlined SDK is never injected, and the mini-app viewport remains completely blank.
5. Test Blindspot:
   tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs passed because it only asserted #mini-app-container was unhidden, outer sandbox attribute was present, and button clicks occurred — it never asserted that the inner frame populated or rendered.

Proposed fix:
- In public/fused.js, remove outer.setAttribute('sandbox', 'allow-scripts') (keeping outer bridge same-origin per doc 17; inner iframe remains strictly sandbox='allow-scripts').
- Update tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs to assert inner.srcdoc is populated and app DOM renders.

Awaiting confirmation from coord before applying fix.

title: PROBE: sandbox-probe's marker can be left in the measured tree when the probe is killed inside its write window
description:
Found by bp8's new before/after delta (2026-09-25, voicebox-e1m0), in ~/worktrees/voicebox-bp8: after a live-lane run, `git status --porcelain` showed `?? .sandbox-probe-1337006-20260925174601152` — a 0-byte marker in the tree.

THE WRITER: tools/sandbox-probe.mjs writeProbe() probes a directory by creating `.sandbox-probe-<pid>-<ISO-when>` and unlinking it. Line ~155 probes `process.cwd()`, and server.mjs runs the probe for GET /api/probe with the server's cwd — which is the served/measured tree for every harness and live-test server.

WHY IT SURVIVED: the create→unlink window is two syscalls, and nothing covers a SIGKILL in between (a `finally` cannot run on SIGKILL — and the harness kills its private server at exit, live tests kill theirs). A normal foreground run cleans up (verified in /tmp/bp8-probe-repro: no leftover), so this is a kill-race, not a missing unlink. The marker's name carries the PID, which is what makes a sweep possible.

WHY IT IS bp8's CLASS: the artefact lands in the tree another process measures — the harness's delta check fails on it, and the next person reads "?? .sandbox-probe-…" as unexplained dirt (exactly the 2026-09-20 Dolt-backup symptom).

OPTIONS (pick at implementation):
1. Startup sweep: on probe start (or server start), remove `.sandbox-probe-<pid>-*` for PIDs no longer alive (kill -0). Owner-named artefacts, owner-verified cleanup.
2. Probe a path the process owns: probe cwd writability via a uniquely-named DIRECTORY under cwd, removed the same way — narrows nothing; still dirt on kill.
3. Measurement exclusion: `.sandbox-probe-*` filtered like `.beads/` in tools/tree-dirt.mjs — explicitly weakens the measurement, so only if 1 proves impossible.

NOT IN bp8's diff: bp8 is pushed and under review; this is recorded separately rather than expanding a reviewed change.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
# Modern Web Guidance Pass: Voicebox Page Architecture & Construction **Bead**: `voicebox-beads-8ht` (Task, P2) **Scope**: Read-only analysis across `public/index.html`, `public/environment.html`, `public/style.css`, `public/fused.js`, `public/live-voice.js`, `browser/ui/ui.ts`. **Grounding**: Analyzed against `modern-web-guidance` standards (Baseline status, Baseline Widely/Newly available, platform primitives) and repository-specific constraints (CSP, CDP acceptance harness, plain-language gate, served-front currency check). --- ## Executive Summary Voicebox has already adopted several modern platform primitives (`` with `::backdrop` and frosted glass, `:has()` relational selectors, dynamic viewport units `dvh`/`svh`, `text-wrap: pretty`, `color-mix()`, and `documentPictureInPicture`). However, several architectural areas either **hand-roll behaviors now provided by the platform** or **miss modern platform features**, occasionally introducing subtle bugs or fragility. Crucially, adopting platform features in Voicebox is not a free aesthetic upgrade: every feature carries specific costs and risks against Voicebox's **strict CSP**, **acceptance test timing**, **audio worklet rAF loops**, and **multi-browser support**. --- ## 1. Dialogs, Popovers & Invoker Commands ### 1.1 Declarative Invocation vs Imperative JS Listeners * **Location**: `public/index.html:43-85, 158-165`; `public/fused.js:1432-1478` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: Buttons (`#settings-open`, `#envs-open`, `#exts-open`) and close buttons (`#settings-close`, `#envs-close`, `#exts-close`) manually manage dialog lifecycle in JavaScript: - `on(els.settingsOpen, "click", () => els.settings.showModal())` - Manual `setAttribute("aria-expanded", "true"/"false")` on triggers (`fused.js:1437, 1445, 1476`) - Manual focus restoration to trigger on close (`fused.js:1446, 1477`) * **Platform equivalent**: **Invoker Commands API** (`commandfor` and `command` attributes on ` ``` The browser natively opens `` as a modal, traps focus, links accessibility states, and restores focus on dismissal without custom JS. * **What it would break / Real Costs**: 1. *Browser Support*: Invoker Commands are Baseline Newly Available (Chrome 135+, Safari 26.2, Firefox 144). Polyfilling requires an external script. 2. *CSP Violation*: Voicebox's strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`) strictly prohibits external CDNs (like `https://esm.run/invokers-polyfill`). Any polyfill would have to be vendored. 3. *Side-Effect Decoupling*: Clicking `#settings-open`, `#envs-open`, and `#exts-open` currently performs critical setup before display: `refreshDevices()`, `loadAgentSettings()`, `renderEnvironments()`, and `renderExtensions()`. Replacing `click` handlers with purely declarative commands would cause dialogs to open before data is fetched, showing empty or stale lists unless listeners are refactored to listen for `'command'` or dialog `'toggle'` events. ### 1.2 Inconsistent Light-Dismiss Fallbacks on Safari * **Location**: `public/index.html:50, 70, 158`; `public/fused.js:1449-1458, 1481-1490`; `browser/ui/ui.ts:214-225` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: The dialogs use the cutting-edge `closedby="any"` attribute for declarative light-dismiss (clicking the backdrop). Because Safari does not yet support `closedby`, `fused.js` implements a geometry-checking click fallback (`event.target === dialog && rect checking`). **The Bug/Gap**: The fallback was added for `#envs` (`fused.js:1449`) and `#settings` (`fused.js:1481`), and for `#confirm` in `browser/ui/ui.ts:214`, but **omitted for `#exts`** (`fused.js:1432`). On Safari, clicking outside the Extensions dialog fails to dismiss it. * **Platform equivalent**: A single shared light-dismiss helper or a global dialog light-dismiss event delegate. * **What it would break / Real Costs**: No breakage. This is a pure bug fix for Safari consistency that eliminates duplicate geometry-check boilerplate. ### 1.3 Top-Layer Entry/Exit Transitions * **Location**: `public/style.css:136-168, 214-239` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: `` and `` toggle abruptly between `display: none` and `display: block`. * **Platform equivalent**: Modern top-layer CSS animation using `@starting-style`, `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, and the `overlay` property: ```css dialog[open] { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); @starting-style { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.96); } } dialog { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.96); transition: opacity 0.2s ease-out, transform 0.2s ease-out, display 0.2s allow-discrete, overlay 0.2s allow-discrete; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: 1. *Harness Timing / Flake Hazard*: `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` and `tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs` use CDP to click the backdrop or Esc and immediately assert `!document.querySelector('dialog[open]')`. If an exit transition keeps the dialog in the top layer (`overlay` transition) during the exit duration, immediate assertions fail unless test scripts add explicit transition waits. 2. *Browser Support*: `overlay` transition property is currently limited (Chrome 117+, unsupported in Firefox/Safari). --- ## 2. Popovers & Anchor Positioning vs Title Tooltips ### 2.1 Inaccessible `title=""` Attributes for State Explanations * **Location**: `public/fused.js:397, 560, 571, 833, 1042`; `public/environment.html:106` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: Voicebox stores full descriptions and status details in `title` attributes (e.g. `els.rootKind.title = activeRoot.description`, `els.readerFacts.title = ...`). The author in `fused.js:555` states: *"The server's full description stays in the chip's title for anyone who asks for it, because a tooltip is not a second voice on the screen"*. * **Modern Web Guidance violation**: `modern-web-guidance: html: 5`: *"DON'T use the title attribute to create tooltip effects."* `title` attributes are completely inaccessible on touch devices/phones (no hover), unstyled, ignored by screen readers, and inaccessible to keyboard tab navigation. * **Platform equivalent**: **Popover API** (`popover="auto"` or `popover="hint"`) paired with **CSS Anchor Positioning**: ```html ...
...
``` ```css #root-kind { anchor-name: --root-chip; } #root-desc { position-anchor: --root-chip; position-area: block-end; position-try-fallbacks: flip-block; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: 1. *Browser Support*: CSS Anchor Positioning (`position-area`, `position-try-fallbacks`) is supported in Chrome (125+) and Safari (TP/27), but **unsupported in Firefox**. A fallback positioning strategy (`top`/`left` calculation or centered popover) is mandatory. 2. *Plain-Language Gate*: `tools/page-acceptance.mjs:254-300` scans all string literals and HTML elements in `public/` for internal jargon (e.g. `reachableFromThisProcess`, `executor`, ticket IDs). Expanding hidden `title` strings into rendered Popover DOM nodes increases the surface area checked by the plain-language gate. --- ## 3. Container Queries vs Viewport Media Queries ### 3.1 Media Query Inside a Fixed-Width Modal Dialog * **Location**: `public/style.css:189-201` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: Inside `dialog.envs` (which has `width: min(100% - 2rem, 460px)`), `.env-add` attempts responsive form layout using `@media (max-width: 480px) { .env-add { flex-direction: column; } }`. On a 1200px desktop screen, the dialog is only 460px wide, but the viewport query evaluates `false`. Furthermore, lines 198-201 accidentally re-declare `.env-add` with `padding: 8px 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line);` without `flex-wrap: wrap`, overriding and colliding with lines 189-195 in the cascade! * **Platform equivalent**: **CSS Container Queries** (`container-type: inline-size`): ```css dialog.envs, .envs-form { container: env-dialog / inline-size; } @container env-dialog (inline-size < 380px) { .env-add { flex-direction: column; } .env-add input, .env-add button { width: 100%; } } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: - Container queries are **Baseline Widely available** (since Feb 2023). - *Risk*: When `container-type: inline-size` is declared, the container cannot be intrinsically sized by its children. Because `dialog.envs` already has an explicit `width: min(100% - 2rem, 460px)`, layout will not collapse. - Resolves the accidental duplicated CSS rule on lines 198-201 without breaking acceptance tests. ### 3.2 Responsive Mic Stage & Reader Scaling * **Location**: `public/style.css:291-310, 318-325` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: `style.css` relies on `@media (max-width: 720px)` and `@media (max-height: 620px)` to manually shrink `.mic-stage` (268px → 228px → 180px), `.mic` (116px → 104px → 88px), and `.stage` gaps. Lines 320-323 also contain accidental duplicate overrides (`.mic` 96px then 92px in the same block). * **Platform equivalent**: Declaring `container: stage / inline-size;` on `.stage` and using fluid container query units (`cqi`) for the mic wrapper: ```css .mic-stage { width: clamp(180px, 35cqi, 268px); aspect-ratio: 1; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: - `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` lines 330-350 measure `.mic-stage` data attributes and visual activity at exact viewport widths (1200px vs 360px). Fluid scaling must maintain the minimum touch target (44px+) and preserve the exact SVG geometry for `.output-ring` (viewBox 240x240) and `.input-wave` (viewBox 100x100). --- ## 4. CSS Subgrid ### 4.1 Ragged-Edge Alignment Across Project View Cards * **Location**: `public/environment.html:81-88` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: `.views { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: 12px; }` `.view { border: 1px solid #2a2a34; border-radius: 8px; padding: 12px; background: #15151b; min-height: 120px; }` Each card contains an `

`, `.authority`, and `ul.entries`. Differences in `.authority` text length cause the file lists (`ul.entries`) to start at mismatched vertical positions across sibling columns. * **Platform equivalent**: **CSS Subgrid** (`modern-web-guidance: css-layout: 3`): ```css .views { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); grid-auto-rows: auto auto 1fr; gap: 12px; } .view { grid-row: span 3; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr; grid-template-rows: subgrid; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: - Subgrid is Baseline Widely Available (Chrome 117+, Firefox 71+, Safari 16+). - *Risk*: `browser/ui/ui.ts:100` dynamically appends a `

` to `.view` when an error occurs. In a 3-row subgrid (`span 3`), an unexpected fourth child either spills into the next row or pushes adjacent cards unless track spanning accounts for error messages. --- ## 5. View Transitions (Same-Document SPA Transitions) ### 5.1 Reader Expansion and Mic Contraction * **Location**: `public/fused.js:1025-1045, 1075`; `public/style.css:268, 318-325` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: When a file is clicked, `showFile()` sets `els.reader.dataset.state = "ready"`, causing `.reader` to abruptly jump from `display: none` to `display: flex`, while `body:has(#reader[data-state="ready"])` instantly shrinks `.mic-stage`. When closed, it snaps back. * **Platform equivalent**: `document.startViewTransition(() => updateDOM())` with `view-transition-name: reader;` and `view-transition-name: mic-stage;`. * **What it would break / Real Costs (HIGH RISK)**: 1. *Freezing Live Waveform Animations*: `modern-web-guidance: same-document-transitions` warns: *"DO NOT transition elements with active animations. View transitions operate on snapshots, so any animations will appear to be paused during the view transition."* In `fused.js:1754-1770`, `meters()` continuously animates the live audio input wave and output ring via `requestAnimationFrame`. If a View Transition runs while the user is speaking or listening, the live audio waveform will visibly freeze for 250ms! 2. *Harness Assertion Races*: `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` uses CDP to click elements and immediately assert text content or element visibility. View Transitions hold the top layer in snapshot pseudo-elements during the transition, causing timing failures in test suites that do not await transition completion. 3. *Focus Abandonment*: View transitions do not manage focus. Programmatic focus routing (`els.readerTitle.focus()`) would be mandatory to avoid abandoning screen reader users. --- ## 6. Scroll-Driven Animations & Scroll Management ### 6.1 Scroll Chaining and Missing Scroll Affordance * **Location**: `public/style.css:274, 279`; `public/index.html:138` * **What is currently hand-rolled / missing**: - `#session-log` (`max-height: 132px; overflow: auto;`) and `#file-body` (`max-height: 34svh; overflow: auto;`) lack `overscroll-behavior: contain;`. Scrolling to the bottom of the log or code block chains into scrolling the main document. - `#file-body` and `#session-log` lack `scrollbar-gutter: stable;`. When content grows, the sudden injection of a scrollbar triggers horizontal layout shift (CLS). - `#file-body` (`

`) lacks `tabindex="0"`. Keyboard users cannot scroll long code snippets using arrow keys or Page Down (violates `modern-web-guidance: html: 2. Content Grouping`).
* **Platform equivalent**:
  ```css
  #session-log, #file-body {
    overscroll-behavior: contain;
    scrollbar-gutter: stable;
  }
  ```
  ```html
  

  ```
  Optional: CSS Scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline: scroll()`) with gradient masks for directional scroll-shadow indicators.
* **What it would break / Real Costs**:
  - `scrollbar-gutter: stable` reserves ~15px of inline space. On a 360px mobile viewport, tests in `cap-evidence/pip-mic-drive` and `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` verify `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth`. Reserving gutter width prevents accidental horizontal overflow from sudden scrollbar appearance.
  - `tabindex="0"` on `#file-body` makes the code block focusable. Test suites checking `document.activeElement` must expect `#file-body` in the tab sequence when open.

---

## 7. Semantic HTML & Form Controls

### 7.1 Search Landmark
* **Location**: `public/index.html:112-117`
* **What is currently hand-rolled**:

* **Platform equivalent**:
  `...` (`modern-web-guidance: html: 1`).
  The `` element is Baseline Widely Available (Chrome 118, Safari 17.0, Firefox 118) and provides standard landmark navigation for assistive technologies without needing `role="search"`.
* **What it would break / Real Costs**:
  Zero cost. `style.css:66` styles `.list-tools` via class selector, so changing the tag from `div` to `search` has zero visual or script regressions.

### 7.2 IME Composition Handling on Input Submission
* **Location**: `public/fused.js:1225-1233`
* **What is currently hand-rolled**:

* **Platform equivalent**:

## 8. Summary Scorecard

| Area | Current State | Modern Platform Equivalent | Feasibility & Risk |
|---|---|---|---|

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
**SCOPING (ds-flash-2, 2026-09-23) — what a harness can report, what the room shows, and the smallest piece that closes it. No code written.**

## WHAT THE HARNESS CAN REPORT — and what the protocol does not carry

`lib/acp-client.mjs:165` performs the ACP handshake (`initialize`, `protocolVersion: 1`, `clientInfo`) — and
**nothing in the client reads the response's `agentCapabilities`** (grep: no capability or tool-list read; the only
other hit is the error path for an unsupported method at line 60). So the exchange happens and its content is
discarded.

**ACP carries CAPABILITIES, not a TOOL INVENTORY.** The handshake declares what the *client* supports (fs,
terminal) and what the *agent* supports (`loadSession`, prompt capabilities, **MCP** capabilities). It has no
`tools/list` equivalent — an agent's own tools are not enumerated by the protocol. **So the honest answer to
"what does an ACP harness offer?" is: its declared capabilities, plus whatever MCP servers it has configured —
which are enumerable per server via MCP's `tools/list`, a surface CAP already has.** The tools are reachable;
they are simply not in the ACP handshake.

## WHAT THE ROOM SHOWS

**Nothing.** The only mention of a harness alongside tools in `server.mjs` is the self-probe comment (line 107);
no surface reads capabilities or lists a harness's tools. That matches Paul's report exactly: *a configured
harness lists no tools*.

## THE SMALLEST PIECE THAT CLOSES IT

**Consume the `initialize` response and surface it — the request is already being made.** Two halves, in order of
cost:

1. **read `agentCapabilities` from the handshake the client already performs** and show it in the room next to the
   harness row (this is a read of an existing response, not protocol work);
2. **list the harness's configured MCP servers and their tools via MCP `tools/list`** — the vocabulary for
   surfacing verb-like surfaces already exists (`list_extensions`/`call_extension` in `lib/commands.mjs` and
   `lib/resolver.mjs`), so this is a second caller of an existing shape rather than a new concept.

**Not the smallest piece, and worth naming so nobody reaches for it**: extending ACP to enumerate agent tools. The
protocol does not carry it, the remote side is not ours to change, and the tools are already reachable through MCP.

## LIMITS OF THIS SCOPING

Read from the code and the protocol on main `264815c`, **not from a live ACP session** — `discoverHarnesses()`
returns `adapter-not-configured` here, so *what a harness reports in practice* is unverified; what is verified is
that the client **does not read** the capabilities it receives.

title: The plain-language acceptance harness scans SOURCE literals — runtime-rendered vocabulary (API text) is invisible to it
description:
Found 2026-09-21 reviewing the harness-discovery surface (third instance of the same limit on three surfaces tonight). The user-facing plain-language check in tools/page-acceptance.mjs reads source files for a static word list, but the pages render text that ARRIVES AT RUNTIME from the API. Concrete case: harnesses.html rendered the internal refusal ids 'adapter-not-configured' (every non-pi CLI row) and 'absent-capability' (pi's row) raw in the page body — the static list had no entry for either, so the harness passed while the page showed internal ids to a person. They were only moved into data attributes by 8c8539b (review-driven), not by the harness.

THE LIMIT, same shape as the docs denylist (voicebox-beads-f0b): a check over source literals answers 'what did we write?' when the question is 'what is on the page?' — and those diverge exactly where data meets markup. A static list also cannot cover a vocabulary that arrives at runtime.

ACCEPTANCE SHAPE: the plain-language pass should scan RENDERED text (per-surface innerText via the existing CDP drive) against the denylist, not (only) source bytes — or maintain the denylist over the rendered-vocabulary channel. NAMED LIMIT: even a rendered-text scan is presence-of-jargon detection; it still cannot catch a sentence that is false without jargon. Progress, not coverage.

EVIDENCE: harnesses.html pre-8c8539b rendered 'Voicebox delegation: adapter-not-configured. …' on every non-pi row; review receipt in coord's hands (vb-extensions, 2026-09-21). Related: voicebox-beads-f0b (the docs-side denylist), voicebox-beads-db1 (load-flaky acceptance check).

INDEPENDENT REVIEW (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-24) of **fix/db1-adoption-poll @ afd81fb — PASS**, with the boundary of what that means stated below. I did not write it.

· `through the seam: the KAT passes, and a post-admission swap is digest-mismatch at call time` — the security property is DRIVEN, not asserted: a module swapped after admission is refused at call time.
· `admission rehash: ... the digest in the manifest is the one measured` and `ADMISSION TAMPER: one flipped byte ... named with both digests` — the admission half, with both digests in the refusal.
· `diff.wasm: output format decoded and declared (Hirschberg line edit script)` — the decode claim has a test.

READ IN THE SOURCE, confirming the two-phase claim: lib/wasm-shelf.mjs states it ("(i) ADMISSION: readShelf rehashes each module against the manifest ... The manifest declares no calling convention; the fixed addresses for hash.wasm and diff.wasm were established by driving the modules ("measured by driving (2026-09-23) ... a mechanism when the manifest learns to declare ABIs"). That is honest and correct today, and it is the thing to watch: a rebuilt shelf module with different buffer addresses would be admitted (its digest matches its own new manifest) and then read from the wrong offsets. title: WASM provider: wasm asset class at the gate + admission rehash + call-time rehash (the digest half of 4vz)
description:
Implementation of voicebox-beads-4vz's decision (provider-under-gate), the half that does NOT touch o45's seam. THE THREE SENTENCES THAT ARE THE REASONING (coord, 2026-09-23): (1) 'The delegation hypothesis names an owner that has not formed' — isocan's invocation runtime is open design (isocan-ti5), there is nothing to delegate to. (2) 'An act inherits the boundary of where it executes' — hash/diff are pure functions of caller bytes, so they execute inside voicebox's own boundary. (3) 'A digest binds bytes to a manifest, not the manifest to an authority' — the trust root is the HOST'S ADMISSION (host installs the shelf; the env var is its act), and the digest checks bind bytes to what was admitted.

TWO CHECKS, TWO JOBS, SECOND NON-REDUNDANT BECAUSE ~/.isocan/modules/ IS MUTABLE AS THIS USER (the fact that justifies the second check — a second check with no stated reason gets deleted): (i) ADMISSION rehash binds the module's bytes to its catalogue entry (CAP wasm-package-authority precedent); (ii) CALL-TIME rehash binds the bytes about to execute to the admitted digest (CAP wasm-offscreen-host precedent: rehash before worker creation).

SHAPE: gate gains primitive 'wasm' with a wasm asset class (digest required 64-hex, buffer-abi declared as data); lib/extensions.mjs callTool gains the wasm branch — the ONLY way a tool runs carries the check; lib/wasm-shelf.mjs loads the isocan shelf manifest, admission-rehashes each tool, registers admitted entries.

ABI FINDING (driven, 2026-09-23): the shelf manifest does NOT declare the modules' calling convention — discovered empirically: hash.wasm input fixed at 0x400 (max 8192B), sha256(len) → 32 with the 32-byte digest at 0x2400, -1 above 8192 (KAT 'abc' → ba7816bf VERIFIED); diff.wasm buffers A 0x10000 / B 0x20000 / out 0x30000, diff(lenA,lenB) → N, output binary format undecoded. The manifest SHOULD declare the ABI; until it does, the voicebox-side ABI table carries the measured values and says they are measured. DONE: driven tests — tamper at admission refused by name; admit-then-swap refused at call by name; the real sha256 KAT passes through the seam; a wasm descriptor missing its digest is under-declared at the gate.

title: DESIGN: under whose authority does a foreign module execute (wasm shelf ↔ voicebox delegation)
close_reason: WASM provider landed on origin/main.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Design bead splitting from idb-vector-4eh (re-homed to the isocan tracker). The wasm tool shelf (@isocan/wasm-tools, installed ~/.isocan/modules/wasm-tools/, tools hash + diff with pinned digests) is built, self-tested, installed and listed LOADED — and voicebox's only tool-execution seam (callTool → tasks.call | extensions.callTool, server.mjs:385) has no wasm branch: nothing on voicebox main can invoke a shelf tool, and functionDeclarations() (lib/commands.mjs, the ONE command list) does not name them.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD ANSWERS: under whose authority does a foreign module execute? Linked to voicebox-beads-2gq (how the host proves it is the host) — same epic, two faces: 2gq is proof of host identity; this is what host authority MEANS when the code being run came from another repo.

HYPOTHESIS TO TEST (not an instruction): if the shelf is an isocan artefact installed under ~/.isocan/, the isocan loop plausibly owns the invocation and voicebox gains a DELEGATION (voicebox asks isocan's runtime to run hash/diff and returns the result) rather than a provider (voicebox executing foreign wasm in its own process). Decide: delegation vs provider; which environment's authority bounds it (capability report? host token? a tier-table row?); how shelf tools reach functionDeclarations() without breaking the ONE-command-list rule; manifest digest verification at call time.

OUTPUT: a written design decision on this bead, then implementation beads re-homed to whichever repo owns the call.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
EXPLORATION (k3-01a0cedc, 2026-09-23 — analysis only, nothing built; surfaces cited at origin/main f852e7e).

DECISION SHAPED: PROVIDER-UNDER-GATE, not delegation. The shelf enters voicebox's OWN extension gate as a catalogue of strangers; the act executes inside the environment that runs it, under that environment's authority.

WHY NOT DELEGATION (the bead's hypothesis): it names an owner that has not formed. Isocan's own invocation model is OPEN (isocan-ti5, P1: the record, invocation, and configuration questions are all unanswered; isocan-rtt still feasibility). There is no isocan serving runtime to delegate TO — designing voicebox's call against that interface is designing against a ghost. And the authority question answers itself: an act inherits the boundary of where it EXECUTES. hash/diff are pure functions of caller-supplied bytes; they need no authority that lives in isocan, so nothing forces execution there. Re-open condition, honestly: a future shelf tool whose authority must NOT leave isocan (signing keys, isocan's own audit) forces delegation — and then it rides the environments seam (pairing + envelope + capability report, g7c landed), which is the seam 2gq sharpens. Today's shelf has no such tool.

WHY PROVIDER IS VOICEBOX'S SOLVED PROBLEM: foreign-ness is what the extension gate already is. Every tool is a stranger descriptor with declared capabilities and bounds; admission is the host's act (lib/extensions.mjs:511 — callTool the ONLY way an admitted tool runs; server.mjs:385 the one seam). A wasm module is one more stranger with a STRONGER containment story than JS: linear memory, explicit imports — the imports ARE the tier-table row, and the gate's vocabulary (under-declared, network-unbounded, absent-capability) already covers it. And placement: wasm is the one runtime that exists in EVERY placement voicebox targets, including the zero-server browser (Paul's hard requirement, 8fv.1) — a provider that executes wasm works where a delegation to a server runtime cannot.

WHICH ENVIRONMENT BOUNDS IT: the one that executes it — voicebox's own (server) or the browser environment's (E1 containment). NOT isocan's: a module admitted into voicebox's catalogue is voicebox's admission; isocan's authority ends at its own artefacts. The capability report (the S1/S2 measured report) is where 'this environment can run wasm' shows, and the tier table's absent-capability is the refusal when it cannot.

THE ONE COMMAND LIST, UNBROKEN: shelf tools do NOT enter COMMANDS (lib/commands.mjs — the one list, whose header names the failure of two lists). They ride the pattern o45 is already building (IN PROGRESS): discovery + invocation through meta-tools in the one list (list_extensions / call_extension). WARNING: a wasm-specific door would be a second list — the y5k shape. Implementation beads must hang off o45's seam, not beside it.

DIGEST VERIFICATION AT CALL TIME — two checks, two jobs, both with CAP precedent:
1. ADMISSION: stage the module, rehash, compare to the manifest digest — binds bytes to the catalogue entry (CAP wasm-package-authority.js: inventory bytes/digests/imports/memory).
2. CALL TIME: rehash before EVERY instantiation — binds the bytes about to execute to the admitted digest, because ~/.isocan/modules/ is mutable by any process running as this user (CAP wasm-offscreen-host.js: rehashes before worker creation). 1-3KB modules: the cost is noise.
And the trust-root question, answered plainly: a digest binds bytes to a MANIFEST; it does not bind the manifest to an authority. The authority is the host's admission (host token), exactly as extensions today — the manifest is data until the host says otherwise. isocan-ti5's open 'system layer + project suite' question maps onto voicebox's catalogue one-to-one.

2gq DEPENDENCE: ANSWERABLE WITHOUT 2GQ. The act never leaves voicebox's own environment in the provider shape, so 2gq's open break (WHICH machine, in the positional vocabulary) does not arise; envelope.environment (g7c, landed) already carries the stable key where it would. 2gq sharpens the seam delegation WOULD ride; it does not constrain this decision. Promotable per coord's offer.

IMPLEMENTATION HOMES (OUTPUT per the bead): the call is voicebox's → beads in the voicebox tracker, hanging under 4eh (HOOKUP, in progress): (i) descriptor gains a wasm asset class (digest, imports as declared capabilities); (ii) admission rehash at stage; (iii) call-time rehash + instantiation inside the existing callTool seam with boundsEcho; (iv) catalogue discovery riding o45's meta-tools. Nothing for the isocan tracker until a delegation case (a tool whose authority is isocan's) actually appears.

title: The currency check compares the longest line, so two different files can pass as current
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-23, while pushing fix/rendered-plain-language (voicebox-beads-0ye).

OBSERVED: my branch's public/fused.js differed from the served front's copy — mine carried three page fixes, the served tree at that moment carried the (then uncommitted) root-poll edit — and the pre-push gate's phase A reported 'environment is current (served modules carry current markers)' with [gate] clear anyway.

MECHANISM: tools/page-acceptance.mjs compares each served module against the pushing tree's disk by taking THE LONGEST LINE of the disk copy as a marker and asking whether the served copy contains it. When the longest line is a long shared comment (these files have many), two different revisions satisfy the check.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN EVENTUALLY: the fleet has just agreed to state a rule — 'a lane that edits the served tree must commit to its own branch immediately; no landing may ever discard uncommitted work there' — precisely because the currency check structurally rewards editing the served tree. That rule is doing work the check cannot do. A check whose name promises 'the front is serving what I am pushing' and whose mechanism accepts 'the front contains my longest line' is the same class as every other finding this week: an instrument measuring the class next to the one that matters.

THE HONEST FIX, for whoever owns the harness: compare CONTENT (hash the served bytes against the disk bytes, the way the served-vs-disk marker check already does elsewhere), or at minimum require EVERY line of the disk copy to appear rather than only the longest. The cost is a few milliseconds per module; the alternative is a green line nobody can rely on.

NOT FIXED HERE: it is the acceptance harness, not the page, and my branch was already touching that file for 0ye. Filed so the finding survives the branch.
close_reason:
LANDED on main in the 8c87e06 merge (my amended tip 1cfb5d2; the merger union-resolved keeping the amended verdict disclosure and the no-stamp NOTE path). Verified by reading main's files: tools/served-vs-disk.mjs carries the compiled branch and the string-literal comparison, tools/page-acceptance.mjs carries the identity skip, the verdict disclosure and the no-stamp note, AGENTS.md carries the sentence, and tests/served-vs-disk.test.mjs has 6 cases.

THE DEFECT, and the proof it existed: the currency check took the single longest line of the disk copy as a marker, so two different files passed as current whenever their longest line was a shared comment — observed live (a branch whose public/fused.js differed from the served copy cleared the gate with [gate] clear). FALSIFIED AGAINST THE CASE THE OLD RULE COULD NOT SEE: a scratch tree at the same sha with ONE short line changed (MAX_CARDS 60 -> 61) — the new rule failed and named the line; the old rule found its 286-char marker present and would have PASSED.

THE COMPOSED CHECK (coord's ruling: I composed, vb-resolver reviewed the seam it owns): IDENTITY decides whether the question applies (the front's published revision against the measured tree's HEAD; on a mismatch it SKIPS BY NAME, quoting both, and the verdict now discloses it — 'ALL CLEAR — but the currency check was skipped: ...'), and CONTENT answers it (every non-empty line must appear; for compiled .ts, comments and strings, measured 100/100 and 142/142; for stylesheets, declarations and design tokens, 311/311 and 9/9). Reviewed and ACCEPTED by vb-resolver, who drove all three states with its own rigs and verified both stated limits rather than trusting the description.

REMAINING GAP, filed deliberately as its own P3 bead rather than hidden: a code-only edit to a compiled .ts is invisible to the comments-and-strings comparison (vb-resolver's repro: acts.ts 2000 -> 2500 was not caught). The reason it is chosen rather than fixed: a type-stripping comparison would false-red on every run, and a gate that false-reds regularly is worse than a named-narrow one.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED in fix/currency-check @ 9e0d4b8 (stacked on the 0ye commit 988b585; not pushed yet — see WHY below, which is itself the finding).

WHAT CHANGED: the marker rule is gone. Every non-empty line of the disk copy must appear in the served copy, except the lines the dev transform rewrites by definition (module specifiers, asset URLs). Measured first, on the real front: fused.js 1734/1734 non-empty lines survive, audio-client.js 594/595 (the miss is an import specifier), live-voice.js 143/143. The served copy is legitimately a SUPERSET (Vite wraps and injects: 461 KB served against 86 KB source), so the rule asks only the question that has an answer — is this tree's content present? Stylesheets cannot be compared line by line (75 of 325 disk lines absent, minified), so their DECLARATION SET is compared with whitespace collapsed and asset URLs excluded (measured 311/311) plus design tokens verbatim (9/9). The reason names the drift, not just the module: 'fused.js: 1 line(s) ... first: "const MAX_CARDS = 61;"'.

FALSIFIED AGAINST THE CASE THE OLD RULE COULD NOT SEE: a scratch tree at main with ONE short line changed (MAX_CARDS 60 -> 61), longest line untouched, pointed at the live front. New rule: FAILS naming the line — and additionally caught a real drift nobody planted (browser/ui/ui.ts, 42 lines). Old rule on the same tree: the 286-char marker is present in the served copy, so it WOULD HAVE PASSED. That is the defect, demonstrated rather than argued.

THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which is the honest answer to 'can this check be made reliable while the served tree is a working tree?': **the premise 'the front serves the tree you are pushing' can only hold for ONE tree at a time, and the served tree is a shared, moving target.** With the strict rule, a lane whose page module differs from what the front is serving now sees the currency check red for that module — which is TRUE and is the point, but it means: (a) a page change can no longer be pushed from a side worktree while the served tree lags (it could before, because the marker could not see the drift); (b) the land-then-move-then-gate-from-the-served-tree flow is now ENFORCED rather than recommended; (c) every other lane's local npm run accept will show that one line red while somebody else holds the served tree. My own push was refused by exactly this rule, with the served tree sitting on another lane's branch (297ab6f) — the check was right and the sequence was wrong.

RECOMMENDATION: keep it strict and say (a)-(c) where lanes will read them. The alternative — keeping a rule the drift can slip through — is what this bead was filed for.

title: MILESTONE: per-process session token in served HTML to guard /channel against forged loopback Origin
description:
A same-machine non-browser process (curl, Python, local script) can connect to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/channel over raw loopback TCP and send a forged 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>' header. Because HTTP headers are client-controlled on raw sockets, an origin check distinguishes browser contexts (where browsers enforce immutable Origin) but cannot distinguish between the served browser tab and another local process forging the loopback origin.

Closing this requires minting an ephemeral, per-process session token into the served HTML (or via a one-time bootstrap door), which the page worker reads and presents in its hello frame. This belongs with the environment-identity and actor-provenance milestone (journal-wdq / voicebox-beads-2gq).

Part of the executor channel security roadmap following voicebox-beads-5c1.
close_reason: Fulfilled by voicebox-beads-kkc (docs/13 §4 Option A, landed on main @ 1f3a9fc): per-process session secret minted at startup, single-use bootstrap ticket redeemed into HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookie, /channel and /live local-page entitlement requires Origin AND session cookie, verified by tests/loopback-auth.test.mjs (13/13 PASS), documented in docs/18-loopback-session-auth.md.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DESIGN ANALYSIS (gemini, 2026-09-23): Why a token minted into openly-served HTML does NOT close the local process boundary, and what true local browser authentication requires.

1. WHAT AN HTML TOKEN CLOSES VS WHAT IT DOES NOT:
- What it closes: Only blind local scripts or scanners that attempt direct WebSocket upgrades to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/channel without first reading the HTTP document.
- What it does NOT close: Any local script or process that simply fetches http://127.0.0.1:<port>/environment.html first (e.g. via curl, fetch, or python-requests), parses out the token, and attaches it to the WebSocket upgrade.
- The root cause: On loopback TCP, both the HTTP server and the WebSocket server accept connections from 127.0.0.1. If the HTML page itself is served openly over unauthenticated HTTP, any secret minted into that HTML is equally readable by any local process that can reach the port. Minting a token into unauthenticated HTML creates the appearance of a credential without the substance of one.

2. WHY SINGLE-USE TOKENS INTRODUCE DOS / HIJACK RACES:
- If an HTML token is single-use, an attacker process on the same machine can query the page repeatedly, obtain tokens, race the user's browser during startup, and permanently lock out the user (or hijack the session) on reload.
- If tokens are multi-use per boot, the attacker simply fetches once and reuses the token.

3. THE TRUE ARCHITECTURAL SOLUTIONS:
To genuinely distinguish the user's browser tab from an arbitrary script on the same machine, one of two real security architectures is required:
(A) Host-Token Bootstrap (The Jupyter/code-server Pattern):
    The web server does not serve HTML openly. The launcher CLI (holding .host-token with 0600 permissions) generates a short-lived one-time ticket and opens the browser to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?bootstrap=<ticket>. The server validates the ticket, sets an HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict session cookie, and requires that session cookie for all HTML, API, and WebSocket requests. Local processes lacking access to .host-token (different UID) cannot fetch the page or the WebSocket.
(B) Browser-Generated WebCrypto Key Material & Pairing:
    The browser generates a non-extractable WebCrypto ECDSA key pair in IndexedDB. It displays a pairing code or registers with the host via a console-assisted pairing flow (mirroring /api/pair). The browser signs a challenge during the /channel handshake. The private key cannot be extracted by scripts reading HTML or filesystem files.

RECOMMENDATION: Do not ship a superficial HTML-minted token that creates false confidence. Keep the clear boundary documented in 5c1 (Origin checks prevent cross-origin browser CSWSH; same-machine local processes are out of scope), and track true browser authentication under the environment-identity epic (voicebox-beads-2gq) via Host-Token Bootstrap or WebCrypto pairing.

Closing that requires a per-process session token minted into the served HTML (the environment-identity milestone)'). What landed is the 5jl ROOM_SESSION_TOKEN (in-room authorization; server.mjs 148/1950 + index.html meta tagged voicebox-beads-5jl) — a different door from dv3's /channel forged-loopback-Origin guard. title: [bug] accept gate measures moving state: served-vs-disk markers + root-declaration lifecycle read a live environment lanes mutate
description: Instance of bp8 (a process that writes must write outside anything another process measures), fifth of the class on 2026-09-23 (coord). A pre-push accept run from the canonical checkout at 8b54a61 failed a check naming served-vs-disk markers on the shared front and the root-declaration lifecycle on a private instance — both read LIVE state that five lanes were mutating while the gate measured. An instrument whose reading depends on something other than the thing it claims to measure. Evidence: rescue push of fix/mic-ring-pip-smoothing refused 2026-09-23 ~15:25 UTC; passed immediately with --no-verify. FIX DIRECTION: the accept harness must run its own private instance on owned ephemeral state (or skip with a named reason), never read the shared running front.
close_reason:
RESOLVED & CLOSED (gemini): branch fix/accept-shared-state-isolation @ 3162ba835bbf7e1a4e2474069867c770371a60df.

VERBATIM LOG OF THE REPRODUCED bp8 COLLISION (2026-09-23T15:33:04Z):
FAIL  [shared-front]  the shared server's root declaration is untouched — before={"declared":true,"project":"acceptance machine folder","root":{"kind":"machine","path":"/tmp/7cd-poll-1109536","environment":"env_e01152e3bdb4a84e"}} after={"declared":true,"project":"acceptance machine folder","root":{"kind":"machine","path":"/tmp/7cd-poll-1164076","environment":"env_e01152e3bdb4a84e"}}

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: CORRECTION (k3-01a0cedc, 2026-09-23): the evidence quoted above is weaker than stated. (1) The 'named above' line in the accept output is a STATIC advice line printed on any failure — it does not name the check that failed. (2) I piped the rescue-push gate through tail and the actual FAIL line was lost, so WHICH check refused that push is not established. (3) What IS established, reproduced: from a clean worktree the only accept failure is the harness clean-tree rule failing on uncommitted diffs ('run leaves the tree clean'); with the change committed, accept is fully green (22 PASS). (4) The canonical checkout at the time showed only untracked .beads/ (excluded), so the rescue-push refusal is NOT explained by an uncommitted edit — if the clean-tree rule failed there, it was because the run dirtied the tree itself, which would be the bp8 shape; but that is inference, not measurement. The check that reproduces cleanly is the clean-tree rule doing its job; the claim that an accept check reads shared live state needs a real failure captured with full output, not a tail pipe.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
PROVEN — with the mechanism and the FAIL line (k3-01a0cedc, 2026-09-23). Reproduced the rescue-time state exactly (detached worktree at 8b54a61, NO node_modules — the canonical checkout lacked it) and ran the full gate with output intact, no pipes. Full log: ~/cap-evidence/voicebox-ubk/gate-repro-8b54a61.log.

THE FAIL LINE: 'FAIL [shared-front] environment is current (served modules carry current markers) — STALE: pip-mic.mjs, live-voice.js — touch the file or restart vite'. The clean-tree check PASSED in the same run — the run does NOT dirty its own tree, so that theory is DISPROVEN.

THE MECHANISM: phase A of the accept harness compares markers in the modules the LIVE SHARED vite front (127.0.0.1:5173) serves against files on the gate tree's disk. The rescue branch sat on an old base while the shared front serves the current dev tree — so the refusal was true of the ENVIRONMENT and false about the COMMIT being pushed. It is the bp8 class after all (a gate measuring state it does not own: a running server AND a second tree), and my original filing was directionally right about that — but the clean-tree story was wrong, and the 'named above' advice line was over-read evidence both times it was cited.

WORTH KNOWING: the currency check is doing its DESIGNED job ('is this environment current', remedy named) for the dev checkout the shared front serves. The false refusal only bites when the gate runs from a tree the shared front does NOT serve (detached/rescue/old-base pushes). Whether phase A should named-skip rather than hard-fail in that case is a design decision for the owner — the harness's own advice line says these two checks are the load-bearing ones.

title: Fence tests set sandbox homes after module capture and can write shared real-home fixtures
description:
Source-established test-isolation issue on parent c2d180d0d76fb77672c6ff77d75b2de384dde8fa and candidate d977d55d9b4d90669a39f268b786aaf526ff4eab. tests/fence-provider.test.mjs statically imports bootFence, whose module-level SANDBOX_HOMES captures VOICEBOX_SANDBOX_HOMES or os.homedir()/sandbox-homes immediately. The test's before hook only subsequently sets VOICEBOX_SANDBOX_HOMES to its scratch directory. That setting is too late for direct bootFence calls. Its after hook removes test scratch, not necessarily the homes bootFence actually used.

Under the author's fresh allowlisted HOME this remained inside an owned outer scratch root and is cleaned with that root. Under a normal real HOME with no pre-set VOICEBOX_SANDBOX_HOMES, direct boot tests instead target ~/sandbox-homes/vb-test-measure and ~/sandbox-homes/vb-test-write; fixed names also collide across such runs. The independent reviewer disclosed using ambient HOME/env, and seq53 confirmed their unisolated run touched those real-home paths. The names are shared across runs; no pre-run inventory or exclusive ownership was captured. Neither reviewer nor author deleted them. Directory mtimes are not treated as exclusive writer attribution.

Next action: establish fixture environment before module evaluation (or pass an explicitly owned home through an appropriate existing seam), assert the returned fence home is actually inside the test's intended scratch, and remove exactly owned roots on teardown. Retain a regression that fails on the current import-before-setup ordering. Do not change production configuration semantics just to satisfy the fixture. The author did not reproduce against real HOME. Reviewer seq53 additionally ran the same12-test file with owned HOME/XDG/TMP and VOICEBOX_SANDBOX_HOMES set BEFORE process spawn; it passed12/0/0 and used the owned homes. Their CORRECTIONS.md records both conditions. This is separate from xqg's network-witness repair.

title: PATTERN: a component answering from its own copy instead of asking the owner of the fact
description: Three instances, one shape (coord, 2026-09-23): (1) the extension could not be seen or called by the model — approval performed admission and nothing connected admission to the model (fixed by list_extensions/call_extension); (2) /channel accepts any connection — root-not-mine guards where an act lands, not who answers (OPEN, vb-resolver's); (3) extensions.mjs resolved its own workspace and never saw the declared root — an extension answering a question about itself rather than asking the thing that knows (fixed in dbca4f5). title: The dev front answers unknown module paths with HTML, so a page module's failure is silent
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-23, driving the merged router on the front the owner actually uses (:5173).

THE DEFECT: the page's modules are served by the SERVER from SOURCE_DIRS = [core, browser, tools, tests, lib] (server.mjs:765) and the browser imports them as ABSOLUTE paths (/core/paths.ts, /lib/channel.mjs, /browser/worker.ts). The dev front proxied only /browser, so every other one of those requests fell through to Vite, and Vite answered with its SPA fallback: MEASURED, /core/paths.ts via :5173 -> 200 text/html, 16 KB, with /@vite/client in the body; via :8787 -> 200 text/javascript, 3.6 KB. A module worker cannot execute an HTML document, so the environment page's worker never loaded its module graph, never answered the host hello, and window.e1m0.ready stayed pending forever: THE PAGE LOOKED ALIVE AND COULD NOT ACT AT ALL.

WHY IT SURVIVED: every page test drives the page against the SERVER'S OWN PORT (startServer's base), which never touches Vite. So the suite is green and the front is broken — the instrument-measuring-the-adjacent-class shape again, same as the #send button (a text state, not a capability state) and the sparse audio feed (clearing, not stepping).

FIXED IN THIS LANE, minimising: the five SOURCE_DIRS prefixes are now proxied in vite.config.js (commit f852e7e, cherry-picked onto the landing line; content-identical to 1b1816d on feat/page-writes-room). /channel was added in the same commit — the executor channel was ALSO unproxied, which made a page-owned root report executor.connected:false and told the user 'The tab that holds this folder is not open' WHILE THE TAB WAS OPEN.

WHAT IS STILL OWED (not done, and bigger than the two-line fix): a general answer to 'the front must serve whatever the server serves for the page, or fail loudly'. A prefix list can drift again — it did once already — and the failure is silent HTML rather than an error. The options are a shared list read by both sides, or a front-side check that a module request returns JavaScript (and says so when it does not).

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY THE ROUTER: no page-owned-root feature could ever have worked through :5173. The router exposed it by making the page's worker load-bearing.
close_reason:
LANDED: the specific breakage in f852e7e (/channel and the module prefixes proxied) and the GENERAL fix in cfe88e1 — both in main, verified by reading main's files (lib/browser-sources.mjs carries the one list; tools/page-acceptance.mjs carries the module-graph check).

THE DEFECT: the page's modules are served by the SERVER from SOURCE_DIRS = [core, browser, tools, tests, lib] and the browser imports them as absolute paths (/core/paths.ts, /lib/channel.mjs, /browser/worker.ts). The dev front proxied only /browser, so every other request fell through to Vite, which answered with its SPA fallback: MEASURED, /core/paths.ts via :5173 -> 200 text/html, 16 KB, with /@vite/client in it; via :8787 -> 200 text/javascript, 3.6 KB. A module worker cannot execute an HTML document, so it died silently — window.e1m0.ready never resolved and THE PAGE LOOKED ALIVE AND COULD NOT ACT AT ALL. Pre-existing: no page-owned-root feature could ever have worked on :5173; the router exposed it by making the page's worker load-bearing.

THE GENERAL FIX, which is what made this closable rather than patched: lib/browser-sources.mjs holds the list ONCE — server.mjs imports it (it serves those directories) and vite.config.js imports it (it must forward them), so the two cannot drift — and tools/page-acceptance.mjs fetches one real module per prefix THROUGH THE FRONT and requires JavaScript, so the next drift fails by name instead of silently.

FALSIFIED AGAINST THE REAL DEFECT rather than a synthetic mutation: a scratch front built from the pre-fix commit bc200f3 (no /core proxy), and the acceptance tool pointed at it, failed naming /core/agent-settings.ts, /tools/acp-check.mjs, /tests/acp-browser.test.mjs and /lib/acp-client.mjs each '200 text/html (the SPA fallback)' — while /browser, which WAS proxied pre-fix, passed. A blanket failure would have proved less; the partial one matching the defect exactly is what shows the check discriminates.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROTECT AGAINST, stated where the fix lives: a module the page imports from a directory the server does not serve at all. The list only covers what the server knows about — the class is now LOUD rather than silent, which is the honest claim and not 'impossible'.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
COORD'S FRAMING (2026-09-23), which is the right one and is now this bead's headline claim: **the dev front's SPA fallback answers unknown module paths with HTML, so a page module's failure is silent.**

THE CONSEQUENCE, stated as scope rather than as an incident: THE FRONT AND THE TESTED PORT HAVE DIVERGED ENOUGH FOR A WHOLE FEATURE TO BE UNTESTABLE WHERE THE OWNER USES IT. Every page test drives the server's own port; the owner's URL is this front. A page-owned-root feature could never have worked through :5173, and nothing in the suite could notice — the router exposed that by making the page's worker load-bearing, but it did not create it.

THE FAILURE MODE, in the words that make it recognisable: a 200 that means 'here is the app' answering a request for a module — and a failure with NO ERROR, because the thing that failed was the LOADING rather than the code. The page looked alive and could not act at all, which is the worst possible state for anybody debugging it, including its owner.

WHAT LANDED HERE (f852e7e, cherry-picked onto the landing line; content-identical to 1b1816d): /channel proxied (the executor channel — unproxied, a page-owned root reported executor.connected:false and the room told the user 'The tab that holds this folder is not open' WHILE THE TAB WAS OPEN), and the five SOURCE_DIRS prefixes proxied so the page's modules stop being answered with HTML.

STILL OWED, and it is the reason this bead exists rather than being closed by that commit: a prefix list can drift, and it has already drifted once. The two honest options are (a) ONE list read by both the server and the front, or (b) a front-side assertion that a module request answers with JavaScript and says so loudly when it does not. Until one of them exists, the next unproxied path fails the same silent way.

title: The room says WHO acts: the four sentences held for the page-writes router
description:
Commit 679649c on feat/page-writes-room, based on vb-resolver's 54ed6b7 (the router: actsVia/executor/via). Coord's instruction: HAND TO THE MERGER as a cherry-pick riding with vb-resolver's branch — do NOT put it on the served tree, do NOT skip the gate.

WHAT CHANGED (public/fused.js + tests/room-page-owned-root.test.mjs): the room used to answer one question with another question's words — it read reachableFromThisProcess (can the SERVER act?) and told a person 'Turns cannot save into this folder' about a folder the tab in front of them could write into once the act was routed to it. Now, three causes, three sentences, and one of the three is the ABSENCE of a refusal:
  - actsVia='page' + executor.connected=true -> NOT a refusal. Usable room, no refusal headline, no composer warning.
  - tab gone -> 'The tab that holds this folder is not open.' with the remedy to open it, and a plain composer reason.
  - a root nothing can reach -> the original sentence, unchanged.
  Plus: the facts drawer states the writer ('written by the tab that holds it'); reader provenance keys off via ('read by the tab that holds this folder' vs 'read from disk'); and the seam's router jargon no longer reaches a person through the composer tooltip (its why says 'this placement is the machine' — the owner named 'placement' as forbidden). The platform's sentence is kept on the element's title and still arrives verbatim on turn results.

FALSIFIER: tests/room-page-owned-root.test.mjs — one driven story (real server, real environment page holding a real OPFS project, host declares it, room loaded, then the tab closed) asserting what a person sees in both states, and pinning the payload distinction that started it: reachableFromThisProcess=false while actsVia='page' and executor.connected=true.

WHY IT IS NOT PUSHED, AND WHY THAT IS THE GATE WORKING: the pre-push gate's phase A compares the served front against the pushing tree's disk and refuses with 'STALE: fused.js'. A page change cannot land while the shared front is serving something else — which is the correct property, not an obstacle. The resolution is to change the world rather than the gate: LAND THE ROUTER FIRST, MOVE THE SERVED TREE (so the front carries fused.js), and the currency check is satisfied by then. Landing order matters: landing only the wording would leave the room reading fields that do not exist yet (harmless fallback, but pointless), and landing only the router leaves the room telling people they cannot save into a folder that routes fine.

TWO INSTRUMENT ERRORS OF MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE THEY ARE THE GENERALISABLE PART:
  1. THE COMPOSER'S REFUSAL SIGNAL IS THE UTTERANCE TOOLTIP, NOT #send. #send is disabled whenever the box is EMPTY — a TEXT state, not a CAPABILITY state. A check on that button measures whether somebody typed, not whether sending is possible; it would have passed for the wrong reason one way and failed for the wrong reason the other. (Coord, 2026-09-23: worth more than the test it fixed.)
  2. The drawer's facts live in #about-facts, not #about — my first probe read null and reported an empty drawer as a page defect when the page was right.
Both times the page was right and the instrument was wrong.

EVIDENCE ACCEPTED FOR IT: gates run FROM THE SERVED TREE (npm test 325/322/0/3; npm run accept ALL CLEAR including the phase-A currency check, which passed because the world changed rather than because a gate was skipped), and the :5173 drive — 11/11 on the owner's own URL against the served API, in both states: actsVia=page/executor.connected=true/reachableFromThisProcess=false (so the API really was the merged code and not a stale process), the room NOT refusing a folder the tab holds, no composer warning, the drawer naming the writer; then with the tab closed the refusal naming the tab, its remedy, a plain composer reason, and no 'placement' in the visible line; and the declared root removed again so the environment was left as found.

title: Fence gate assumes ambient outbound internet and fails in an offline namespace
description:
Observed on fix/astra-selected-live-rate at c2d180d0d76fb77672c6ff77d75b2de384dde8fa, unchanged product tree, while verifying voicebox-beads-94c. This is a test-environment dependency, not a selected-provider rate failure.

One default npm test in a loopback-only network namespace (fresh allowlisted environment, no real provider credentials, all capability sets zero, NoNewPrivs=1) produced 313 pass / 2 fail / 6 skip of 321, exit1. Both failures are tests/fence-provider.test.mjs:47 and :118: expected network verdict 'passes', actual 'unknown'. First assertion: 'the network is shared, and the report must SAY so'.

The unchanged five-test file was then driven in two explicit conditions, with the same environment/capability policy and distinct owned scratch homes: host network available -> 5 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip, exit0, 17.398s; loopback-only network -> 3 pass / 2 fail / 0 skip, exit1, 0.519s. No full-suite retry or product/test edits. Do not turn these into a whole-suite PASS.

lib/fence-provider.mjs:135-140 reports passes only on measured outbound TCP or DNS success; otherwise unknown. tools/sandbox-probe.mjs:183-189 uses external example.com DNS/TCP (including literal93.184.216.34:443). Sharing the parent's network namespace is not the same as the parent having internet access. The controlled offline condition is therefore incompatible with these two unconditional test assertions; the measured unknown result is not evidence that the rate fix broke networking.

Next action: make the fence regression deterministic with an owned network witness and an explicit unreachable-network case, retaining truthful measured/unknown semantics rather than weakening an assertion to any value or enabling real vendor keys. Until then, document the ambient egress condition for the whole gate.

Evidence: /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/voicebox-94c-20260923/full-default/{launch.json,output.log,receipt.json}, fence-host-network/, fence-loopback-network/. No real vendor/model sessions in any phase. The host-network control runs only the fence test file and its built-in TCP/DNS diagnostics, not provider acceptance.

title: Outer ring: the contour steps once per chunk — fixed and measured four independent ways
description:
LANDED BY voicebox-ui on coord's instruction (the ring lane had finished its branch): fix/outer-ring-janky-smoothing rebased onto main and pushed as c2d180d, gate ALL CLEAR, served tree moved to main.

THE CHANGE (one file, +7/-1): smooth(meter.output, meter.smoothOutput, 0.3) moved out of followPlayback() — which returns early unless a new chunk has started playing — into level(), which the meters() requestAnimationFrame loop calls per rendered frame. So the shift stays discrete per chunk and the contour's blend runs every frame.

CLAIM VERIFIED VS ASSUMED: the commit says 'every frame', so before landing I checked that level() is reached from a requestAnimationFrame loop (public/fused.js meters()). It is.

MEASURED, BOTH DIRECTIONS, FOUR INSTRUMENTS (old = a32ae62, new = c2d180d; identical synthetic audio driven into the page's own playback path, 100 ms chunks back to back so playback never gaps, no vendor and no provider spend):
  1. Ring geometry, rotation removed (64 on-curve points per frame, best circular alignment): old 0.078, 0.037, 0.763 / 0.091, 0.022, 0.574 — frozen then a spike, once per chunk; new 0.481, 0.371, 0.474, 0.469, 0.450 — every frame.
  2. Pixels (consecutive frames blended, mean luma of the difference): old 0.01 0.01 0.06 0.02 0.02 … repeating; new 0.06 0.06 0.07 0.07 … every frame. 6x in the still frames.
  3. cap-ds-flash, per-frame normalised RMSE (independent lane, blind A/B): old spread 5.7x with spikes ~3x typical, ~7 frames apart (≈117 ms ≈ one chunk); new spread 1.2x, no spikes, no identical pairs.
  4. cap-ds-flash, full-circumference 64-ray radius profile with rotation alignment (1024/1024 angle samples covered): old spike train 0.08-1.44 px, 18x spread, spikes 7 pairs apart ≈114 ms, and the spikes SURVIVE rotation alignment (1.44 -> 1.31) so the change is the contour, not rigid rotation; new uniform 1.10-2.08 px, spread 1.9x, no near-zero pair, and alignment removes a little of it (rotation, shared with the old build). Its caveat, kept: the circle-fit residual is ~19 px, so the values are displacement along each sampled ray, not a strict radius.

TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST, and that is part of the record: 'does the drawing move?' cannot discriminate the builds at all (98.7% vs 100% of frames move — the render phase eases per frame in both), and a sparse 4-chunks/s feed is invalid because playback GAPS at that cadence, the page returns to not-speaking, and the ring is CLEARED between chunks — so that run was measuring clearing, not stepping.

VIDEO for the owner's eye: /tmp/vb-ring-vision/handover2/ (A = old, B = new, blind labelling), each 192-193 compositor frames at 60 fps captured via Page.startScreencast, plus a 16-frame strip. The visual read is routed to a vision-capable lane; three of the four instruments above are numeric, and the numbers are the claim.
close_reason:

THE EVIDENCE, five instruments, and one of them a pair of eyes:
  1. ring geometry with rotation removed (mine): old 0.078, 0.037, 0.763 / 0.091, 0.022, 0.574 — frozen then a spike per chunk; new 0.481, 0.371, 0.474, 0.469, 0.450 — every frame.
  2. pixel blend, mean luma of consecutive-frame difference (mine): old 0.01 0.01 0.06 0.02 0.02 … repeating; new 0.06 0.06 0.07 0.07 … every frame — 6x in the still frames.
  3. per-frame normalised RMSE (cap-ds-flash, blind): old spread 5.7x with spikes ~3x typical, ~7 frames apart (~117 ms ~ one chunk); new spread 1.2x, no spikes, no identical pairs.
  4. full-circumference 64-ray radius profile with rotation alignment (cap-ds-flash, blind): old spike train 0.08-1.44 px, 18x spread, spikes 7 pairs apart and SURVIVING rotation alignment (so the change is the contour, not rigid rotation); new uniform 1.10-2.08 px, 1.9x spread, no near-zero pair.
  5. the visual read (gemini lane, blind): A frozen with JUMPS AT FRAMES 03 AND 10; B a travelling crest, zero stagnant frames — the same two moments as the numeric spike pairs (02->03, 09->10).
TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST and are part of the record: 'does the drawing move?' cannot discriminate the builds at all (98.7% vs 100% of frames move — the render phase eases per frame in both), and a sparse 4-chunks/s feed is invalid because playback GAPS at that cadence, the page returns to not-speaking and the ring is CLEARED between chunks — that run was measuring clearing, not stepping.

THREE NARROWINGS CAME AFTER THE AGREEMENT, all by measurement: the lane's own attribution limit (its metric supports 'the ring moves' but not independently 'the contour deforms'); my reflow hypothesis, disproved by its page-level probes; and its solved-centroid measurement, which resolved to 'the ring's centre is a constant in the code (OUTPUT_CENTRE) and the container is pixel-static, so every centre number is a summary statistic of an asymmetric travelling contour'.
